... and Blues hope Allan holds key as they agree deal

Manchester City have reached an agreement with Palmeiras over the signing of Allan Elias.

The deal for the winger is worth up to £34million. City are paying £32m plus £2m in add-ons.

Allan is a left-footed winger who predominantly plays off the right like Savinho, who is heading to Spurs for £75m plus £10m in add-ons.

Coventry pinning hopes on Pinnock

Coventry have agreed a £6m deal to sign Ethan Pinnock from Brentford.

Earlier today Daily Mail Sport reported that the clubs were in talks over a move. The Jamaica international has been on the periphery of Keith Andrews' first team but has been attracting enquiries from a number of clubs including West Ham.

However, Coventry manager Frank Lampard has recognised that the 33-year-old Pinnock's Premier League experience could benefit his side during what will be a testing season.

Pinnock could sign in the next 24 hours.

Ethan Pinnock is set for a move to promoted Coventry

Newcastle back in for Pardo

Newcastle have rekindled talks over Lille forward Matias-Fernandez Pardo.

The clubs have been discussing an offer worth around £40million for the Belgium international who can play across the front line.

Daily Mail Sport has previously reported Newcastle's interest in the 21-year-old while Red Bull Leipzig and Atletico Madrid have made proposals recently too.

Pardo was on Liverpool's watchlist previously and played for Belgium at the World Cup.

Tigers target towering forward

Hull are in talks for towering Union Berlin forward Ilyas Ansah.

The Germany Under-21 international was considered for selection by Ghana ahead of the World Cup and Hull are offering £19m, including add-ons.

The 21-year old is 6ft 6in tall and was a target for Besiktas earlier this year. He scored five goals and registered two assists in 26 games for Union Berlin last season.

Hull had a £7m offer for Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas knocked back last week and are continuing to work on other options.

Imps land Wheatley

Manchester United striker Ethan Wheatley has joined Championship side Lincoln City.

The 20-year-old agreed the move on Friday after seeing Everton pull out of a deal to sign him permanently earlier last week.

Wheatley, who had a spell at Bradford last season, joins on loan for the rest of this campaign.

Sports.title: Fulham 2-3 Chelsea: Of all the signings big-spending Blues have made, they've forgotten to recruit a new goalkeeper - writes OLIVER HOLT... but with Cole Palmer, the Premier League title is possible
Sports.content:
The River Thames was at low tide on Monday evening. Gulls and a lone heron stood stoically on banks of exposed grey shingle, scrutinising the pebbles for signs of sustenance. Fifty metres or so from the river bank, the Chelsea team bus disgorged its players and sent them into Craven Cottage to feed on what they could find. A miserable season that cost two managers - Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior – their jobs in the space of a few months in the course of the last campaign and ended with the ignominy of a tenth-placed finish appeared, weirdly, only to have heightened expectations for what lies ahead. Much of that optimism stems from the appointment of Xabi Alonso, whose reign at Real Madrid was short-lived but whose reputation still basks in the memory of how he led Bayer Leverkusen to their first and only Bundesliga title in 2023 without losing a match, humbling Bayern Munich in the process. Some have even tipped Chelsea for the title, reasoning that last season’s mediocrity has brought the precious dividend of no European football and the luxury of being able to concentrate resources on domestic challenges. Stellar talents such as Cole Palmer and new £117m signing Morgan Rogers, the reasoning goes, will be fit and raring to go each week. In the fifth year of the hitherto troubled BlueCo ownership, there have even been glimpses of a more coherent strategy emerging. After the trolley-dash approach of co-owner Todd Boehly and then the obsession with youth-as-resale, Chelsea have signed Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, players – and leaders - who each have more than twice as many Premier League appearances as anyone else in the squad. Chelsea may be leaky at the back but they can win the title with Cole Palmer Joao Pedro opened the scoring inside 30 seconds with a deft finish at Craven Cottage Chelsea's new look attacking trio were purring in the opening stages of Monday's game Fulham levelled when Roberto Sanchez allowed a Josh King strike in at his near post The Fulham youngster celebrates after equalising for the hosts against their local rivals If Chelsea can also conjure the magic trick of getting their money back for the thuggish, limited Enzo Fernandez by selling him to Manchester City before the transfer window closes, it will have been a profitable summer indeed. Even though injured Moises Caicedo did not make the opener, Fernandez was still only judged worthy of a place on the bench. In this Chelsea-themed narrative, Fulham and their new manager Alvaro Arbeloa, an old friend and teammate of Alonso, were supposed to be sacrificial lambs in the west London derby. Even then, few expected Chelsea to establish their dominance with such brutal and unforgiving immediacy. It took the visitors just 31 seconds to take the lead. Maxence Lacroix, another new signing, intercepted a long ball out of the Fulham defence and headed it back to the edge of the area. Palmer flicked it on, Joao Pedro seized on it and lifted a delicate finish over Bernd Leno. The Cottage was stunned into silence. Chelsea almost let Fulham into the game immediately. Levi Colwill let a pass run under his foot and as Oscar Bobb nicked it past him and set off for goal, Colwill brought him down. The home crowd clamoured for a red card. Colwill escaped with a yellow. It could easily have gone the other way. Gradually, Fulham clawed their way back into the game. Josh King let fly from distance and stung the fingers of Robert Sanchez with a shot that he could only spoon behind. King set up Cesar Palacios, who curled a shot over. Fulham’s belief grew. Midway through the half, they were level. It was no surprise that King was the scorer. Once more, Chelsea gave him space to advance and when he rifled a shot towards the near post, Sanchez dived to save it but somehow allowed it to evade his grasp. After all the signings Chelsea have made, they forgot to sign a new goalkeeper. It was the position they needed to strengthen most. We can add it to the list of mystery omissions that have so puzzled and infuriated Chelsea supporters these past few years. Morgan Rogers put Chelsea back in front before the half time break with a cool finish The £117million signing was on hand to find the net at Craven Cottage The Chelsea star finished from a tight angle after a classy attacking move But Chelsea handed their rivals another lifeline when a defensive error allowed Gonzalo Garcia to strike Chelsea reasserted their superiority. Joao Pedro hooked a volley just wide, Reece James mishit a shot when he should have done better and Leno saved at point-blank range from Romeo Lavia. Through it all, the class of Palmer was a common denominator. His exclusion from Thomas Tuchel’s England squad felt like even more of an aberration by the time the interval arrived. Chelsea made their superiority count five minutes before half-time when Palmer fed Lacroix and Lacroix showed just how good he is on the ball by turning his man inside out in the Fulham area and crossing low to the back post. Rogers, on his competitive debut for his new side, was there to meet it and drilled his shot beyond a desperate attempt to hack it off the line. Rogers had had a fine half. Not quite as good as Palmer but close. Palmer started the second half with a quite brilliant dribble that ended with a shot he curled just wide. A minute later, he burst into the Fulham box on the overlap and ran on to a pass from Joao Pedro. Palmer looked up and then threaded the ball between Leno’s legs for Chelsea’s third. This game was not about to go quietly. Timothy Castagne got in behind Colwill and Sanchez could only push his shot back into the danger area. Fulham’s new £40m signing Gonzalo Garcia reacted fastest and nodded the ball back past the goalkeeper and in off the underside of the bar. Fernandez came on, accompanied by a deafening chorus of boos, midway through the half. That was the main sport for Fulham fans until 12 minutes from the end when Antonee Robinson ran on to a long ball behind the Chelsea defence. With Sanchez stranded, Robinson lobbed him but directed the ball agonisingly wide. Chelsea hung on for a 3-2 win but Palmer gave them a scare when he pulled up suddenly, clutching his calf. It looked like cramp. The title? Chelsea’s defence will have to improve but anything is possible if Palmer can stay fit and play like this.

Sports.title: Fulham 2-3 Chelsea - PLAYER RATINGS: Who got top marks from Blues' dazzling attacking trio? Which Cottagers star impressed? And how did Robert Sanchez fare?
Sports.content:
Fulham 2-3 Chelsea - PLAYER RATINGS: Who got top marks from Blues' dazzling attacking trio? Which Cottagers star impressed? And how did Robert Sanchez fare?

Xabi Alonso's Chelsea reign got off to a winning start with a 3-2 victory at west-London rivals Fulham.

Chelsea took the lead within seconds when Joao Pedro broke the deadlock before Josh King equalised midway through the first half after a Robert Sanchez error.

After half-time Chelsea pulled into a 3-1 lead thanks to goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer, before Gonzalo Garcia reduced the deficit for Fulham. However, they were unable to find an equaliser.

Daily Mail Sport's KIERAN GILL was at Craven Cottage to run the rule over both teams.

Fulham (4-2-3-1)

Bernd Leno - 5

Leno is not the first goalkeeper to be left helpless when Joao Pedro is through. Deserted his goal as Morgan Rogers blasted in. Nutmegged by Cole Palmer for Chelsea's third.

Timothy Castagne - 5

Rogers was all on his own to score Chelsea's second as Fulham's defenders were ball-watching and dropping towards their goal rather than guarding the threats in their box.

Calvin Bassey - 5

Fulham captain. We imagine Alvaro Arbeloa will be playing back some of these conceded goals for his defenders in the coming days. Booked for diving in a bid to win an attacking free-kick.

Calvin Bassey and his defenders are set to be shown their errors which led to Chelsea's goals

Jorge Cuenca - 5

Defenders can be skinned. No shame in that. But by another defender? Oof. Now that's hard to take. Maxence Lacroix turned Cuenca, crossed, and Rogers made it 2-1.

Antonee Robinson - 5

Did not have the easiest evening trying to tame Palmer. Only had to lob the stranded Sanchez to make it 3-3 in the 78th minute but got his angles wrong when through on goal and sent it wide.

Josh King - 7

Loved a driven rocket from distance. Robert Sanchez saved his first crack unconvincingly, so he kept going, until he finally beat Chelsea's goalkeeper from 20 yards.

Josh King provided an attacking threat for Fulham and scored their opener with this driven shot

Sander Berge - 5

Unlike his midfield partner, he was reluctant to try his luck from distance, even when the Fulham fans were encouraging him to do so. Not much creativity to his game.

Oscar Bobb - 6

Thought he was through until Levi Colwill brought him down, cynically so. Five metres closer to Chelsea's goal and his opponent might have been in bother. Replaced by Shea Charles.

Alex Iwobi - 6

Was dropping rather deep considering he should have been adding a threat to a Fulham attack which had Chelsea predominantly worried from out wide.

Cesar Palacios - 6

The new £8.6m arrival from Real Madrid. Fortunate to avoid a booking when he dragged down Palmer to kill a potential attack. Lasted 73 minutes until Arbeloa changed it up.

Gonzalo Garcia - 6.5

Another £34m newbie from Real. Reacted like a flash when Sanchez palmed a shot back into the danger area as Garcia headed in to make it 3-2 and get himself off the mark.

Gonzalo Garcia showed his goalscoring instinct by reacting quickest to score Fulham's second

SUBS USED

Shea Charles (for Bobb, 67 mins) - 6

Young summer signing was introduced to try to help Fulham find a way back in, and we like seeing him in the central areas more than Berge.

Kevin (for Palacios, 73) - 6

That opportunity to get Fulham back into the game never arrived for the substitute.

Ryan Sessegnon (for Berge, 73) - 6

Fulham tried, and did put pressure on the visitors, but could never get that breakthrough.

Rodrigo Muniz (for Robinson, 82) - N/A

SUBS NOT USED: Benjamin Lecomte, Kenny Tete, Harrison Reed, Emile Smith Rowe, Luc De Fourgerolles

MANAGER: Alvaro Arbeloa - 6

CHELSEA (3-4-2-1)

Robert Sanchez - 4

Chelsea fans may be saying: 'Told you so.' They have called for a new goalkeeper for a while now, and Sanchez was weak in both of the goals he conceded here. Still time to sign a new one…

Robert Sanchez's form from last season has carried over as he was at fault for Fulham's goals

Josh Acheampong - 7

The Cobham graduate, 20, had to produce several blocks in the first half as Fulham grew into this game. Chelsea are debating whether to loan him away. He is ready for more regular minutes.

Maxence Lacroix - 7.5

Why the £52m summer signing was practically playing a right winger momentarily, we're not entirely sure, but he turned Cuenca for a lovely assist for Rogers. Blocks galore at the end, too.

Levi Colwill - 6

Yellow carded for hacking down Oscar Bobb inside five minutes when Fulham fans wanted a red for DOGSO. Failed in a defensive header before the home side's second goal from Garcia.

Malo Gusto - 6

A minor injury meant there was no Marco Palestra, with Gusto manning the right-hand side. Tiring job in Xabi Alonso's system. Pedro Neto replaced him for the final 15 minutes.

Reece James - 6.5

A minor setback ruled Moises Caicedo out of contention as Chelsea's captain was used in midfield instead. Accused King of faking a foul which earned him a caution.

Reece James was deployed in central midfield and controlled thing from there for Chelsea

Romeo Lavia - 6.5

With Enzo Fernandez on the bench, Lavia added aggression into midfield, crunching Calvin Bassey to earn himself an early yellow.

Jorrel Hato - 6.5

A new position for him at left wing back but he flew forward when he could, one such sprint nearly making it 4-1 to Chelsea. Being timed out for a throw-in was not appreciated by his team-mates.

Cole Palmer - 8

Like his old, cold, creative self. First-time pass in behind allowed Joao Pedro to sprint and score. Was twisting and turning Robinson and Co at will. Then he grabbed the goal he deserved.

Cole Palmer reminded England boss Thomas Tuchel what he missed out on at the World Cup

Morgan Rogers - 7

The £117m man. While he was signed for what he adds to the attack, he allowed King to run off him for Fulham's 1-1 leveller. But got his goal after Lacroix's lovely assist.

Joao Pedro - 7.5

After eight goals in eight games in pre-season, he took 31 seconds to score here, a delicate dink over Bernd Leno. Nearly volleyed in a second to Palmer's cross before half-time.

SUBS USED

Enzo Fernandez (for Lavia, 65) - 6

Booed by all of Craven Cottage – but not the Chelsea away end. They applauded him and sang his name. Now to see what happens between now and the summer window closing.

Pep Chavarria (for Hato, 65) - 6

Making his Chelsea debut, could not get too far forward with a great deal of defending to do.

Pedro Neto (for Gusto, 76) - N/A

Geovany Quenda (for Rogers, 83) - N/A

Estevao (for Palmer, 83) - N/A

SUBS NOT USED: Mike Penders, Valentin Barco, Jamie Gittens, Danny Welbeck

MANAGER: Xabi Alonso - 7

REFEREE: John Brooks - 6

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
