World.title: Uba Sani approves ₦300m for KASU-ASUU, sets up negotiation c’ttee to avert strike
World.content:
The Kaduna State Government has constituted a nine-member negotiation committee to engage with the Kaduna State University (KASU) chapter of the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) and other staff unions over their outstanding demands.

The government also approved a one-off payment of ₦300 million as Earned Academic Allowance (EAA) for academic staff of the university.

The decisions were contained in a statement issued by the Secretary to the Kaduna State Government, Dr AbdulKadir Mu’azu Meyere, on Monday.

According to the statement, the interventions are part of the administration’s efforts to resolve long-standing staff welfare and funding issues at KASU while preventing disputes that could disrupt academic activities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Meyere said the ₦300 million EAA payment was part of the government’s sustained efforts to address a backlog of more than ₦800 million in accumulated entitlements and allowances dating back to 2016.

He said the intervention demonstrated Governor Uba Sani’s commitment to staff welfare, industrial harmony and the stability of the university through constructive dialogue and sustainable solutions.

Background

The latest development comes amid demands by university-based unions for improved welfare, payment of outstanding allowances and implementation of agreements affecting academic and non-academic staff.

The government said its interventions over the past three and a half years had included the settlement of outstanding withheld salaries, payment of more than ₦300 million for accreditation of academic programmes and resource-verification exercises for postgraduate programmes, and the release of funds to clear outstanding SIWES supervision allowances.

It also said the administration had established a ₦50 million monthly standing order to facilitate the systematic settlement of outstanding arrears.

The government said the measures were aimed at addressing inherited liabilities while ensuring that KASU remains financially and academically stable.

Committee to Review Union Demands

The negotiation committee will be chaired by the Commissioner for Education, Professor Abubakar Sani Sambo.

Other members are the Commissioner for Business, Innovation and Technology, Mrs Patience Fakai; Commissioner for Youth, Mrs Gloria Ibrahim; Chairman of the Local Government Service Board, Professor Ladan Sharehu; Director-General of the Kaduna State Schools Quality Assurance Authority, Professor Usman Abubakar Zaria; Vice-Chancellor of KASU, Professor Abdullahi Ibrahim Musa; and Pro-Chancellor of the university, Dr Ibrahim Umar.

The Permanent Secretary, General Services, Office of the Secretary to the State Government, is also a member, while the Permanent Secretary, Establishments Services and Training, will serve as secretary to the committee.

The committee has four weeks to complete its assignment and submit its recommendations to the state government.

It is mandated to review the demands of ASUU, the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), the Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU), and the National Association of Academic Technologists (NAAT).

Among other issues, the committee is expected to examine the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA), compare KASU’s situation with prevailing practices in other state-owned universities, and assess the financial implications of implementing demands arising from the 2025 ASUU–Federal Government agreement.

Mr Meyere said the committee was expected to recommend practical, equitable and financially sustainable solutions to the outstanding issues.

Government Appeals for Dialogue

The Secretary to the State Government urged the unions to embrace dialogue, negotiation and collective bargaining rather than resorting to industrial action that could disrupt the academic calendar and adversely affect students and their families.

He said the government’s channels of engagement remained open, assuring the university community of its commitment to strengthening KASU, improving staff welfare and safeguarding uninterrupted academic activities.

The latest intervention therefore places emphasis on negotiation as the preferred route for resolving the KASU unions’ grievances, while the government seeks to balance staff demands with the state’s financial capacity.

World.title: GMAP: How UBA is Strengthening Africa’s Future Leadership Through Excellence, Enterprise and Execution
World.content:
As Africa’s young population continues to grow, the need for skilled and adaptable leaders has never been more urgent. Through its Graduate Management Accelerator Programme (GMAP), the United Bank for Africa is investing in young African professionals by building the excellence, enterprise and execution needed to thrive in a changing business environment and shape the continent’s future. Chiemelie Ezeobi reports

“Excellence, enterprise and execution are the three things I am taking back home to Zambia to implement — putting the customers first. Being here in Nigeria has been a great experience and being at GMAP is prestigious. It took a lot of persistence and hard work. Thank you, UBA.”

Those were the words of Thomas from Zambia, as he graduated last week Thursday from the Graduate Management Accelerator Programme (GMAP), United Bank for Africa’s flagship talent development initiative, which continues to prepare young professionals for leadership roles within the financial institution and the wider African business environment

For Thomas, whose reflection captured the wider purpose of GMAP, the graduation was more than the end of an intensive training programme. It was the beginning of a new phase in a career shaped by lessons gathered from across borders, cultures and professional experiences.

Like Thomas, 373 other young professionals also graduated from the GMAP and were inducted into the workforce, marking the completion of Cohort 21 of GMAP, increasing the more than 5,000 already existing alumni and creating a growing pool of professionals within what UBA describes as the UBA Tribe.

Building Leaders Beyond Borders

The ceremony at the Landmark Events Centre in Lagos brought together young professionals from Nigeria and seven other African countries where the bank operates

The composition of the graduating class reflected UBA’s pan-African structure. Of the 374 graduates, 345 were from Nigeria, while 29 came from UBA operations in Guinea, Tanzania, Kenya, Mozambique, Uganda, Zambia and Côte d’Ivoire.

Beyond the numbers-223 women and 151 men, the programme offered a meeting point for young Africans with different backgrounds and experiences. That diversity became part of the training itself, giving participants opportunities to work with colleagues from different cultures and understand how business can be approached from different perspectives.

For an organisation operating across multiple African markets, that experience has practical value. The bank is not simply preparing employees to work within individual country operations; it is developing a workforce capable of collaborating across borders and responding to the realities of an increasingly interconnected African economy.

From Training To Responsibility

At the graduation, UBA Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Mr. Oliver Alawuba, challenged the new graduates to see their certificates as the beginning of responsibility rather than the conclusion of training.

“You came from different countries, with different experiences and disciplines, but today you have graduated as one UBA family, united by one ambition, to build Africa’s future,” Alawuba told the graduates.

He reminded them that their first posting might not necessarily be their preferred destination, but urged them to approach every assignment with commitment.

“Your first posting may not be your preferred destination, but make it your platform and give it your best. No assignment is too small to reveal a great attitude, and no role is too modest for excellence,” he said.

Service as the Differentiator

UBA Group Chairman, Mr. Tony Elumelu, brought another dimension to the conversation, focusing on the customer.

Why you may ask? As technology continues to reshape banking, financial products and services are becoming increasingly similar. Digital platforms and other technological tools can be adopted by competitors, making it harder for banks to rely on products alone as a competitive advantage.

For Elumelu, the answer lies in service.

“Products can be commoditised, but service never can, because there is always a differentiator in how you serve and how you create,” he said.

He further explained that as banks increasingly adopt similar technologies, the real distinction would come from how those technologies are deployed to improve the customer experience.

Elumelu also used his interaction with the graduates to address the uncertainties that often accompany the beginning of a career. In responding to their questions, he drew from his experience to discuss workplace pressures, difficult situations and the importance of maintaining a positive attitude.

He encouraged them to remain resilient and see challenges as opportunities to learn and grow, adding that “As future leaders of UBA, people like you give me confidence that if we hand over to your generation, UBA will be safe”.

An Investment in Africa’s Talent

The significance of GMAP extends beyond UBA’s immediate staffing needs.

Africa has one of the world’s youngest populations, while its economies continue to face the challenge of creating opportunities for a growing workforce. For businesses, this creates both a responsibility and an opportunity: developing skilled people who can participate meaningfully in economic growth. UBA’s investment in GMAP reflects that wider need.

The programme combines formal training with mentorship and practical exposure, giving participants an understanding of the demands of the banking industry while developing the leadership and professional skills required to operate in a competitive environment.

The more than 5,000 professionals who have passed through the programme represent a growing network of talent shaped within UBA’s African operations.

The Real Test Begins

The applause, photographs and presentation of certificates marked the close of the ceremony, but not the end of the journey.

The 374 graduates now move into different roles and markets, carrying with them the expectations attached to the training they have received.

For some, like Thomas from Zambia, the next step is already clear: take the lessons home and turn them into action, with the customer at the centre.

His decision to identify three words — excellence, enterprise and execution — as the lessons he would take back to Zambia reflects the broader philosophy behind GMAP because through GMAP, UBA is investing in that human capital and preparing young professionals not simply to occupy positions, but to grow into leaders capable of shaping the bank, its customers and the wider African economy.

World.title: Where Health Reform Becomes Real: Reflections from Nigeria’s Primary Healthcare Frontline
World.content:
Nkata Chuku

On an ordinary morning in a primary healthcare centre, a mother may walk several kilometres with her baby on her back to have him immunised. Whether she returns home relieved or turned away often depends on small, but critical, details: whether the vaccines are available, whether the health worker is there, whether the doors are open at all.

Across Nigeria, these everyday moments are becoming increasingly important measures of whether health reforms are delivering on their promise.

They remind us that while policies, financing and infrastructure create the conditions for change, the real test of reform is whether people experience better care when they need it most.

And that experience is shaped at primary healthcare centres, where stronger systems and essential services covering malaria, family planning and immunisation come together in the care families rely on.

There are encouraging signs that this is beginning to happen.

The Basic Health Care Provision Fund, ongoing primary healthcare revitalisation efforts and stronger fiscal commitments by many states are creating renewed momentum for primary healthcare. Across the country, facilities are being upgraded, equipment is improving and state governments are demonstrating greater commitment to strengthening services closer to communities.

Yet progress is rarely defined by infrastructure alone. A facility may look transformed, but if essential medicines are unavailable, routine immunisation is inconsistent or health workers lack the support they need, families continue to face uncertainty.

The distance between policy commitments and a consistently functioning clinic is often bridged by factors that receive far less attention than the reforms themselves.

What Progress is Beginning to Look Like

One of the most encouraging developments in recent years is that, across different states, common patterns are beginning to emerge where reforms are translating into better services.

These are rarely places transformed by a single innovation. More often, they are places where leadership remains focused on implementation, where data is used to solve problems rather than simply report them, where frontline health workers receive regular support, and where different parts of the health system work towards shared priorities.

Yobe’s recognition in the 2025 Primary Healthcare Leadership Challenge reflects many of these characteristics.

Improvements in the availability of essential medicines, stronger coordination across services and greater confidence in routine data did not happen overnight; they are the result of sustained attention to the fundamentals of primary healthcare.

Kaduna offers a similar perspective.

The state’s efforts to strengthen selected primary healthcare centres and expand health insurance coverage have undoubtedly improved access for many families. But perhaps the more significant lesson lies beneath those visible investments.

Conversations with state officials and frontline health workers consistently point to the value of regular performance reviews, closer coordination between partners and government, and sustained leadership attention to implementation.

These examples are different in many respects, yet they reinforce the same observation: reforms gain traction when implementation becomes everyone’s daily business, not just a policy ambition.

The Work that Often Goes Unseen

Some of the most important improvements in primary healthcare rarely attract headlines.

They happen when community health workers identify pregnant women early and continue supporting them throughout pregnancy. They happen when facility teams use routine data to identify children who have missed vaccinations and bring them back into care.

They happen when referral systems function as intended, reducing delays during obstetric emergencies, or when supervisors address supply challenges before they become stock-outs.

None of these actions is new.

What is changing in many places is the consistency with which they are being applied.

That consistency matters because it builds confidence – not only within the health system but among communities themselves. When people know that services will be available, and also believe in the responsiveness of the system as it shows up in health worker attitudes and quality of care, they are more likely to seek care early, return for follow-up visits and recommend those services to others.

Development partners also have an important role to play, but experience increasingly shows that the greatest impact comes when support strengthens government priorities rather than creating parallel systems.

Lasting progress depends on national and subnational leadership, with partners helping to reinforce the systems already being built.

Building on the Momentum

There is every reason to recognise the progress Nigeria has made in strengthening primary healthcare. Equally, there is every reason to recognise that this progress remains fragile. Workforce shortages, supply chain interruptions and fiscal pressures continue to test even the strongest systems.

Across government, frontline health workers, development partners and communities, there is an opportunity to keep learning from states where reforms are beginning to translate into better experiences for families – not to replicate one model, but to understand the conditions that allow progress to endure.

Ultimately, health reform is not measured by the number of policies adopted or facilities renovated. It is measured by whether a mother arriving at her local clinic finds the care she came for.

That is both the promise of Nigeria’s primary healthcare reforms and the challenge ahead: ensuring that the encouraging progress already visible in many states becomes the everyday experience of families in every community across the country.

*Nkata Chuku is Deputy Director Health Systems Strengthening & Primary Healthcare, Gates Foundation

World.title: Nine NFF Board Members Set to Throw in the Towel
World.content:
Duro Ikhazuagbe

No less than nine members of the Executive Committee of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) are believed to have signaled their intentions to quit the board in the face of mounting criticism over the federation’s poor handling of the country’s football administration.

THISDAY learnt at the weekend that the 13-member NFF board that has Ibrahim Musa Gusau as President with two vice presidents and 10 others, have met and considering the options of resigning en-masse despite initial plans to have most members returned to office at the election scheduled for September 27 in Lafia, Nasarawa State.

A top level sports administrator who confided in THISDAY, insisted that this option is believed may pave the way for a Normalisation Committee to run the country’s football for the next couple of months. “During this period, we expect a new governance structure to be put in place to midwife a new board for the NFF. We expect also for the new board to be a departure from what Nigerians have been used to in the last two and half decades,” observed the official.

Although some names have been speculated to lead the Normalisation Committee, he was categorical that none of those listed in the media reports will be in the committee. He declined to give out any name as consultation was still ongoing as there may be changes before the list is announced.

Before Super Falcons’s failure in Morocco, the Super Eagles failed to qualify for the 2026 FIFA World Cup hosted by USA, Canada and Mexico.

The inability of the Super Falcons to qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup sparked the pressure for the NFF board to quit office. The team was dismal in Morocco, failing to reach the semi final of the 2026 WAFCON as well as also failing to pick ticket to the World Cup for the first time since the inaugural edition of the women’s Mundial in China in 1991. The country’s men’s U20 and U17 have similarly failed in Africa and also failed to qualify for the global level.

Although the NFF board later fired the fumbling Falcons coaching crew led by Justin Madugu, football stakeholders were not impressed, thereby calling for a total clean up of the NFF to pave way for a breadth of fresh air.

The country’s two anti-graft agencies, the EFCC and the ICPC, have equally stepped into the financing of football at the NFF. The two agencies last week moved into the federations offices in Abuja to check how government’s N17billion released for the prosecution of the 2023 AFCON in Cote d’Ivoire, the 2026 World Cup qualifiers as well as the 2025 AFCON in Morocco was spent.

Both Gusau and the General Secretary of the NFF are believed to be amongst those who have agreed to quit the federation.

A former Super Eagles Captain, John Obi Mikel in his latest Obi One Podcast, restated his stand on why the NFF board should exit the federation now for fresh leadership to restore the country’s football fortunes.

Mikel warned that Nigeria risk missing a third consecutive World Cup after failing to qualify for the 2022 and 2026 editions if Gusau is allowed to return for another four years in office as NFF president.

World.title: Terem Moffi Completes Hamburg Switch
World.content:
Super Eagles forward, Terem Moffi, has joined Hamburg from Nice on a permanent transfer for 2.5 million euros, which includes 500,000 euros in bonuses.

Moffi’s arrival was confirmed by HSV earlier on Monday.

The 27-year-old centre-forward joined from OGC Nice after spending the second half of last season on loan at FC Porto.

He signed a three-year contract with Hamburg.

Before signing the contract, Moffi completed routine medical examinations at the Athleticum of Volkspark at the weekend.

He will wear the number 9 shirt at Hamburg.

According to Claus Costa, HSV’s Director of Professional Football, Moffi is a striker who is difficult to control due to his physicality, determination, and style of play, and is expected to add power and versatility to the team’s squad.

The transfer gives Moffi a fresh start in Germany and gives Hamburg an experienced striker for another Bundesliga challenge. HSV sporting board member Kathleen Krüger said the Nigerian’s physical strength and international experience would give the team more options in attack.

Moffi is expected to join his new team-mates in training this week.

His first competitive chance could come on Saturday, when Hamburg travel to face Borussia Dortmund in their German Bundesliga opener.

World.title: NPFL Top Scorer, Anas, to Battle Osimhen, Lookman for Nigeria Pitch Award Honour
World.content:
Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) top scorer, Anas Yusuf of Nasarawa United FC is set to give his more illustrious Nigerian forwards,

Ademola Lookman of Atlético de Madrid and Galatasaray’s Victor Osimhen a run for their money in the race for the Rashidi Yekini Award for the Best Striker of the Year at the 12th Nigeria Pitch Awards Ceremony.

The 12th edition of the Nigeria Pitch Awards Ceremony, which had been scheduled for earlier in the year, is to hold on Tuesday, 8th September 2026, at the Ibis Hotel, Toyin Street, Ikeja, Lagos.

The 12th Awards Ceremony will feature awards in 18 categories.

In the King of the Pitch category, Atlético de Madrid striker Ademola Lookman, the 2024-winner of the award, will face competition from Fulham defender Calvin Bassey and Galatasaray S.K. goal poacher Victor Osimhen.

The Queen of the Pitch Award will be a stiff battle between Chiamaka Nnadozie of Brighton & Hove Albion Women FC, Esther Okoronkwo of AFC Toronto, and Rasheedat Ajibade of PSG Feminine.

The award for the Football Friendly Governor of the Year will be a contest among Governors Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State, Dapo Abiodun of Ogun State, and Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom State.

There are other categories of awards to be given out at the ceremony.

Speaking ahead of the award, President of Nigeria Pitch Awards, Dr. Shina Phillips, stressed that hosting the 12th Awards Ceremony at this time is “a demonstration of our faith in Nigerian football. Since 2013, when we held our maiden edition in Calabar, we have shown Nigerians that our players deserve commendations and encouragement for their selfless, patriotic contributions to the growth of our football,” Philips noted.

On behalf of the organizers, Philips regrets the delay in hosting the 12th edition of the awards, stating that although the trophies and other logistics were already in place, certain factors necessitated postponing the ceremony beyond the expected date.

“All necessary logistics, including the award statuettes, have been in place, but the awards itself could not be held as earlier scheduled,” Philips noted.

World.title: AFN Warns Nigerian Athletes against Signing Unfavourable Deals
World.content:
The Athletics Federation of Nigeria (AFN) has reaffirmed its commitment to protecting the welfare and long-term interests of Nigerian athletes, insisting that no agreement entered into by an athlete is “cast in stone.”

AFN President, Chief Tonobok Okowa, said the Federation is closely monitoring agreements involving Nigerian athletes and will intervene where such deals are considered detrimental to the athlete or the interests of Nigeria.

Okowa, who is also a Senior Vice President of the Confederation of African Athletics (CAA), said the welfare of athletes remains a key component of the Federation’s responsibilities.

He clarified that the AFN has not entered into any agreement with agents or agencies to provide scholarships to Nigerian athletes, urging athletes and their families to exercise caution before committing themselves to any arrangement.

The Federation also stressed that athletes who are minors should not enter into agreements without the knowledge and consent of their parents or legal guardians.

“It is necessary to protect young athletes from arrangements that could negatively affect their education, careers or national representation.” Okowa stated.

The AFN disclosed that it has advised an athlete to terminate an agreement involving an agent and a school after determining that the arrangement was not in the athlete’s best interest and could be inimical to the interests of Nigeria.

The Federation also revealed that it is not prepared to work with Auburn University in the United States for as long as coach Ken remains at the institution.

“AFN’s position is based on concerns that the coach discourages Nigerian athletes from representing the country,” the AFN Boss added.

Okowa said the Federation would continue to scrutinise agreements involving Nigerian athletes, particularly those involving foreign institutions, agents and other third parties.

He noted that while foreign scholarships and training opportunities can provide valuable platforms for athletes to combine education with elite-level development, such arrangements must not undermine their careers or their responsibility to represent Nigeria.

“In a particular case, I directed the AFN Second Vice President, Akuchukwu Aghazu, who is a lawyer, to examine the circumstances surrounding an athlete’s agreement.” Okowa said.

Aghazu subsequently reviewed the matter and provided legal guidance to the Federation on the appropriate course of action.

Okowa urged athletes and their families to seek proper advice before signing agreements and assured them that the AFN would continue to protect their interests while ensuring that opportunities presented to Nigerian athletes contribute positively to their development.

World.title: Ogundare, Obieze Lift Indian 80TH Independence Day Titles at Ikeja
World.content:
The Indian Independence Day Cup 2026 Tournament at Ikeja Golf Club has produced winners in all the categories with Jimoh Ogundare and Linda Obieze emerging champions in the men and women’s categories.

This third edition was spectacular as it was used to mark the 80th independence anniversary of Indian.

With over 140 players drawn from across most of the golfing communities of Ikeja, Ikoyi, Lakowe, the Indian Independence Day Tournament lived up to billing with the golfers not sparing anything to be amongst the winners of the various categories.

At the end of a competitive outing, Ogundare with 38 points emerged the Overall winner of the men’s category on count back. He was rewarded with a trophy and a carton of vegetable oil. Wale Kalejaiye was first runner up with same 38points as Ogundare while Henry Gboneme (37points) was second runner up. Arun Sharma with 74 points emerged best Gross winner

In the women’s category, Linda Obieze emerged Overall winner with 36 points while Abiodun Hassan (33points) was runner up.

Tokunbo Ogunbiyi emerged men’s Longest Drive winner while Chichi Alamu won the ladies’ version. Zed Jituboh also won men’s Nearest to the Pin and Shot on the Green on Hole 17. Rasaki Muritala was runner up.

Speaking at the prize presentation ceremony, Vice captain of the club, Ejiro Ogomigo, who represented the Captain, described the tournament as a huge success adding that the Indian community didn’t spare anything to serenade all participants at this edition.

“This is the third edition of the Indian Independence Cup. Every year there is improvement, of course this year there’s been major improvement.

“This is one tournament a lot of members look forward to play in, it is keenly contested, it is very challenging.

“For some reason the course today was extremely challenging, you can see the highest points today was 38 points compared to the previous year where we had about 40 points.”

A member of the Indian golf Community, Gagandeep Lakhanpal, expressed his excitement at celebrating their country’s 80th anniversary with their Nigerian friends at the Ikeja Golf Club.

“This is one of our ways to give back to the community. We are very happy with the massive turnout at the tournament. We hope to make it an annual event,” stressed the Indian Tournament organizing community member.

World.title: Argentine Football Scout Houseman Discovers Pam after Kaduna Screening
World.content:
Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja

Nigerian U-20 player Jahmang Pam has signed a contract with a renowned Argentine international football scout and agent, Marcelo Houseman, following a weeklong scouting programme.

Pam signed the contract over the weekend at ABT Football Academy in Kwoi, Southern Kaduna, at the end of the programme, organised by Alhamdu Bala, chairman and proprietor of ABT Football Academy, which attracted no fewer than 800 young footballers from 15 academies.

The players participated in intensive training, technical assessments, tactical sessions, and competitive matches designed to identify promising talents for international opportunities.

Sixteen players across the U-17 and U-20 categories were selected for further development and consideration for opportunities abroad at the end of the rigorous scouting exercise.

Pam, who featured prominently during the programme, impressed the scout with his technical ability, tactical intelligence, vision, versatility, and understanding of the game.

Speaking after the signing, Houseman described Pam as an exciting young talent with qualities capable of attracting interest from clubs outside Nigeria.

“Pam has exceptional qualities, but talent alone is not enough; he must remain disciplined, focused, and committed to continuous improvement,” Houseman said.

He promised to work towards securing a lucrative international opportunity for Pam within the next few weeks as part of efforts to further develop his football career.

“I see a player with great potential, and my responsibility is to help create the right pathway for him to grow and compete at a higher level,” he added.

Houseman also commended ABT Football Academy for creating an environment where young players could showcase their abilities before international scouts.

An elated Adama Jang, Pam’s mother and personal manager, expressed gratitude to Houseman and the academy for recognising her son’s talent.

Jang said the contract represented “a major step forward” in Pam’s career and expressed confidence that the partnership would open new doors for the young footballer.

“I am grateful to God and everyone who has supported Pam. We are excited about this opportunity and hopeful about what lies ahead,” she said.

She, however, promised that Pam would remain disciplined and focused while taking every professional advice necessary to succeed.

Pam, who described the development as a dream come true, said he was delighted to have earned the confidence of the Argentine football scout.

“I feel happy and motivated by this opportunity. I know there is still a lot of work to do, and I am ready to learn, improve, and give my best,” Pam said.

He thanked his mother, coaches, teammates, ABT Football Academy, and everyone who had contributed to his development, promising to remain committed to his football career.

Pam is a Nigerian professional footballer who plays primarily as an attacking midfielder and winger, with the versatility to operate in central midfield.

His big break came when he gained recognition after earning a call-up to Nigeria’s U-20 national team, the Flying Eagles, in 2024.

He was invited to the Flying Eagles training camp under former coach Aliyu Zubairu ahead of the WAFU B U-20 qualifiers.

Pam began his football journey in Jos, Plateau, at the age of nine. He continued to develop his technical and tactical abilities and had a stint with Mighty Jets, featuring in a number of matches.

His playing style is characterised by tactical intelligence, vision, ball control, and versatility, qualities that have continued to attract attention from football development stakeholders.

Bala, the academy proprietor, described the scouting programme as a significant opportunity for young Nigerian footballers seeking international exposure.

He said the academy was committed to providing talented players with professional development opportunities while creating pathways for them to pursue careers beyond Nigeria.

Katlego and Vincent Tshituka have welcomed their new baby. Images via IG

Springbok and Sharks player Vincent Tshituka is a proud new dad after welcoming a baby with his wife, Katlego.

The 27-year-old – who made his national team debut last year – and his partner recently celebrated their first wedding anniversary.

VINCENT TSHITUKA IS A FIRST-TIME DAD!

On his Instagram account, Vincent Tshituka made an exciting announcement – his wife, Katlego, had recently given birth to their first child.



Posting pics of both mom and dad embracing their baby, Vincent shared: “It’s so much bigger! Thank you God for a new purpose to live”.

The post was inundated with well-wishes, including those from fellow Springboks Ox Nche, Jese Kriel, and Jordn Hendrikse, amongst others.

The Tshitukas have yet to announce the baby’s gender or name.

Last month, the couple celebrated their first wedding anniversary. In May, they announced that they were expecting a baby.

COUNTDOWN FOR SPRINGBOK RG SNYMAN

Meanwhile, fellow Springbok RG Snyman and his wife, Saskia, are also awaiting the birth of their baby.



The player, nicknamed “The Viking”, and his partner have shared glimpses of her pregnancy on their social media accounts.

Like Vincent Sthituka, RG – who has returned to Ireland amid an ACL injury – is also set to become a first-time father.

World.title: Born and bred in SA : Meet Tharina Botes, Miss Universe Thailand
World.content:
South African-born model Tharina Botes has won Miss Universe Thailand. Images via IG

South African-born model and former Miss SA finalist, Tharina Botes, has been crowned Miss Universe Thailand.

The beauty queen and businesswoman was born in Randburg to a South African father and Thai mother.

Tharina moved abroad in 2019 at the age of 22.

THARINA BOTES CROWNED MISS UNIVERSE THAILAND

Over the weekend, Tharina Botes added another pageant title to her name – Miss Universe Thailand



Tharina, representing Bangkok, was awarded a diamond crown, a cash prize, sponsorship deals and the opportunity to represent Thailand at the Miss Universe pageant on 24 November in Puerto Rico.

“Dreams really come true”, the 29-year-old model and businesswoman shared in an Instagram post.

In another, Tharina added that convinced that hearing a Tyla song during the competition was a “sign”.



WHO IS THE SOUTH AFRICAN-BORN STUNNER?

Tharina Bortes was born and raised in Roodepoort to a South African father and Thai mother.

She attended Monument High School in Krugersdorp and became involved in modelling and pageantry as a teenager. She studied a BCom at Damelin College and later pursued economics through UNISA.

In her early days, she won Miss Teen Gauteng and Miss Rand Show, and represented South Africa at Miss International in Tokyo



In 2018, she entered the Miss South Africa pageant at the age of 21. The pageant, which included finalists like Bryoni Govender and Margo Fargo, was won by Tamaryn Green.

After the pageant, Tharina Botes moved to Thailand, where she continued pageantry.

Tharin won Miss Grand Phuket and Miss Thailand World in 2019 and 2023, respectively.



Before winning the title of Miss Unirsee Thailand, she was named first runner-up in 2021.

World.title: Orlando Pirates star Maswanganyi moves overseas
World.content:
Patrick Maswanganyi celebrates scoring for Orlando Pirates in the MTN8. Image: Official PSL

Orlando Pirates confirmed that an agreement had been reached with the Bahraini club. The club revealed Maswanganyi expressed his desire to continue his career abroad.

His departure brings an end to a spell in which he established himself as a popular figure among the Orlando Pirates supporters.

PATRICK MASWANGANYI GETS ORLANDO PIRATES FAREWELL

Maswanganyi remained an important part of the technical team’s plans for the new season. However, discussions between the player, his representatives and the club ultimately led to Orlando Pirates agreeing to allow him to pursue the opportunity overseas.



The club confirmed that the 28-year-old Maswanganyi’s decision was respected despite his importance to the squad.

“In recognition of his service to the Club and his ambitions for the next chapter of his career, Orlando Pirates agreed not to stand in his way,” the club said.

A transfer was subsequently concluded with Alkhaldiya Sports Club, allowing Maswanganyi to begin a new chapter in Bahrain.



“Tito” leaves Orlando Pirates as a league champion and a firm favourite among the Ghost. His performances in the famous black and white jersey earned him a special place among the supporters.

The club also highlighted his commitment to representing Orlando Pirates with pride throughout his time in Soweto.

Also read: Latest report: SAFA make decision on Pitso Mosimane



THE BUCCANEERS THANK TITO

Maswanganyi departs having made a lasting impression both on and off the field. His personality and performances made him a popular member of the Buccaneers squad.

“From his first appearance in the famous black and white jersey, he gave the Ghost countless moments to celebrate and represented this club with pride,” Orlando Pirates said.

His exit will now leave the technical team with another important squad decision as the club continues its campaign across domestic competitions.



Orlando Pirates thanked the playmaker for his dedicated service and wished him success in the next chapter of his career.

The club added: “He departs as a league champion, a firm favourite among the supporters and a player who understood the responsibility of representing Orlando Pirates Football Club.”

Maswanganyi will now look to make his mark in the Bahrain Premier League after closing the door on his Orlando Pirates chapter.

World.title: SA passport holders can travel to these 101 countries without a visa
World.content:
SA passport holders can travel to 101 destinations without obtaining a visa in advance, according to the latest Henley Passport Index. Image: Allianz Travel Insurance

Holders of a South African passport can travel to 101 destinations without obtaining a visa in advance, according to the latest edition of the Henley Passport Index compiled by Henley & Partners.

The updated ranking places South Africa 96th out of 199 passports globally, with a visa-free score of 101.

The index evaluates passports based on the number of countries their holders can enter without needing to obtain a visa before departure.



It covers 199 passports and 227 travel destinations, making it one of the most widely cited indicators of global mobility.

Where does South Africa rank?

With a visa-free score of 101, South Africa’s passport ranks behind Qatar, which offers access to 112 destinations, and is one ahead of Belize in the global standings.

The ranking means South African travellers can visit 101 destinations with relative ease, although visas or advance authorisations are still required for many countries worldwide.

World’s Most Powerful Passports

According to the index, Asian and European countries continue to dominate global travel access.

Singapore holds the most powerful passport , with visa-free access to 192 destinations .

, with visa-free access to . Japan, South Korea and United Arab Emirates follow closely, each offering access to 188 destinations .

. Sweden ranks fifth, with a score of 187.

At the other end of the spectrum, Afghanistan remains the lowest-ranked passport, with access to only 22 destinations without a prior visa.

Measuring Global Mobility

The Henley Passport Index is widely used as a benchmark for global mobility.



The rankings reflect a range of factors including diplomatic relations, international agreements, and security considerations, all of which influence visa policies between countries.

Three Types of Visa Access

The 101 destinations available to South African passport holders fall into three main travel categories:

Visa-Free Access: Travellers can enter the destination simply by presenting their passport at immigration, with no advance application required.

Travellers can enter the destination simply by presenting their passport at immigration, with no advance application required. Visa on Arrival: Visitors can obtain a visa at the airport or border entry point, often after paying a fee.

Visitors can obtain a visa at the airport or border entry point, often after paying a fee. Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA): Travellers must complete a short online application before departure but do not need to visit an embassy or consulate.

While the 2026 ranking highlights moderate global mobility for South Africans, it also underscores the gap between South Africa’s travel access and that enjoyed by holders of the world’s most powerful passports.

World.title: ‘Give us a full mandate’ :  Morero’s pitch for the Joburg mayor position:
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The ANC's Dada Morero believes he is still the man for the job.

Morero was speaking to eNCA on Monday and stated his case as to why Johannesburg residents should give him and his party another chance.

It comes two days after the ANC unveiled potential candidates for the 2026 local government elections set for November as it opted not to name its final mayoral candidates.

Morero’s name was enlisted alongside his deputy Loyiso Masuku and party veteran Reverend Frank Chikane.

READ | ‘ANC cannot be trusted to fix what it has broken’ - DA

He said they have worked hard to revive the City of Johannesburg.

“The work that we've done in Johannesburg, considering what has happened between 2016 and 2022, is an indication that since we took over power in 2023.”

Much of what he told eNCA mirrors his State of the City Address back in May 2026, where he acknowledged the City’s mounting infrastructure and financial challenges but defended his record under the banner: We are a City at work.

As he did then, Morero once again painted a picture of a city that is functioning and growing despite decay and service delivery failures.

“There's been serious interventions that we're doing to reclaim the city, to ensure that we bring back the city to where it was, by law enforcement, dealing with financial sustainability of the city, and dealing with issues around service delivery,” he told eNCA.

But Morero’s hopeful picture of the city of gold comes at the back of critics who claim that it has lost its shine.

For residents living through water shortages, roads ridden by potholes, crime at its peak, and decaying infrastructure, seeing the glimmer of hope in Morero’s future almost feels impossible.

READ | Power outage leaves these Joburg areas with dry taps

Morero has put voters to the test: “Give the ANC a mandate to lead once more.”

This mandate, according to him, will act as a guide to delivering.

World.title: 'They're desperate': Pupils turn to fire hydrant for drinking water
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Pupils at Reiger Park Secondary School in Gauteng are reportedly being forced to endure shocking conditions just to get through the school day.

With more than 2,000 pupils and only a handful of functioning toilets, the school is also allegedly without access to drinking water.

The situation has become so desperate that pupils are reportedly turning to fire hydrants to quench their thirst.

READ | Water woes, broken toilets plague Reiger Park school

This is according to a source who asked not to be identified.

"They're really desperate for water...They can't get water from the toilets because they're quite disgusting... The cleaners are refusing to clean, and we've had this problem for a while now," the source told eNCA.

Continuing to paint a grim picture of the situation, the source said they often have to wait for a long time to use the bathroom given the limited number of toilets available.

The situation is reportedly worse during break time.

"The only taps that are running are the ones in the staff room and we can't get water from those taps and when we try to get water from those taps, they tell us to go to the taps in the bathrooms," he said.

School Governing Body (SGB) claims it was not aware of the extent of the conditions faced by pupils.

Chairperson Charona Louw said the matter has now been escalated to the district office.

World.title: Power outage leaves these Joburg areas with dry taps

This loss of power also disrupted water supply.

READ | Are you affected ? Throttling expected in these parts of Joburg

According to a statement by Joburg Water, due to the power outage which impacted the bulk supplier, the Randburg and Roodepoort System have declined to low and critically low water levels.

This has resulted in poor pressure to no water in various supply zones.

Some of the systems affected include:

Honeydew Reservoir and Tower

Boschkop Reservoir

Linden 1 Reservoir

Waterval and Quellerina Towers

Helderkruin Reservoir

Florida North and Horizon Towers

Constantia Tower

Witpoortjie Reservoir

"Despite the restoration of pumping to full capacity, customers will experience a delayed impact on water supply due to the period which there was no pumping from the Eikenhof Pump station," the statement read.

Meanwhile, City Power has confirmed that it has made progress in restoring supply following the Fordsburg Substation fire.

READ | Dry taps, leaking pipes: Lenasia residents demand answers

According to the power utility's spokesperson, Isaac Mangena, Bree Substation remains the only substation without power, affecting customers in the inner city of Johannesburg, Newtown, Hillbrow and surrounding areas.
