World.title: 'It was not yet Zolani's time' | Boxing world mourns Tete
World.content:
MDANTSANE - The death of former two-time boxing world champion Zolani Tete has been described as a huge loss, not only to the boxing fraternity but to the Eastern Cape at large.

Former boxer-turned-pastor Masibulele “Hawk” Makepula says the whole continent is devastated.

"People across the world are mourning Zolani's passing. Words cannot describe how we feel.

"No one came and said this was the will of God. No one can say Zolani ran his race and completed it, and no one can say his time came," Makepula said.

"It was not yet Zolani's time. His life was taken prematurely, and brutally so. Zolani died before his time."

July marked the end of Tete’s four-year ban following a doping scandal, which he denied. Makepula says Tete was ready to return to doing what he loved most.

"He kept himself fit and ready the whole time during the ban so that when the time came, he would be ready to get back in the ring.

"He was not selfish with his time and talent. He was training other boxers. It was only a matter of time before he became a world champion again. He was going to fight one or two fights and move on to a title fight because he was destined for greatness."

Boxing promoter Ayanda Matiti says what makes Tete’s death even more difficult to come to terms with is the way he was killed.

"It was a brutal assassination. No assassination can ever be accepted. Zolani was like a sheep; he did not deserve this.

"His body was full of bullets. Logic tells us that if it was a robbery, then they would have taken something. They did that to an unarmed man."

Matiti thanked authorities for acting swiftly but said this would be a difficult loss to overcome.

"We are all very sad. We are all mourning, not just his family or the boxing fraternity, but the whole province. In fact, the whole country," he said.

Tete was killed on Friday night while waiting for his gate to open. He was with a 27-year-old woman who was wounded and taken to hospital.

On Saturday, two people were taken in for questioning. One suspect, aged 30, was later released, but police spokesperson Brigadier Nobuntu Gantana said he remains a potential suspect.

The remaining 22-year-old suspect is appearing in the Mdantsane Magistrate’s Court. He has been charged with murder and attempted murder.

Two additional suspects, both aged 27, were arrested in Scenery Park on Sunday. They are expected to appear in court on Tuesday.

World.title: Springboks change half-backs for second All Blacks Test
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Springboks have changed their half-backs for the second Test against New Zealand on Saturday in Cape Town, promoting experienced duo Handre Pollard and Cobus Reinach.

Fly-half Pollard and scrum-half Reinach replace Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, now on the bench, and Grant Williams, who is unavailable due to a "niggle".

The changes were predictable as Feinberg-Mngomezulu, playing only his second match after injury, and Williams performed poorly in a 33-16 first Test loss last Saturday.

A third alteration to the team that fell in Johannesburg is Ethan Hooker coming in on the left wing in place of Kurt-Lee Arendse.

Arendse, who went off concussed early in the match at Ellis Park, moves to the right wing in place of Cheslin Kolbe, another "niggle" casualty.

There could yet be a fourth change to the starting line-up. If flanker Siya Kolisi is passed fit after a hamstring injury, he will replace Paul de Villiers.

"Handre has delivered for us under extreme pressure, and we feel that is what he and Cobus have the potential to bring at the beginning of the game," said head coach Rassie Erasmus.

"Then we have Morne (van den Berg) and Sacha coming on later with their different styles of play that will be good for us this weekend.

"Cheslin and Grant suffered niggles last weekend, which ruled them out of contention for selection.

"We have bracketed Siya alongside Paul to allow us time to monitor how Siya comes through training this week."

Loose forward Pieter-Steph du Toit will continue as captain and is set to win his 100th cap on Saturday, one week after centre Damian de Allende reached the milestone.

Ox Nche, widely regarded as the best loosehead prop in the world, will make his 50th appearance for the Springboks.

The bench has been reshuffled with only two survivors from the first Test -- 'hybrid' player Andre Esterhuizen, a centre who can play as a loose forward, and prop Gerhard Steenekamp.

Among those promoted is Deon Fourie, who will celebrate his 40th birthday in September. He can operate as a hooker or flanker.

Should he take the field, Fourie will become the oldest Springbok to play in a Test, surpassing Victor Matfield and Schalk Brits, who were 38 years old in their final Tests.

South Africa (15-1)

Damian Willemse; Kurt-Lee Arendse, Jesse Kriel, Damian de Allende, Ethan Hooker; Handre Pollard, Cobus Reinach; Jasper Wiese, Pieter-Steph du Toit (capt), Siya Kolisi or Paul de Villiers; Ruan Nortje, Eben Etzebeth; Wilco Louw, Malcolm Marx, Ox Nche

Replacements: Deon Fourie, Gerhard Steenekamp, Thomas du Toit, Lood de Jager, Andre Esterhuizen, Cameron Hanekom, Morne van den Berg, Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu

Coach: Rassie Erasmus

World.title: Wamunyoro's report on road to 2027
World.content:
Democracy for Citizens (DCP) party leader Rigathi Gachagua delivers his conclave report after the end of a 55 days retreat at his Wamunyoro residence in Mathira constituency, Nyeri County, August 24, 2026. [Mose Sammy, Standard]

When former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua announced his 45-day conclave on June 9 in Wamunyoro, he assured the country that he would come out with a formula for identifying a single Presidential candidate in the Opposition.

The conclave, he announced, would come up with the negotiations implementation framework strategy with his fellow Opposition leaders.

World.title: Relief for schools as government releases Sh18.5b capitation
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Education CS Julius Ogamba. [File, Standard]

The government has released Sh18.5 billion in capitation to support operations in public basic education institutions during the third term of 2026, as schools reopened across the country on Monday.

Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba said the funds have already been released and will support learners in pre-primary, primary, junior and senior schools.

The allocation is intended to facilitate smooth school operations and ensure learning activities continue without disruption.

The Sh18.5 billion has been distributed across three major capitation programmes, with Free Day Secondary Education (FDSE) allocated Sh10.963 billion, accounting for the biggest portion of the Term Three capitation.

The money will support operations in public day and secondary schools and comes as institutions prepare learners for a busy academic term.

Free Day Junior School Education has received Sh6.1 billion, to support learners in the second tier of basic education and help institutions meet operational requirements as the Competency-Based Education system continues to expand.

Meanwhile, Free Primary Education has been allocated Sh1.4 billion to support learning in public primary schools.

The funds come as a relief to school heads who had raised concerns on the insufficient funds disbursed to schools this year.

However, Ogamba said the disbursement demonstrates the Government's commitment to ensuring that learners have access to free and compulsory basic education as provided for under Article 53(1)(b) of the Constitution.

“The Government affirms its commitment to fulfil its duty to learners and educational institutions,” said the CS.

Ogamba also warned school heads and principals against misuse of the funds, directing them to ensure the money is spent prudently and for the benefit of learners.

School administrators have further been cautioned against imposing unauthorised levies on parents and learners.

Ogamba said the Ministry would take firm action against institutions found to have misappropriated public resources or imposed illegal charges.

“We will deal firmly with any verified cases of misappropriation of resources and the imposition of unauthorised levies,” he said.

The warning comes as schools reopen for the third term, a period that is expected to be particularly demanding for institutions and learners because of the academic activities and assessments scheduled for the school calendar.

The Ministry has maintained that capitation is meant to ease the financial burden on families and enable schools to provide essential services without passing prohibited costs to parents.

Ogamba reiterated that school administrators must remain accountable for the public funds entrusted to them, warning that verified cases of misuse will attract action from the Ministry.

The Government has also reaffirmed that every child is entitled to free and compulsory basic education, placing the responsibility on education officials and school managers to ensure capitation achieves its intended purpose.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro begins nationwide political mobilisation ahead of 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro after attending service at Gathuki-ini ACK Church on August 23, 2026. [Boniface Gikandi, Standard]

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro has said he will take his campaign for national transformation across Kenya as he positions himself for the 2027 presidential race.

Ndindi said he was interested in leadership committed to addressing concerns in education, health, youth and unemployment, among other needs.

Nyoro, who is the People’s Party of Kenya leader, spoke at St Michael Gathuki-ini ACK Church in Kiharu on Sunday, where he called for respect and political maturity.

Addressing residents in Kiria-ini (Mathioya) and Gakira (Kangema), he urged politicians to engage in a responsible manner.

“I trust in God that after next year Kenya will be able to have leadership that will be responsible for improving citizens' standards of living,” he said.

He regretted that hundreds of university graduates in the area were yet to secure employment.

“I plead with Kenyans to support my course that is geared to transform the nation and ensure equality and transparency,” said the PPK leader.

Nyoro said that after engaging Murang'a residents, he will take his transformation campaigns to all parts of the country.

Speaking at Kiria-ini market, he said he would engage the people to seek their blessings.

“All along had been feeling the urge to lead the country, thus the need to come out in the open and fight for position,” he said.

On Monday, the MP announced his exit from the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA), declaring that he will join the opposition ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Nyoro, an economist serving his second term as Kiharu MP, said he will work with opposition leaders to push for what he termed real change in Kenya.

The legislator said all opposition presidential aspirants are welcome at rallies organised by the PPK.

His move marks a significant political shift as parties and leaders begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 polls.

World.title: City Hall in rush to expand drainage system ahead of El Nino
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja during an inspection tour of the ongoing drainage system expansion. [GPS]

Nairobi County has embarked on drainage expansion works aimed at mitigating floodwaters ahead of El Nino rains.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, while calling on city residents to remain alert and proactive, said City Hall has intensified preparations and accelerated identification of hotspots.

The governor on Friday said his administration is taking early and coordinated action to minimise the impact of heavy rains, urging residents to stay calm, pay attention to official information and follow guidance from the multi-agency team established to coordinate the city’s preparedness and emergency response.

“We are working proactively to address the challenges of flooding before El Nino hits the ground. We urge our people not to panic but to be alert and get information from our multi-agency team,” said Sakaja.

The Governor spoke during an inspection tour of several flood-prone areas in Nairobi, including the Mombasa Road-Bunyala Junction corridor and Globe Roundabout, which experienced significant flooding during previous heavy rains.

Sakaja said drainage works are already underway in the affected areas, with teams working to open up and deepen drainage channels, clear obstructions, and improve storm-water flow to prevent a repeat of the flooding witnessed previously.

His remarks come as weatherman warned of increased rainfall in the coming months, with Nairobi among the urban areas requiring heightened preparedness because of its exposure to flooding and the impact of heavy rainfall on roads, settlements and other critical infrastructure.

Sakaja said the county has so far brought together the disaster management teams, Kenya Red Cross, Kenya Urban Roads Authority (KURA) and Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA) under a coordinated programme worth Sh2.4 billion to strengthen Nairobi’s flood resilience.

Of the amount, Sh2 billion has been set aside for drainage and flood-mitigation works targeting 19 roads in flood-prone areas.

The projects are at an advanced stage, with tenders awarded and contractors expected to commence implementation after completion of the necessary processes.

Sakaja reiterated that the programme will complement ongoing county interventions under the Nairobi Regeneration Programme, which includes the rehabilitation and upgrading of critical infrastructure across the city.

“The Sh2 billion will support a comprehensive drainage overhaul that complements the ongoing Nairobi Regeneration Programme. Our goal is to permanently address the flooding challenges that have affected the city for many years,” Sakaja said.

He said the focus is not only on responding to floods after they occur, but on addressing the infrastructure weaknesses that have historically made Nairobi vulnerable to flooding.

To strengthen preparedness, the county has established five specialised sub-committees under the multi-agency framework.

The committees include Infrastructure and Drainage; Emergency Response and Evacuation; Shelter and Relief; Security and Traffic and Communication.

While the Infrastructure and Drainage committee will coordinate the clearing and improvement of drainage systems, rivers and other critical infrastructure, the Emergency Response and Evacuation committee will oversee rapid response, rescue and evacuation operations whenever emergencies occur.

The Shelter and Relief committee will prepare safe shelters and coordinate the provision of food, water, medical assistance and other essential support to affected residents.

The Security and Traffic committee will coordinate security, traffic management and emergency access, while the Communication committee will strengthen early-warning systems, public alerts and timely dissemination of information.

Sakaja said the county is also mobilising personnel, equipment and other resources to clear blocked drains, remove silt and waste and strengthen emergency response systems in areas identified as vulnerable.

He urged residents and their associations, businesses and other stakeholders to play an active role in flood preparedness by keeping drainage areas clear and paying attention to official warnings.

The county chief said residents in high-risk areas will be provided with timely information on emerging weather conditions and the actions they should take when heavy rains occur.

“We don’t want people to panic. We want people to be proactive, to listen to information and to work with us. The multi-agency team is in place, and we are preparing before the rains intensify,” Sakaja said.

According to him, the multi-agency approach will also help eliminate jurisdictional gaps by bringing together national and county agencies to operate as one coordinated team.

He said the combination of drainage upgrades, emergency preparedness, early-warning systems and coordinated response would strengthen Nairobi’s resilience and reduce disruption caused by heavy rains.

The multi-agency team is expected to meet next week to review progress, coordinate ongoing works and further push the city’s El Niño preparedness agenda.

World.title: Public officers eyeing elective posts to resign by February 10 - IEBC
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon addressing the press at a past press conference. [File, Standard]

Public officers seeking to contest elective positions in the 2027 General Election have until February 10, 2027, to resign from office, the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has announced.

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon said the deadline falls exactly six months before the August 10, 2027, General Election, which the Commission has confirmed will be held on a Tuesday.

“Any public officer who intends to contest in this election must resign from public office by Wednesday, 10th February 2027, which is exactly six months before the election,” Ethekon said.

The IEBC said adherence to the timelines will be non-negotiable, noting that they are legally binding and essential to ensuring an orderly electoral process.

Under the timetable, political parties must submit their membership lists and details of candidates participating in party primaries by March 16, 2027.

Party primaries and any related disputes must be concluded by May 8, while independent candidates are also required to meet their legal obligations by the same date.

Presidential aspirants will have until May 24 to submit lists of supporting voters drawn from a majority of Kenya’s counties.

Candidate registration will begin on May 29, with specific deadlines applying to the various elective positions.

The official campaign period will commence after candidates are registered, but not earlier than May 29, 2027.

Ethekon warned political parties, candidates and their supporters against breaching the prescribed campaign period, saying any electioneering outside the legal window will be unlawful.

The restrictions cover campaign posters, billboards, political caravans and other forms of campaigning.

Campaigning will close on August 7, 2027, 48 hours before Kenyans head to the polls.

“The law prescribes when election campaigns may commence,” Ethekon said, urging political parties, candidates and their supporters to strictly comply with electoral laws and regulations.

The deadline is among key milestones unveiled by the electoral commission as political parties, aspirants and other stakeholders begin preparations for the next General Election.

World.title: Schools will open on August 24 as scheduled, Ogamba says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Students heading home during recent demonstrations. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The Ministry of Education said the official academic calendar remains unchanged.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, August 19, Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba insists that learners will return to school on Monday, August 24, 2026.

The CS has dismissed reports circulating on social media claiming that the reopening of schools for the third term has been postponed, warning parents, teachers, learners and education stakeholders against relying on unauthorised online notices.

“We wish to clarify that the academic calendar for Basic Education institutions and Teacher Training Colleges remains unchanged,” the CS said.

The clarification comes two days before the scheduled reopening of schools, amid reports circulating on social media platforms suggesting that the government had pushed back the start of Term III.

"Our attention has been drawn to misleading information circulating on various social media platforms, purporting that the academic calendar for basic education institutions and Teachers Training Colleges has been changed," he stated.

The Ministry termed the reports “FALSE” and urged members of the public to completely disregard them.

Ogamba said the Ministry had directed Regional Directors of Education, County Directors of Education and Sub-County Directors of Education to ensure strict compliance with the approved academic calendar contained in a circular dated October 9, 2025.

According to the Ministry, pre-primary, primary, junior, senior and secondary schools will begin Term III on Monday, August 24. The term will run for nine weeks and end on October 23, 2026.

The reopening marks the final academic term of the school year, with schools expected to implement the approved programmes as they prepare learners for the end-of-year national assessments and examinations.

Diploma Teachers Training Colleges will also resume academic operations on August 24, with their third term scheduled to conclude on November 6, 2026.

The Ministry further confirmed that the national assessment and examination calendar has not been altered for KPSEA, KILEA, KJSEA, KPLEA and KCSE are scheduled to begin from October 26, 2026, as earlier announced.

The Ministry also reminded schools that extracurricular activities and visits to secondary schools will remain banned during Term III.

The latest clarification is part of efforts by the government to prevent confusion among parents, learners and teachers as schools prepare to reopen.

Ogamba urged education stakeholders to obtain information through official Ministry communication channels, rather than social media posts whose authenticity cannot be established.

“Parents, teachers and learners and members of the public are advised to strictly rely on the Ministry's official communication channels and field officers for accurate information," he said.

World.title: Ruto denies Sh104bn SHA technology contract
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto has dismissed claims that the government entered into a controversial Sh104 billion contract with Safaricom and Apeiro Limited for the Social Health Authority (SHA) technology system.

Speaking on Tuesday evening at the Presidential Townhall held during the National Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in Nairobi, Ruto defended the government's investment in digital health, saying the technology was designed to improve transparency and accountability in the management of SHA services.

“There is no Sh104 billion contract. What we have done is design a digital system to make sure that everything is visible. Every treatment must be traceable, and every payment must be accounted for,” Ruto said.

He explained that the government had not purchased the technology outright but had engaged investors who own the equipment, with the State paying for the services provided.

His remarks were echoed by Digital Health Agency Chief Executive Anthony Lenaiyara, who rejected claims that SHA had committed Sh104 billion to technology upgrades.

“It is not correct or true that SHA has undertaken any upgrade or invested Sh104 billion in technology upgrades. What we did is build a digital superhighway comprising 43 systems to support Universal Health Coverage,” Lenaiyara said.

Lenaiyara said the technology infrastructure had been rolled out without requiring health facilities to purchase the devices, adding that the system had transformed the processing and accountability of SHA claims.

He contrasted the new system with the former National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) model, where claims were processed using physical files that moved between different offices for verification and approval.

Ruto also addressed other government programmes, saying the State had mobilised resources to construct 23,000 additional classrooms to ease pressure caused by shortages of learning spaces.

World.title: 'That was not healthcare, it was theft'- Ruto on old health system
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during the official opening of the Kenya Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC), Nairobi, August 18,2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has accused the defunct National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) system of enabling theft from sick Kenyans, citing claims for procedures that never happened.

Speaking on Tuesday, August 18, at the opening of the Kenya Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in Nairobi, Ruto described the old system as opaque and vulnerable to abuse.

"We heard of claims for procedures that never happened, fictitious patients and inflated bills. That was not healthcare, it was theft, and theft from sick Kenyans," said Ruto.

He called digital health systems the backbone holding the reforms together and said they would close loopholes that let people profit from the system's weaknesses.

Ruto ranked Universal Health Coverage (UHC) alongside the Affordable Housing Programme as one of the government's most consequential social transformation efforts, crediting collaboration between national and county governments for changes in how healthcare is financed, delivered and accounted for.

The two-day summit, themed "Reforms Delivered, Health as a Right," has drawn more than 5,000 delegates to audit progress under the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA) and set priorities for the remainder of Ruto's term, according to Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale.

Ruto said 32.3 million Kenyans are now registered with the Social Health Authority (SHA), which replaced NHIF in October 2024.

Eight million have received treatment, more than 1.2 million mothers have been supported to deliver safely and more than 500,000 surgical procedures have been supported, he added.

He put Kenyans' previous annual out-of-pocket health spending at Sh150 billion ($1.16 billion), saying families had borrowed, sold assets or organised harambees to cover medical costs before the reforms.

"Millions paid out of pocket, borrowed, sold assets, organised harambees or stayed away from hospital because they could not afford care," said Ruto.

Since October 2024, SHA has received more than Sh209 billion ($1.62 billion) and paid more than Sh178 billion ($1.38 billion) to contracted facilities across all 47 counties, Ruto added.

He credited 107,800 Community Health Promoters, deployed under a shared financing arrangement between national and county governments, with reaching more than nine million households and referring over 750,000 people for further treatment.

On supply chains, Ruto said the Kenya Medical Supplies Authority's (KEMSA) fill rate had risen from about 40 per cent to 91 per cent, helped by a Sh1.5 billion ($11.6 million) recapitalisation and a Sh10 billion ($77.4 million) credit line.

The reforms rest on four laws Ruto signed on 19 October 2023: the Primary Health Care Act, the Social Health Insurance Act, the Digital Health Act and the Facilities Improvement Financing Act.

Ruto acknowledged gaps remained in registration, benefit clarity, claims processing and digital systems.

"The ultimate measure of reform is not the laws we pass or the numbers we register, but the experience of the patient in terms of dependable, affordable and dignified care," said Ruto.

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki, Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, Duale and Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja attended the opening session, alongside county governors, principal secretaries, members of Parliament and development partners.

The summit runs through Wednesday.

World.title: Quiet on set. How AI transformed China’s microdrama scene
World.content:
Hengdian, China —

Everything seemed to be business as usual as filming got underway on a dimly lit set in a basement in Hengdian, a town nicknamed “China’s Hollywood” for its sprawling complex of film studios.

Cameramen raced around hectically setting up lights and checking shots as choreographers ran through fight sequences and a prop team worked out how to hoist a net that would later restrain a hostage.

Actors, most dressed as assassins and hitmen, milled about or squatted, smoking cigarettes and getting occasional touch-ups from roving hair stylists and make-up artists as they waited for their scene to start.

But behind the bustle was a new reality: while just a few months ago, production of these so-called “microdramas” was flourishing in Hengdian and other hubs – today, these sets are falling quiet.

Seemingly overnight, new AI-video generation tools have taken over the microdrama industry, able to produce these popular, vertical shows at a fraction of the cost, decimating the number of live-action productions across the country and flooding platforms with AI-made content. More than 120,000 microdramas were released in the first three months of this year — with 95 percent of those generated by AI, according to Chinese state media.

That’s made the industry one of the most visible examples of how China’s breakneck AI transformation is impacting people’s livelihoods — wiping out jobs and creating new ones, leaving everyone unsure what’s next. It’s the kind of technological disruption that many creatives fear could upend movie-making far beyond China.

Between takes actor Junlin, who asked to be identified by her stage name, talks about how she’s struggling to stay afloat as a “bitter winter” has arrived for productions like hers.

“With fewer productions hiring, your space for survival is constantly squeezed,” said the 24-year-old, dressed in combat boots and a high ponytail to play a head assassin who storms around with a posse of hitmen in an upcoming microdrama.

She’d worked only seven days in June, a sharp fall from the spring when she’d been filming 25 out of about 30 days per month in Hengdian and other cities. “I’m someone who gets anxious easily,” she said. “If I’m not on set, I would be in a constant state of anxiety.”

Boom time

Hengdian, a town of just over 200,000 tucked in a rural part of eastern China’s Zhejiang province, had been booming with the rise of the microdrama industry in recent years.

Broken into roughly 90-second episodes, microdramas first emerged during the pandemic, capitalizing on the popularity of short video apps like Douyin and Kuaishou as cinemas and studios closed.

While each episode is designed to be quick to consume on a mobile phone, together the clips weave together plotlines that can stretch the length of a feature film.

These microdramas — and their often soapy or outlandish plots about wicked mother-in-laws, mistaken identities, wartime heroics and wronged lovers — have since proliferated in China and spread to audiences overseas, where they’ve spawned a fast-growing, multi-billion-dollar industry.

They’ve also caught the attention of China’s censors, who are tightening oversight of microdramas with new rules set to take effect in September. Plotlines, for example, will need to “adhere to correct political direction.”

Last year, the domestic microdrama industry was valued at nearly $15 billion, according to market research firm DataEye, almost double the market size for box-office feature films in the country. Its rise ushered in a welcome heyday for young creatives at a time of high youth unemployment in China.

“Once microdramas took off, there was a nonstop stream of roles I could take on as long as I wanted to film,” said Bi Zhiqiang, 27, another actor living in Hengdian, who quickly built a career after moving there in 2021 as the industry was taking shape.

“Many people who didn’t even study acting or film and television joined because there were more and more opportunities.”

The lure drew thousands of crews to Hengdian last year to shoot projects in and around the sprawling Hengdian World Studios.

It was a fresh injection of energy for the town and its decades-old eponymous studio, known for its large-scale replicas of some of China’s iconic imperial architecture, like the Summer Palace and the Forbidden City, and for birthing Chinese blockbusters.

Other hubs — like Qingdao, Xi’an, and Zhengzhou — emerged across the country, too, with microdrama crews shooting in expressly built complexes with fake mansions, boardrooms, and ERs.

Tourists explore a vast film set replica of Beijing’s Forbidden City at Hengdian World Studios. Matthew Knight/AFP/Getty Images

But the industry quickly became a pressure cooker for actors and production crews, due to a hyper-competitive model built around cranking out as many microdramas as possible in the hopes that one would go viral.

Actors and crew describe standard 18 to 20-hour working days as productions rushed to stay within budget while shooting what are essentially feature-length movies in the space of roughly a week.

“As long as they keep filming, they can keep releasing. And the logic is — there will always be one that becomes a hit,” said Guo Ertai, a director and actor at the National Theater of China in Beijing, who followed audiences and money into the microdrama industry several years ago.

At the bottom of the pecking order are extras, who might work long shifts for as little as 10 Chinese yuan ($1.50) per hour, a wage one former actor commented wryly was less than the rental rate for some of the animals used in productions.

Even still, the allure of success kept the industry flush with young, ambitious actors, directors and creatives.

A cameraman optimizes a shot for mobile phone consumption at a Hengdian microdrama film set in June. Joyce Jiang/CNN

Unlike film, which has a high barrier to entry, microdramas “gave an ordinary person an opportunity,” said Guo, the director. The thinking is “‘I can become rich overnight, I can become a star overnight, I can earn a lot of money overnight with very little outlay,’” he said.

Microdrama actors have become celebrities in their own right with millions of followers on social media platforms. Some television and film stars — including martial arts legend Jet Li — have starred in microdramas. Even those without broad name recognition, who were able to land leading roles in successful dramas, could make multiples of an average monthly urban wage.

But as more money and bigger names entered, competition grew fiercer, pushing a drive to export the dramas overseas for more revenue — and use whatever means available to cut costs.

Enter AI

It took a few weeks for actor Zhuang Wenjie, 28, to realize something was wrong when she returned to Hengdian after celebrating the Chinese New Year holiday in her hometown in February.

She had moved to the area last summer and felt she was just beginning to make a name for herself and could start auditioning for higher profile roles.

Zhuang Wenjie (left) played the personal maid of a fictional Empress Dowager, played by Zhang Xiaoli (right) on a micro-drama production in January. Zhuang Wenjie

A microdrama being filmed at Hengdian World Studios in March 2024. Qian Chenfei/China News Service/VCG/Getty Images A crew using one of the historic replicas as a backdrop. Liu Ziyi/Xinhua/Getty Images

At first, she didn’t quite connect the empty streets around her with the growing number of AI-generated microdramas she saw on her social media feeds.

Soon, though, it became obvious: people weren’t returning because jobs had dried up. “Suddenly (there was) a feeling of impending crisis,” Zhuang said.

ByteDance’s SeeDance 2.0 had arrived.

Seemingly overnight, Chinese social media was swamped with realistic-looking, AI-generated videos, as users played around with the new, powerful video generation tool.

And when it came to microdramas, SeeDance 2.0 was well positioned. ByteDance owns two of the main platforms in China that host microdramas: Douyin, Tiktok’s sister app, and Hongguo. It also has a repository of novels that make up a well of copyrighted material for scripts that collaborating production teams can draw from.

Other tech firms have released rival video-generating technology in recent months, including another short video app owner Kuaishuo, tech giant Alibaba and AI firm MiniMax.

An editor adds titles to a microdrama in Jiaxing, Zhejiang province. VCG/Getty Images

Using next-gen AI video tools, a 120-minute project of ordinary quality can take a five-member team roughly a week to produce and cost some 15,000 yuan, about $2,200, one production firm told CNN — less than a tenth of what’s typically cited as the low-end cost of a live production.

In the first half of the year on Douyin alone, 220,000 new AI-generated microdramas racked up a staggering 500 billion views, according to DataEye, the market research firm. Some were animations, but more than half since March used AI that simulated real people.

Zhuang decided to leave town in April, joining an exodus of actors and crew from the area. “The number of jobs in Hengdian was decreasing day by day, and the pay was also getting lower and lower every day … the hardship really did defeat me,” she said.

Actors who did stay on described cratering salaries, such as being offered 300 yuan (about $45) a day to play the kind of leading role that would have previously paid thousands. Some have turned to side jobs to make ends meet.

Liu Yuzhan, 29, says he’d been making steady money booking four new roles a month in the past couple years. Now, Liu says he’s picking up extra work as a food delivery driver.

“I have my own mortgage and I’m responsible for my parents’ retirement. Given the current market of microdramas… it’s simply not enough to cover my daily expenses,” he said.

The ‘bubble’

As AI tools put microdrama actors out of work, social media chat groups that used to advertise acting opportunities were swamped with a different kind of classified: for AI editors, programmers, designers and screenwriters. And a new crop of companies, editors and entrepreneurs have poured into the space.

Among them is Tan Chen, a 21-year-old college student who founded a startup that began focusing on AI production in April.

His team, which is based in Jinan, a provincial capital in eastern China, takes scripts or novels, and “optimizes” them for microdramas by crunching down the narratives and ramping up the excitement and suspense. They decide the look of the characters and the set, a process Tan describes as “similar to casting and location scouting,” and then build a storyboard.

“We need to transform what we see in words into something that can be expressed visually. That really tests our production staff’s directorial thinking and audiovisual language abilities,” he said.

How well the AI images come together depends on that language. Employees known as “card-pullers” must use prompts — typically written with the help of AI — to repeatedly generate AI video clips until they get ones that best convey the scene, which are then edited together.

When his team started, Tan said clients would pay them 1,000 yuan, about $150, a minute, typically for a 120-minute project.

But just like actors and live production crews, these creatives are also feeling the squeeze.

A crush of programmers joined the industry and middlemen taking a cut to link creators with clients have multiplied, driving down profits for teams like Tan’s. He’s now fielding projects for as low as 150 yuan per minute — around $20.

“This rapidly growing market inevitably has a certain degree of bubble,” he said.

His company also recently switched to making AI-generated cartoons to avoid inadvertently using AI images that draw from real actor’s faces.

‘If you can’t beat it’

The use of AI characters that resemble real-life actors, without permission, has become a key issue in the industry — with at least one case of a well-known actor receiving court-ordered compensation, state media reports.

But other actors, aren’t so lucky.

Actor Yu Shutian, 31, recently found what she believes was her own face “blended into AI,” after fans alerted her to an AI-generated character that resembled her.

She knew it was nearly impossible to prove the likeness was based on her face, so she never pursued legal action. She also says she realized it was probably the technology, not the creator who was responsible.

“AI is unstoppable. If you can’t beat it, join it, so I’d rather find a reasonable way to embrace AI,” said Yu, who is starting to use the tech as she’s moved some of her focus to directing.

That sentiment illustrates a central tension raised by many of the actors who shared their stories with CNN.

While AI may render the miles of studio space and life-sized sets of places like Hengdian unnecessary, what role humans — including actors — ultimately play in the industry, working alongside AI to create art and entertainment, is far from settled, they say.

Microdrama streaming app Hongguo in recent weeks raised production standards around AI-generated dramas, and ratings in recent weeks suggest there’s still viewer appetite for “real people dramas,” which rank in the platform’s top 10 alongside AI productions and cartoons.

“AI is formulaic — it can’t express the full range of human emotions and desires,” said Junlin, the actor who is staying put, for now, in Hengdian. “How could it possibly replace humans?”

But when it comes to the transformation underway in her industry, she sees the newer actors like herself, who are still trying to make it, as the most vulnerable.

“AI absolutely can’t replace a real person,” she said. “But it might be able to replace me.”

World.title: The US has been imposing sanctions on Iran since 1979
World.content:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has warned in an op-ed that an “economic D-Day” is coming for Iran, stopping short of giving further details.

“Now we are entering the endgame. At dawn begins an economic D-Day — the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary,” he wrote in the Financial Times ahead of a scheduled news conference today.

The US has been imposing sanctions on Iran since 1979, after the US embassy in Tehran was seized following the Iranian Revolution, according to the US State Department.

A Congressional Research Service (CRS) report on US sanctions on Iran says they were used to “deter, constrain, and encourage change in the adversarial behavior of the Iranian regime.”

“US sanctions on Iran are arguably the most extensive and comprehensive set of sanctions that the United States maintains on any country,” the report says.

The financial penalties are wide-ranging, banning nearly all US trade with Iran, blocking Iranian government assets in the country and prohibiting foreign assistance and arms sales, the report outlines.

In 2013, the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control said that the US could sell food, medicine, and medical devices to Iran.

According to the CRS report, the US is also allowed to provide telecommunications equipment to Iranians to help them circumvent the Iranian regime’s attempts at cutting off internet access.

World.title: The world’s oldest president left for a ‘brief stay’ in Europe. He hasn’t returned in two months
World.content:
When Paul Biya won his first presidential election in Cameroon in 1984, Nformi Bime was 23 and still a student.

Bime is now 65 and retired from teaching. Biya is 93 – and still president. Last year, he won a disputed eighth term that could keep him in office until he is nearly 100.

“The best is yet to come,” Biya said before the election, which his opponents called fraudulent and was marred by deadly clashes between protesters and police.

For the past two months, however, the man who has ruled Cameroon since 1982, when as prime minister he assumed power following the resignation of the sitting president, has been thousands of miles away. He left on June 7 for what his office called a “brief private stay in Europe” — now his longest uninterrupted absence from the Central African nation in years.

Last week, government spokesman René Emmanuel Sadi told French radio RFI that Biya was in Geneva, Switzerland and was not hospitalized, but did not give more detail on his whereabouts.

A president who is rarely seen

Biya is Cameroon’s second president since independence in 1960 and one of the world’s longest-serving leaders. He first won office in 1984 under a one-party system, then won six more elections after multiparty politics was introduced.

He has spent extended periods abroad during his presidency. But his latest absence has revived questions about his health and who is running the country while he is away.

Rumors about Biya’s health and whereabouts have long been part of public life in Cameroon, where he is rarely seen in public. His office has repeatedly had to push back against speculation that he was seriously ill or had died. In 2024, the government banned media discussions about his health, calling them a national security matter.

Biya’s long rule also reflects a wider contrast across Africa. The continent has the world’s youngest population, but several countries are still led by aging leaders whose political careers began decades ago, including former liberation figures now governing in a different era.

For millions of Cameroonians, Biya is the only president they have ever known.

Bime’s children are among them. His oldest is 32, and his youngest is 18.

Abit Riassai Acha, a 26-year-old doctoral student and community youth leader at the University of Yaoundé II, belongs to the same generation.

Cameroon incumbent President Paul Biya flanked by his wife Chantal Biya looks on during a campaign rally in Maroua on October 7, 2025. Robert Fimbaye/AFP/Getty Images

“Growing up, President Biya was the only president I knew, so his presidency has been part of my entire experience of Cameroon,” said Acha, who voted for the first time in last year’s presidential election, backing the youthful opposition candidate Samuel Hiram Iyodi, 38.

After more than four decades under the same president, questions about his leadership have only grown.

“Because this has happened repeatedly over the years, many Cameroonians have become used to it,” Acha said of Biya’s long absences. “But becoming accustomed to something does not necessarily mean that people should stop asking questions about how the country is being governed.”

Iyodi, who finished eighth in last year’s presidential election, which several candidates, including one of Biya’s main challengers, were barred from contesting, has called on parliament to ask Cameroon’s Constitutional Council to consider whether Biya’s absence amounts to a vacancy in the presidency. But such a move is unlikely to succeed, given the dominance of Biya’s ruling Cameroon People’s Democratic Movement.

Despite being away, Biya has continued to make key decisions from abroad, including a major military reshuffle announced earlier this month. Yet questions about his prolonged stay overseas have left officials publicly assuring Cameroonians that their president is still alive.

Government spokesman Sadi dismissed concerns about a power vacuum, telling RFI that “President Paul Biya is alive” and “will soon return.”

From hope to frustration

Cameroon’s President Paul Biya talks with French President François Mitterrand, right, at the Elysée Palace in Paris on February 15, 1983. Pierre Guillaud/AFP/Getty Images/File

Bime is old enough to remember when Biya was the change. He first heard Biya’s name in the 1970s, when he served as secretary-general of the presidency under Cameroon’s first president after independence, Ahmadou Ahidjo. After Ahidjo resigned in 1982, Biya took over.

When Biya first appeared on the ballot two years later, Bime saw him as a “representation of hope,” he said. “We believed he was young and dynamic – handsome too. He meant so much to Cameroonians.”

Few imagined that the man they saw as a new beginning would remain in power for decades. For his critics, the disappointment is not just about how long Biya has stayed in office, but what they see as his failure to improve the lives of ordinary Cameroonians.

Related article Pope Leo XIV arrives in procession to celebrate Mass at the Japoma Stadium, in Douala, Cameroon, on Friday. Andrew Medichini/AP Pope’s Mass for more than 100,000 in Cameroon highlights Catholicism’s growth in Africa 3 min read

Political analyst Collins Molua Ikome, a Cameroonian based in Germany, said he saw some of the country’s problems firsthand when he visited Cameroon in April.

“Roads in Cameroon are extremely bad. I even witnessed a fatal accident,” he told CNN.

Ikome also pointed to frequent power cuts, corruption and a lack of jobs for young people.

Wilson Tamfuh, a public and international law professor at the University of Dschang in West Cameroon, said the country has institutions that can keep the government running when the president delegates responsibilities. Key duties, he said, can be handled by the prime minister, the secretary-general at the presidency and ministers.

But the bigger question, Tamfuh said, is whether the government is solving the country’s longstanding problems.

“People want the Anglophone crisis resolved, standards of living ameliorated, more good roads, fewer people on the streets with degrees, and more,” he told CNN, referring to the years-long separatist conflict in Cameroon’s English-speaking regions.

Whenever Biya eventually leaves office, his successor will inherit a country also facing attacks by Boko Haram militants in the north and deep economic frustration among young people.

President Paul Biya is pictured during the summit of the UDEAC in Brazzaville, Republic of the Congo, in December 1984. Martine Archambault/AFP/Getty Images/File

Healthcare is another concern. Ikome said access to quality healthcare remains out of reach for many Cameroonians.

“Life expectancy in the country is below 70 years. However, Biya has far outlived that due to access to medical healthcare abroad, which the ordinary Cameroonian cannot access due to poverty,” Ikome said.

The divide is not unique to Cameroon. Across Africa, political elites have often sought healthcare or maintained homes abroad, even as public services at home struggle.

For Bime, the question is more personal: Will he live to see another president?

After decades of waiting for change, he worries he may not – and that Biya could outlive him and many others who are not part of the country’s elite.

“Anytime they have a cold, they run overseas and are taken care of, but the other Cameroonians are dying because of lack of care,” he said.

World.title: Iranian currency drops to record low as US plans to tighten sanctions
World.content:
Iran’s ​currency – the rial – has dropped ⁠to a record ⁠low of more ‌than ⁠two million to the US dollar on the open market, according to websites that track the currency’s movement.

The free market rate is different from the official rate, which values the rial 29 percent higher against the US dollar.

The decline in the rial comes as the US Treasury plans a new raft of sanctions against Iran, and amid a worsening economic crisis in Iran.

The International Monetary Fund expects the Iranian economy to contract by more than five percent this year, while inflation for food exceeds 100 percent and unemployment rises.

World.title: FM, Finance Minister discuss boosting economic diplomacy
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty received Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk on Sunday, August 23, 2026, to discuss ways to enhance coordination and integration with state institutions and support Egypt’s economic and financial efforts through Egyptian diplomatic missions abroad in line with the state’s economic priorities.

Kouchouk also held a meeting with Egyptian ambassadors appointed to head diplomatic missions abroad to review the state’s economic and financial policy priorities, as well as highlight economic reform efforts and opportunities for enhancing cooperation and investment.

The meeting also discussed ways for Egyptian embassies to support efforts to promote the Egyptian economy, highlight investment and trade opportunities, and strengthen engagement with international financial institutions and business communities in host countries.

The efforts are aimed at strengthening the role of economic diplomacy, supporting the state’s efforts to attract investment and increase exports, and opening new markets for Egyptian products.

World.title: FM, Sudanese finance minister discuss reconstruction efforts
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty held talks on Sunday, August 23, 2026, with Sudanese Finance and Economic Planning Minister Gibril Ibrahim to discuss ways aimed at to expanding economic cooperation and supporting reconstruction efforts in Sudan.

The Ministers discussed cooperation between Egyptian and Sudanese institutions on financial policies, as well as measures to increase trade and investment and remove obstacles affecting bilateral commerce.

Talks also addressed cooperation on rehabilitating Sudan’s infrastructure, particularly roads and transport, as well as the medical and pharmaceutical sectors.

Abdelatty said that Egypt’s experience and capabilities in these fields could contribute to Sudan’s early recovery and reconstruction.

The Egyptian Foreign Minister also briefed Ibrahim on preparations for the first Africa Business Summit, to be held as part of the Alamein Forum for Business in Africa.

He encouraged Sudanese participation, saying the event could provide opportunities for greater economic and investment cooperation between the two countries.

The meeting also addressed developments in Sudan. Abdelatty reiterated Egypt’s support for Sudan’s unity, sovereignty, territorial integrity and national institutions, while rejecting attempts to divide the country or establish parallel entities.

He called for a Sudanese-led political settlement that preserves the country’s resources and meets the Sudanese people’s aspirations for security and stability.

World.title: Egypt Finance Minister: Global investors regain confidence in economy
World.content:
Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk on Sunday, August 23, 2026, said global investors have renewed their confidence in Egypt’s economic trajectory, with investment risk assessments falling to their lowest level since 2014.

“Our economy has started to improve, while the private sector is growing and accounts for 60% of investments,” Kouchouk said at a meeting with Egyptian diplomats abroad.

He said strong activity in industry, telecommunications, information technology and tourism was supporting economic growth, while the government was working to stimulate investment, reduce debt and expand tax and customs incentives.

Kouchouk said Egypt was seeking to expand its productive, industrial and export base to improve the economy’s competitiveness and attract more investment.

“Global investors have renewed their confidence in Egypt’s economic trajectory, and we look to your efforts to drive investment inflows,” he said.

He added that Egypt has significant potential to increase services exports, while its young workforce is capable of competing in global markets.

World.title: US, Egypt discuss port infrastructure, maritime innovation
World.content:
US and Egyptian officials opened the US-Egypt Ports Infrastructure and Maritime Innovation Forum in New Cairo on Sunday, August 23, 2026, to discuss port development, maritime technology, artificial intelligence and investment opportunities.

US Embassy Chargé d’Affaires Robert Silverman and US Deputy Secretary of Commerce Mark Mitchell opened the forum, while Egypt’s Transport Minister Kamel el Wazir addressed the event.

The US Embassy said that American companies presented advanced technologies that could support Egypt’s port infrastructure and artificial intelligence sectors while creating new opportunities for trade and investment between the two countries.

Silverman said the United States supports Egypt’s efforts to build world-class maritime infrastructure and that American companies are well positioned to compete for new projects and expand bilateral commercial ties.

Mitchell said Egypt occupies an important position in global trade and technology. He said US-Egypt cooperation could support the modernization of maritime transport, the development of the Suez Canal corridor, and the deployment of advanced US artificial intelligence and data infrastructure technologies.

The forum also connected American companies with opportunities in Egypt’s maritime, logistics, data and cloud computing sectors.

Egyptian participants included Suez Canal Economic Zone Chairman Mostafa Sheikhon, North Sinai Governor Khaled Megawer and Deputy Transport Minister for Maritime Transport Nihad Shahin.

The US is seeking to expand bilateral trade and private-sector investment through cooperation with Egypt on maritime infrastructure and technology.

World.title: Jak grać w zakłady sportowe, żeby wygrać z kobietą?
World.content:
Jak grać w zakłady sportowe, żeby wygrać z kobietą?

Zakłady sportowe to nie tylko sposób na emocjonujące przeżycia, ale także szansa na wygraną, zwłaszcza gdy skupisz się na strategii, która pozwoli Ci wyprzedzić konkurencję, w tym również kobiety. Aby skutecznie grać w zakłady sportowe i osiągnąć przewagę, warto poznać tajniki analizy oraz psychologii zakładów. W tym artykule przedstawimy kilka kluczowych wskazówek, które pomogą Ci w zwiększeniu swoich szans na sukces.

1. Zrozumienie zasad gry

Przed rozpoczęciem przygody z zakładami sportowymi należy dokładnie zrozumieć zasady, którymi się rządzą. Wiedza na temat rodzajów zakładów, jak również terminologii używanej w sportach, które Cię interesują, jest niezbędna. Zapoznanie się z tymi informacjami pomoże Ci podejmować lepsze decyzje na każdym etapie.

Rodzaje zakładów: zakłady proste, akumulatory, zakłady typu live.

Kursy: jak je interpretować i co oznaczają w kontekście ryzyka i potencjalnych zysków?

Wiedza o sportach: aktualizuj informacje o drużynach, zawodnikach oraz ich osiągnięciach.

2. Analiza statystyk i formy drużyny

Wszystkie zakłady sportowe powinny być oparte na solidnych danych i analizach. Osoby, które śledzą wyniki drużyn i statystyki, mają znacznie większe szanse na trafne przewidywania. Przed obstawieniem warto wybrać się w poszukiwaniu informacji na temat formy zawodników oraz wyników ostatnich meczów.

Najważniejsze kryteria analizy to:

Ostatnie wyniki drużyny. Forma zawodników (czy są kontuzjowani, jak prezentowali się w poprzednich meczach). Styl gry przeciwnej drużyny oraz ich taktyka.

3. Czynniki psychologiczne a strategia obstawiania

Psychologia gra dużą rolę w zakładach sportowych. Wiedza o tym, jak myślą inni gracze, w tym kobiety, może dać Ci przewagę. Gdy pojawia się presja, wielu graczy podejmuje nieprzemyślane decyzje, co może prowadzić do błędów.

Warto znać kilka psychologicznych strategii:

Współczucie – zrozumienie perspektywy przeciwnika może pomóc w ocenie ich wyborów.

Przeciwdziałanie emocjom – unikaj podejmowania decyzji na podstawie impulsów.

Analiza ryzyka – wiedz, kiedy lepiej odpuścić zakład lub postawić na pewny wynik.

4. Ustalanie budżetu na zakłady

Jednym z kluczowych elementów skutecznego obstawiania jest wyznaczenie budżetu. Wiedząc, ile możesz zaryzykować, unikniesz niekontrolowanego wydawania pieniędzy na zakłady. Dobry plan budżetowy pomoże Ci nie tylko w zachowaniu zdrowego podejścia, ale także w długoterminowym planowaniu mostbet.

Trzy zasady dotyczące ustalania budżetu:

Ustal miesięczny limit, którego nie przekroczysz. Nie obstawiaj pieniędzy, których nie możesz sobie pozwolić stracić. Monitoruj swoje zakłady oraz analizuj wyniki finansowe regularnie.

5. Strategia obstawiania i eksperymentowanie

Nie ma jednego sposobu na wygrywanie w zakładach sportowych. Kluczem jest stworzenie własnej strategii, która będzie dostosowana do Twojego stylu gry. Eksperymentowanie z różnymi metodami oraz analiza ich skuteczności pomoże Ci wyciągnąć wnioski i dostosować podejście w przyszłości.

Warto rozważyć:

Obstawianie różnych sportów, aby odkryć, w czym czujesz się pewniej.

Zmiany typów zakładów, np. z prostych na akumulatory w zależności od danego meczu.

Refleksja nad swoimi sukcesami i porażkami oraz uczenie się na ich podstawie.

Podsumowanie

Gra w zakłady sportowe może być zarówno emocjonująca, jak i korzystna finansowo, jeśli podejdziesz do niej z odpowiednią strategią. Zrozumienie reguł, analiza statystyk, uwzględnienie czynników psychologicznych, ustalenie budżetu oraz rozwijanie własnych strategii obstawiania to klucz do sukcesu. Pamiętaj, że obstawianie to nie tylko szansa na wygraną, ale także zabawa i emocje związane ze sportem!

FAQ

1. Jakie są najlepsze sporty do obstawiania?

Najlepsze sporty do obstawiania to piłka nożna, koszykówka, tenis oraz hokej, gdyż posiadają wiele statystyk i dostępnych informacji do analizy.

2. Czy istnieją strategie, które zapewniają wygraną w zakładach?

Niestety, nie ma stuprocentowych strategii, ale dobrze przemyślane analizy i odpowiednie podejście mogą znacząco zwiększyć szanse na sukces.

3. Czy mogę obstawiać na żywo?

Tak, wiele platform oferuje opcję zakładów na żywo, co daje możliwość reagowania na wydarzenia w czasie rzeczywistym.

4. Jakie są największe błędy w zakładach sportowych?

Nieprzemyślane decyzje emocjonalne, brak analizy statystyk oraz przekraczanie swojego budżetu to najczęstsze błędy, które popełniają gracze.

5. Jakie narzędzia mogą mi pomóc w analizie zakładów?

Warto korzystać z narzędzi online do analizy statystyk, prognoz oraz platform do zakładów, które oferują szczegółowe informacje na temat drużyn i zawodników.
