World.title: Watch as Camera Thieves Impact Wildlife Studies in Costa Rica
World.content:
Certain things are guaranteed when camera trapping in Costa Rica. Some things are magnificent, for instance, with enough time and even the smallest patch of forest, you’re going to record an ocelot. Other things are downright infuriating, for example, with enough time, working in just about any forest in Costa Rica, your camera trap is going to get stolen.

I haven’t kept track, because some statistics are too heartbreaking to tally, but I must have had over thirty cameras stolen over the last eight years or so. Theft is simply something that needs to be factored into any wildlife monitoring project using camera traps and its effects are manyfold. First, and for me most devastating, is the loss of data. If I sit and think about the content of the SD cards on all my stolen cameras, a single tear begins to form in the corner of my eye.

Then there’s the loss of the equipment, the associated cost, and the difficulty in acquiring replacement gear. Each of my cameras, with the support, batteries, and SD card, runs about $200. This may surprise you, but I’m not exactly racking in millions of dollars with my wildlife monitoring business, so each time I find an empty spot on a tree instead of a camera, my wallet takes a significant hit. Replacing the camera is no walk in the park.

I can’t go to my friendly camera trap salesman down the street. The cameras I require aren’t sold in Costa Rica. I rely on trips to the US and visitors for my camera replacements and that doesn’t always go perfectly smoothly (My mom was once briefly detained at the airport with 17 cameras in her suitcase. Sorry Mom!).

So, who’s stealing my cameras? Surprisingly, it’s probably people who I have a lot in common with. It’s mostly dudes who love being out in the wild. The trick is, these dudes aren’t recording videos of wildlife or hiking around taking in the natural beauty of Costa Rica, they’re poaching. It’s important that I use the word poaching instead of hunting.

In many cases, I have no problem with hunting. Well managed hunting can be an important conservation tool, but the folks in charge of these types of decisions in Costa Rica decided that a ban on hunting would have the best impact on the conservation of the country’s varied habitats. That is why any hunting that’s happening here is illegal. Thus, any poacher who notices that he’s being recorded by one of my cameras is going to have a strong motivation to hide his activities by stealing the camera. Plus, I’m sure they could make a few bucks by selling them.

I do all sorts of things to combat camera theft during my wildlife monitoring projects. The most obvious is that I avoid putting cameras where poachers will pass by. Unfortunately, these guys like to travel on trails, dry streambeds, and along the sides of rivers, and these are all fantastic places to record wildlife.

I also modify my equipment to make it less steal-able. I mostly use cameras that do not have any visible light at night, because a lot of poaching happens at night and a glowing camera is easily spotted and stolen. To make the cameras more difficult to see during the day, I’ve taken to wrapping them in camouflage.

I have several methods of doing this, but I generally wrap camo fabric around the cameras in a way that breaks up their boxy silhouette and helps them to blend in. While I do believe that the camo fabric does make the cameras harder to spot by human beings, it has the unfortunate side effect of attracting curious wildlife. Many species have decided to give the fabric a hard tug, resulting in cameras being dislodged, recording the sky or the ground for weeks instead of the area I was interested in monitoring.

In the end, no matter what precautions I take, camera thieves are going to continue to participate in my wildlife projects. I suppose the only thing I can do is accept it, say ‘Pura Vida’, and smile at the downstream effects of my attempts to hide my cameras, i.e. videos of wildlife pulling on the camo fabric and spinning my cameras all over the place.

About the Author

Vincent Losasso, founder of Guanacaste Wildlife Monitoring, is a biologist who works with camera traps throughout Costa Rica.

World.title: Fewer Humpback Whale Sightings Reported in Costa Rica’s Golfo Dulce
World.content:
Tour guides in Costa Rica’s Golfo Dulce say humpback whales have been more difficult to find this season, raising questions about whether warmer ocean water is changing their normal movements. Guides have said August usually brings regular whale sightings inside the gulf but this year, however, this year they have experienced days when dozens of tour boats searched the area but very few whales were seen.

On one recent morning, guides said that only one of approximately 30 to 40 boats reported seeing a whale. The observations do not prove that Costa Rica has fewer humpback whales this year but there has been no official population count showing a decline. The whales may simply be spending more time outside Golfo Dulce or moving between different parts of the southern Pacific coast.

Still, guides with years of experience say the change has been noticeable. Captains and guides, who has worked in the area for more than 12 years, said the whales previously remained inside the gulf for longer periods. This season, they appear to leave the protected waters more frequently and stay outside for longer.

The guides believe warmer ocean water could be influencing that behavior. They say they have personally noticed higher water temperatures while swimming and snorkeling. Some have also reported seeing coral with signs of partial or complete bleaching, which can occur when the ocean becomes unusually warm.

Golfo Dulce is one of Costa Rica’s most important whale-watching destinations and humpback whales from the Southern Hemisphere travel thousands of kilometers from waters near Antarctica to Costa Rica’s warm Pacific coast. The whales come north to mate, give birth and care for their calves before beginning the long journey back toward their feeding grounds. The southern whale season normally runs from July through October, with sightings often reaching their highest point during September.

Conditions inside Golfo Dulce are usually well suited for mothers and young calves. It’s warm, relatively calm water gives the animals a protected place during the first weeks of a calf’s life. Scientists have found evidence that water temperature and food availability can affect when humpback whales begin migrating.

A study published in 2025 followed 42 humpback whales traveling from breeding areas in Costa Rica, Panama and Ecuador toward feeding grounds near Antarctica. The researchers found that the whales used information from their surroundings, including water temperature and the amount of marine life in the water, to help decide when to leave.

Warmer water and El Niño conditions were connected with changes in the timing of their southward migration. The research suggests that humpbacks can adjust their movements when ocean conditions change. However, that study used tracking information collected between 2009 and 2016. It does not establish that warmer water is responsible for the sightings reported by Golfo Dulce guides in 2026.

Confirming such a connection would require current water-temperature measurements, whale counts and comparisons with previous seasons. For local tourism businesses, fewer sightings can create a difficult situation. Whale watching supports boat operators, guides, hotels, restaurants and other businesses across the Osa Peninsula and southern Puntarenas.

Guides sometimes remain at sea longer than usual while searching for whales because they know that visitors may have traveled a considerable distance for the experience. But sightings are never guaranteed, even during the busiest part of the season. Visitors can still encounter dolphins, sea turtles and other marine wildlife in Golfo Dulce. Tours in the area also commonly include snorkeling, mangrove visits and trips along the coast.

The guides’ reports offer an early warning worth examining, rather than proof of a permanent decline. Continued monitoring will be needed to determine whether this is an unusual season or part of a larger change in humpback whale migration.

World.title: Motorcyclist Jaime Catalan killed in Cayo collision; second rider detained
World.content:
Motorcyclist Jaime Catalan killed in Cayo collision; second rider detained

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have detained a man in connection with a motorcycle collision that claimed the life of 46-year-old Jaime Haroldo Catalan of San Marcos Village.

The crash occurred shortly before midnight on Friday, August 21, between Duck Run 1 and Billy White Village in the Cayo District.

Catalan was found unresponsive on the roadway with grave injuries. Police also found his damaged motorcycle and a second motorcycle with minor damage.

Investigators believe Catalan was travelling toward Billy White when 26-year-old Javier Pinelo of Bullet Tree Village overtook him. According to preliminary information, Pinelo encountered oncoming traffic and swerved back in front of Catalan, leading Catalan’s motorcycle to collide with the rear of Pinelo’s motorcycle.

Pinelo was also injured and taken to the San Ignacio Community Hospital. Police obtained a specimen from him, detained him under police guard and issued a Notice of Intended Prosecution.

Investigations continue.

World.title: Police review Crime Fusion footage after Christopher Smith found shot dead on Arlington Drive
World.content:
Police review Crime Fusion footage after Christopher Smith found shot dead on Arlington Drive

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating the murder of 23-year-old Christopher Smith, whose body was discovered in a yard on Arlington Drive in Belize City on Sunday morning.

According to police, the body was reported at around 7:00 a.m. on August 23. Investigators found Smith unresponsive with apparent gunshot injuries and recovered several expended shell casings from the scene.

Police believe Smith may have been shot at around 1:20 that morning, when reports were received of gunfire in the area. Officers who responded at that time, however, were unable to establish a crime scene.

Investigators have since retrieved surveillance footage through the Police Department’s Crime Fusion Center, and police say that footage has provided leads which are now being pursued.

No motive has been established.

Police also confirmed that Smith was known to them. He had previously been charged in connection with the 2024 double murder of Belmopan taxi drivers Marvin Cante and Juan Carlos Raymundo, whose bodies were found in a shallow grave near Hattieville. Importantly, however, the murder charge against Smith was withdrawn on November 28, 2025, on instructions from the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

World.title: Sherman Hemmans, Alberto Arreaza charged in armed home invasion and theft of 2026 Wingle pickup
World.content:
Sherman Hemmans, Alberto Arreaza charged in armed home invasion and theft of 2026 Wingle pickup

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have charged two men with aggravated burglary following an armed home invasion in which a resident was reportedly robbed of a 2026 Wingle pickup truck.

Twenty-nine-year-old Sheffan Hemmans, described by police as a post guard officer, and 26-year-old Alberto Arreaza, a Cayo District labourer, have been jointly charged.

Police say the complainant reported that at around 7:45 p.m. on Thursday, two masked men entered his home, one armed with a firearm, and demanded the keys to his black 2026 Wingle pickup.

Fearing for his safety, the victim complied and the men drove away with the vehicle.

Police activated operational procedures and, at around 9:45 p.m., officers in the Santa Rosa area of western Belize intercepted the stolen pickup.

Police also observed another vehicle in the area which sped away. Officers pursued that vehicle and eventually intercepted it. Hemmans was reportedly found aboard.

A search of Hemmans allegedly led to the discovery of 50 live rounds of .22 LR ammunition.

In addition to the aggravated burglary charge, Hemmans was charged with keeping ammunition without a gun licence.

World.title: Three charged after San Pedro raid turns up cannabis, cocaine and crack
World.content:
Three charged after San Pedro raid turns up cannabis, cocaine and crack

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Three San Pedro residents have been jointly charged with drug trafficking following a police raid in the Boca del Rio area.

Police say an operation was conducted at a residence on August 21 and resulted in the discovery of 1,312 grams of suspected cannabis, 21 grams of suspected cocaine and 28 grams of suspected crack cocaine.

Police subsequently arrested and jointly charged three people, including 26-year-old Horace Anthony Crawford and 24-year-old Bridget Alcer, along with another 26-year-old San Pedro resident.

The trio each face three counts of possession of controlled drugs with intent to supply to another.

World.title: High-speed SUV stop leads police to loaded 9mm; Lloyd Parchue charged
World.content:
High-speed SUV stop leads police to loaded 9mm; Lloyd Parchue charged

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A Belize City man has been charged with firearm and ammunition offences after police say a high-speed SUV caught the attention of officers conducting an anti-crime operation.

Police say GI3 personnel were operating in the St. Martin’s area at around 3:40 a.m. when they observed an SUV travelling at high speed.

Officers pursued and intercepted the vehicle.

A subsequent search allegedly led to the discovery of a 9mm Smith & Wesson pistol containing a magazine loaded with eight live rounds of ammunition.

Police formally arrested and charged 33-year-old Lloyd Parchue of Croton Lane, Belize City, with keeping a firearm without a gun licence and keeping ammunition without a gun licence.

World.title: Three Belize City men charged after armed robbery caught on camera at Independence Village store
World.content:
Three Belize City men charged after armed robbery caught on camera at Independence Village store

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have charged three Belize City men following an armed robbery at a store in Independence Village over the weekend, which was caught on camera.

The robbery occurred at approximately 2:30 p.m. on Saturday, August 22.

Police say two men entered the establishment, one armed with a firearm, and made demands of the store owner. The robbers took several items belonging to the proprietor before fleeing.

Information on the suspected perpetrators was circulated to police formations, and officers later intercepted a vehicle reportedly connected to the robbery.

Three men were found aboard and subsequently detained.

Police identified two of the accused as Dorian Garnett, 36, and Krishna Flores, 35, and Anthony Smith.

All three have been jointly charged with robbery.

Police said the suspects are persons known to authorities in connection with activities in the Belize District, but investigators have not established that they regularly operated in southern Belize.

World.title: Meth Heads in Belize? San Pedro man charged after police find 932 grams of suspected crystal meth
World.content:
Meth Heads in Belize? San Pedro man charged after police find 932 grams of suspected crystal meth

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 24-year-old San Pedro resident has been charged with drug trafficking after police say they found almost a kilogram of suspected crystal methamphetamine in his backpack.

Police formally arrested and charged Marcos Tun of San Pedro Town with possession of controlled drugs with intent to supply to another.

According to police, Special Branch and GI3 personnel conducted an anti-drug operation on August 18 during which Tun was searched.

Officers reportedly found a manila envelope inside his backpack containing suspected crystal methamphetamine.

The substance was weighed in Tun’s presence and amounted to 932 grams, police said.

Tun was subsequently formally arrested and charged.

World.title: Ladyville man charged after police find pistol loaded with 14 rounds
World.content:
Ladyville man charged after police find pistol loaded with 14 rounds

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have arrested and charged 30-year-old Anderson Martinez after officers allegedly discovered a pistol and ammunition during a search of his residence.

Police say the search was conducted on Sunday, August 23, and resulted in the discovery of a black Remington pistol.

A magazine containing 14 rounds of 9mm ammunition was reportedly found with the weapon.

Martinez was subsequently charged with keeping a firearm without a gun licence and keeping ammunition without a gun licence.

World.title: Honorary consul to Atlanta Elaine Grant-Bryan ‘humbled’ by OD recognition
World.content:
Elaine Grant-Bryan

When Elaine Grant-Bryan settled in Atlanta in 1990, that city was long acknowledged as the mecca of black empowerment in the United States. She joined a growing Jamaican community which has made an impact in commerce and community politics.

Grant-Bryan has been Jamaica’s honorary consul to Atlanta since 2018. Currently in her third term, she has been awarded the Order of Distinction (Officer class) by the Jamaican government for service to the diaspora.

That award will be presented during the National Honours and Awards ceremony on October 19 at King’s House in Kingston.

In an interview with Observer Online, Grant-Bryan spoke of being “deeply humbled” by recognition of her work. Like New York City and South Florida, she said Jamaicans have made their mark in Atlanta and neighbouring areas such as Decatur and Stone Mountain.

“This region has grown significantly, especially after COVID-19 as Jamaicans moved from colder regions in the United States in great numbers. Our community has doubled, and many have successfully assimilated in the Georgia culture and made significant contributions to Jamaica and this region,” Grant-Bryan stated.

An educator and real estate broker, she points to initiatives started with her husband Gregory as major achievements of her tenure. These include the Elaine Bryan Foundation which drives the Jamaican Pioneer Programme and STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, Mathematics).

The pioneer programme allows Americans of Jamaican heritage to gain citizenship in their family’s homeland. Once that is secured, they increase their contribution to Jamaica’s education system by mentoring and assisting needy students.

STEAM is an enrichment curriculum she developed with her husband, a programmer and Information Technology expert. It teaches coding/programming and offers career assessments, internships, entrepreneurships, and scholarships to Jamaican students completing degrees in STEAM fields.

Empowerment was a buzz word in Elaine Bryan’s home in Kingston, where she was born to a father who was an engineer and her mother, a nurse. A past student of Excelsior and Kingston Technical high schools, she was head girl at the latter.

Staying true to her profession, education is the thrust of upcoming projects by the Elaine Bryan Foundation.

“We will continue to include additional students who are completing degrees in the STEAM fields in Jamaica. The projection for 2026-7 is to extend mentorship programmes in Jamaica, study abroad and exchange programmes,” she disclosed.

World.title: ‘Long overdue’
World.content:
Minister of National Security and Deputy Prime Minister Dr Horace Chang and Minister of Culture, Gender, Entertainment and Sport Olivia Grange are all smiles as they receive the keys to the third Government-run shelter for women facing domestic abuse. (Photo: JIS)

LOCAL gender advocates have welcomed news that work has been completed on a third shelter for victims of domestic abuse.

Minister with responsibility for gender affairs Olivia Grange made the announcement last Friday as she toured the facility at an undisclosed location.

“We made a commitment that we would establish three centres, safe spaces for women, and we have achieved that,” said Grange as she pointed out that prior to the Dr Andrew Holness-led Administration there were no State-run shelters for women wishing to leave violent relationships.

In the last few years the Government completed, and is operating, two shelters for women. Grange said the addition of the third shelter will enable the ministry to offer up to 70 safe spaces for women and their children.

Grange said the completion of this third shelter, which is scheduled to begin providing a safe space for women after September 1, enables the Government to provide much-needed services to vulnerable females across the entire island.

“The completion of this space advances the gender agenda, because what we have been able to do now is to provide the spaces across the island, and we are now better equipped that when we get the call we are able to activate the kind of network that is necessary to move [women in abusive situations] into safe spaces,” said Grange.

On Sunday, gender and development practitioner Judith Wedderburn told the Jamaica Observer that the new shelter was long overdue.

“It is certainly very welcome because, not only from my experience but from the reports of women who do suffer, they have been beaten by a male partner and have experienced gender-based violence. The data does show us that it’s not getting better. More and more reports are coming out that it is happening,” said Wedderburn

According to Wedderburn, she became aware of plans to construct the new shelter through discussions with officials of the Bureau of Gender Affairs, however she was uncertain of the completion time.

“I am acknowledging that I have been in meetings in the last couple months where it was reported by somebody from the bureau that a third shelter was going to be built in a different part of the island, outside of Kingston. My understanding was it was going to serve the western part of the island,” said Wedderburn.

Pointing to a recent article published by the Jamaica Gleaner headlined, ‘The cop who finally listened’, Wedderburn said the presence of another shelter in the country serves as a call to action.

“Two women who recounted years of fear after ending abusive relationships are grateful to a corporal for standing with them. What it said was the woman who had been so badly abused was paying tribute to the only policeman who took her report seriously, the only policeman that supported her. And if you reflect on not just this article but other reports, on many occasions, unfortunately, a woman will not gather up the strength to go to a police station to report the incident,” Wedderburn argued.

Welcoming the initiative Joy Crawford, co-founder and executive director of female support group Eve for Life, told the Observer that the move strengthens the national response to gender-based violence (GBV) and expands access to safety for women and children leaving abusive situations.

“We recommend convening a robust, national GBV shelter working group comprising Government, NGOs, community-based organisations and other stakeholders to improve coordination, effectiveness, and accountability across the shelter system. This should include deliberate efforts to strengthen and expand non-government shelter models, recognising that Government cannot do this alone,” said Crawford.

She told the Observer that the country needs more diverse, accessible safe spaces across the island for survivors with different needs, including women with children, women with complex needs, adolescents, and other vulnerable groups.

“NGOs and community organisations play vital roles in victim identification, referral, psychosocial support, and sustained engagement. Formal referral pathways and partnerships can help survivors access appropriate services and safe accommodation earlier,” added Crawford.

For advocacy officer at Jamaica Coalition for a Healthy Society Philippa Davies, the provision of a third shelter by the Government is a commendable initiative but it is unfortunate that the problem of GBV exists.

“It is always better that society encourages, teaches, and supports healthy, safe relationships between men and women. As such, the family is the fundamental foundational institution of any society. The very real need for such places is evidence of family pathology, which is often passed on through generations,” said Davies.

She argued that the Government needs to establish a Ministry of the Family to address the critical role of the family and the need to prioritise its welfare.

“This would include strongly encouraging women and men to exercise discernment when choosing romantic and life partners, and to seek wise advice before and when challenges arise. It is scientifically established that the brain hormones released during sex bonds partners to the point of overshadowing danger signals such as the potential for or the occurrence of abuse,” added Davies who argued that the Government should also consider providing support for men who may be victims of abuse.

In announcing the completion of the new facility Grange said the Government-run shelters not only provide safety but also provide a therapeutic environment for women to rebuild their lives.

“We not only ensure that we protect them, but we help them to gain skills where they don’t have skills, we provide counselling, we have adequate space that we can facilitate a family — mother and children,” said Grange.

She revealed that during the last few years, one shelter hosted a mother and five of her children, while another mother gave birth while residing at another shelter.

Meanwhile, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Security and Peace Dr Horace Chang, acting in his capacity as chairman of the Citizens Business Group — a Government team that is mandated to manage social interventions across the country — said the establishment of Government-run shelters for women has been a big part of a programme to seek to impact, in a positive way, a number of vulnerable communities in Jamaica and, in particular in this case, women who have suffered abuse.

Chang noted that in the past few years the ministry has established domestic violence intervention centres at selected police stations as part of the strategy to eliminate domestic violence.

World.title: People and culture give Ja tourism edge, says Tortuga Resorts CEO
World.content:
Member of Parliament for St James East Central, Tourism Minister Edmund Bartlett (front row, third right), members of his East Central Education Fund team, and chief executive officer of Tortuga Resorts Leonardo Schlesinger (front row, right), stand with recipients of the constituency’s 2026 tertiary awards at the Montego Bay Convention Centre last Thursday. Horace Hines

MONTEGO BAY, St James — Leo Schlesinger, chief executive officer of Tortuga Resorts which recently acquired Hyatt Hotels’ interest in Playa Hotels & Resorts brand, says Jamaica’s greatest competitive tourism advantage is its culture and people — which no other destination can reproduce.

“Many countries have beautiful beaches. Anyone can copy a beach [but] nobody can copy Jamaican culture — that is Jamaica’s true competitive advantage,” Schlesinger told the St James East Central Scholarship and Welfare Fund’s annual tertiary awards at Montego Bay Convention Centre last Thursday.

According to Schlesinger, the warmth, energy, music, food, humour and authenticity associated with Jamaica give the island a distinctive appeal in the global tourism marketplace.

“Guests may forget the room they stayed in [but] they never forget how Jamaicans make them feel,” declared Schlesinger.

He said the value of that cultural advantage extends well beyond tourism branding as culture has become an important economic asset for Jamaica.

“When tourism is 30 per cent of the economy, culture is, in a very real sense, one-third of the Jamaican economy.

“Culture is not just heritage; it is a tool for the future. We often talk about culture as something to preserve. In Jamaica’s case, we should also think of culture as something we use to create the future,” added Schlesinger.

Tortuga Resorts has expanded its footprint in Jamaica through the acquisition of the former Playa properties — including Secrets, Breathless, Hyatt Ziva, Hyatt Zilara and Dreams resorts — and Schlesinger said the company plans to maintain its focus on the Jamaican market.

“We are deeply invested in Jamaica, and we intend to keep investing in the country,” said Schlesinger.

He argued that tourism’s economic impact reaches far beyond hotels, with visitors generating opportunities for airport workers, taxi operators, hotel employees, farmers, fishermen, construction workers, retailers, musicians, and other service providers.

The Tortuga Resorts CEO warned, however, that Jamaica’s ability to sustain its competitive advantage would ultimately depend on the quality of its human capital.

“The countries that succeed will not necessarily be the ones with the most resources. They will be the ones with the best educated, most adaptable, and most innovative people,” he said.

Schlesinger said while Jamaica faces significant challenges — including climate change, hurricanes, labour constraints, immigration, and infrastructure gaps — its people remain its most valuable resource.

“If you invest in a person in their education, skill, confidence, and creativity, the person grows,” he said. “Knowledge grows when it’s shared. Skills grow when they’re practised. Ideas grow when people collaborate,”

He called on universities to move beyond simply preparing students for employment and underscored that tertiary institutions have an equally important responsibility to develop critical thinkers and responsible citizens who will question, analyse, distinguish fact from opinion, listen to ideas they disagree with, and think independently.

“A healthy democracy does not just need educated professionals, it needs educated citizens,” he added.

For his part, Member of Parliament for St James East Central, Tourism Minister Edmund Bartlett said he wants his contribution to education and human capital development to be his enduring legacy.

Bartlett revealed that 60 tertiary students from the constituency received scholarships from his education programme, valued at just under $10 million this year.

He said the scholarship programme — which began 47 years ago at the start of his political life in St Andrew Eastern and has continued for the past 30 years in St James East Central — reflects his long-standing commitment to education as a vehicle for social mobility and national development.

“If I should be asked, ‘What is it that you would really like to be remembered by 100 years from now?’ — and somebody wants to remember this fat-faced fellow from Westmoreland — I would want to be remembered as the person who made a difference in the lives of the people in this country,” Bartlett said.

“And I would like to be remembered as the one who recognised that education was the surest way for social mobility and human advancement,” added Bartlett.

World.title: Burger Gully residents welcome MP’s relocation plan
World.content:
Residents who live closest to the banks of the gully in the community known as Burger Gully are the ones Member of Parliament Philip Paulwell wants to relocate.x

SEVERAL residents of the flood-prone east Kingston community of Burger Gully have welcomed the announcement from Member of Parliament for Kingston Eastern and Port Royal Phillip Paulwell that close to 150 of them will be relocated.

Paulwell made the disclosure during his address at his annual constituency conference at Vauxhall High School just over one week ago.

“I am willing to relocate; a lot of people are willing too. We really want to see it happen. We a feel it, man. As high as the windows them be, water goes through them. All the stoves and fridge you seeing here, a wash them wash out a people house,” said one female resident as she pointed to several flood-damaged appliances.

“This has been happening for more than 40 years. I have been living here for 38 years and it has been flooding since then,” added the woman who noted that many persons are forced to start over when their homes are flooded during heavy rain.

Her sentiments were echoed by Alton Giscombe, a shopkeeper in the area.

“When it floods, the water comes straight into the shop; I have to place my goods on top of crates. Two a me fridge them mash up,” said Giscombe.

“I am comfortable with relocating because I wouldn’t want for the gully to be flooded again and it flood out my things them,” Giscombe added.

For Frank Smith, another resident, while he appreciates the initiative, he would rather the gully walls be adjusted to prevent the frequent flooding.

“They could have raised the gully a little higher and everybody could be happy. If they carry the gully wall another four feet or five feet high I think we would be happy because the water would just go down,” said Smith, who added that he recently learnt about the relocation initiative.

According to Smith, when the gully overflows its banks the water enters his house and destroys everything.

“Over the years I have been flooded out like six times. You have a time water come here and it don’t trouble me but when the gully bursts, it floods my home.

“Even right now my car is there. When I came out of my house the last time [the gully] burst, it flooded the car. It destroyed my transmission, seat, and engine — everything full of water,” Smith said, pointing to an abandoned car along the side of the gully.

For Hyacinth — who has lived in Burger Gully for 54 years — even though she is not directly affected by the flood waters, the initiative is welcomed.

“The last time the gully come dung it barely came into my house, [and] it did not destroy my stuff. But if it is safer and the community that we will be living in is okay, I will go,” said Hyacinth even as she underscored that she will miss her current community if she relocates.

The flooding of Burger Gully, an informal settlement also called 17 1/2 Mountain View Avenue, has been an ongoing problem but worsened last year as sections of the gully which runs through the community were damaged by flood waters.

According to Paulwell, the Government has already allocated $30 million to repair the gully, with work expected to be completed by next month.

He told the Observer that lands have been identified in the communities of Mountain View and Rockfort for the relocation of Burger Gully residents, but he is awaiting a response from minister with responsibility for works Robert Morgan.

“I have identified three different parcels of land in and around the community. It is for the ministry now to come and do the proper surveying of the land,” Paulwell said.

World.title: Voice House expands
World.content:
Some of the 50 students selected from across the island for the free Singing Summer Intensive hosted by Tessanne Chin Foundation rehearse an item in preparation for the programme’s final showcase on August 23 at Louise Bennett Garden Theatre.

Singer and recording artiste Tessanne Chin, through her charitable foundation, just hosted over 50 talented children — her largest cohort to date — for a 4th annual Summer Singing Intensive training camp.

The programme’s signature end of camp showcase — this year titled Out of the Box — got underway on Sunday, August 23, at Louise Bennett Garden Theatre (Ranny Williams Centre).

The group was coached by Chin and a team of highly qualified performance instructors, among them Evad Campbell, Lori Burnett, Diana Sancho, Victoria Taffe, and Kelly Barrett.

This year’s edition also marks a major milestone for one of Jamaica’s most prominent singers who has plans to expand her year-round performing arts academy, called The Voice House, at a newly dedicated home now located in Liguanea, St Andrew.

She also pointed out that the dynamic performance ensemble associated with the programme will also now be known as The Voice House.

“It has always been my dream is to create a space where children can develop their voices and their confidence all year long. Through The Voice House we will offer comprehensive training in singing, voice acting, stagecraft, and performance development, giving young talent a structured pathway to grow their skills throughout the year,” shared Chin.

“Over the past three years we have been successfully hosting an after-school programme and our kids have been consistently engaged for several corporate and entertainment events, demonstrating the high-calibre output that we are delivering. We see so much potential to deliver so much more under our expanded programme,” she further highlighted.

Looking ahead, Chin and her team are laying the groundwork to establish a talent agency for children, creating a safe, structured avenue for young performers to access auditions, bookings, and industry opportunities both locally and internationally.

“Our new home has and will continue to allow us to give them the kind of consistent, world-class training that builds not just performers, but empowered young people,” she added.

Chin’s vision is being strengthened by the support of some of Jamaica’s most influential artistes, including Sean Paul, who this year has generously offered scholarships to help children access the year-round programme and pursue higher education in the performing arts.

She also noted the kind contributions of this year’s sponsors Tastee, Supreme Ventures, Sagicor, Sandals Foundation, CHASE Fund, Digicel Foundation, Lasco, GraceKennedy Group, Loshusan, and Wisynco.

She also expressed gratitude for her production partners and Jamaica Cultural Development Commission (JCDC) for their involvement in making the programme a success.

World.title: ‘JUST HAVING FUN’
World.content:
Oblique Seville (foreground) celebrates winning the men’s 100m event at the Silesia Diamond League athletics meeting in Katowice, Poland, on Sunday. Photo: AFP

World Champion Oblique Seville says his men’s 100m victory at the Wanda Diamond League meeting in Silesia, Poland, on Sunday, sets him up well for the remainder of the season.

The Jamaican ran a meet record 9.83 seconds (1.4m/s) during the Kamila Skolimowska Memorial, effectively securing his place in the Diamond League final set for Brussells, Belgium, in two weeks.

Kenny Bednarek ran a season’s best 9.87 for second and fellow American Christian Coleman was third in 9.93. Jamaican Ackeem Blake ran 10.26 in his first-round race and failed to advance.

Seville, 25, said he is also eyeing success at the first-ever Ultimate Championships set for Budapest, Hungary, in mid-September.

“I am in pretty good shape and I feel pretty good about the win. I am in great shape for the Ultimate Championships. The victory feels nice — especially as I ran close to my personal best — and I am just having fun,” he said.

After placing second at the London Diamond League last month, he qualified for Sunday’s final after running 9.90 (1.9m/s) in the preliminaries. He then broke the meet record of 9.87 that was held jointly by three men, including compatriot Kishane Thompson.

“There are great things ahead of me,” Seville said. “Many sprinters ran under 10s, that is really special. For the rest of the season I would like to keep winning, and the next win should be in Brussels.”

Brianna Lyston was the best-placed Jamaican in the women’s 100m, placing fourth in 10.96(0.6m/s). The race was won by American Melissa Jefferson-Wooden, who maintained her unbeaten run all year with a season’s best-equalling 10.78. Jefferson-Wooden defeated St Lucia’s Olympic Games champion Julien Alfred who ran a season’s best 10.83. Another American, Sha’Carri Richardson, placed third in 10.96.

Tina Clayton, who had a good start, faded to sixth place with 11.01, while her twin sister Tia was ninth with 11.24.

Megan Simmonds was second in the 100m hurdles, running 12.62 (0.2m/s) behind American Alaysha Johnson who won in 12.52. Poland’s Pia Skrzyszowska placed third with 12.64.

Ackera Nugent, who raced in Finland four days prior, was fourth with 12.64, while two-time world champion Danielle Williams was fifth in 12.70.

Nickisha Pryce ran a season’s best 49.49 for second in the women’s 400m as world champion Marileidy Paulino of the Dominican Republic clocked 48.87 to win for the fifth-straight time on the Diamond League circuit.

Salwa Eid Naser of Bahrain finished third with a season’s best 49.57 while Stacey Ann Williams was sixth with 49.81.

Three days after he competed at the Diamond League in Lausanne, Switzerland, Orlando Bennett was fifth in the 110m hurdles in 13.25 (-0.7m/s).

American Ja’Kobe Tharp, who had finished at the back of the race in Switzerland, rebounded to win with 13.05 in a clean sweep of the top three places for Americans. Trey Cunningham was second with 13.08, just ahead of Jamal Britt (13.09),

Rajindra Campbell was sixth in the men’s shot put with 21.61m as Italy’s world leader Leonardo Fabbri won in dramatic fashion, coming from fourth place with 22.08m in fourth round.

Early leader Jordan Geist of the United States was second with 21.96m while his country man Joe Kovacs was third with 21.86m.

Olympic Games champion Roje Stona was sixth in the men’s discus throw with 67.65m while national champion Ralford Mullings threw a season’s best 66.44m for seventh after starting with two fouled efforts.

Mykolas Alekna of Lithuania set a Diamond League and meet record 72.58m to beat Kristjan Ceh (68.93m) of Slovakia and Daniel Stahl (68.25m) of Sweden.

Alekna broke his own own Diamond League record of 71.70m set in London last year and the meet record 68.60m set by Germany’s Robert Harting in 2013.

Commonwealth Games medallist Ackelia Smith finished eighth in the women’s triple jump with 13.97m (-0.7m/s) as Saly Sarr won with a Senegalese national record 15.08m (0.2m/s). Sarr defeated the Cuban pair of Leyanis Perez Hernandez, who recorded 14.91m (-0.2m/s), and Davisleydi Velazco, who jumped 14.84m (1.2m/s).

Lamara Distin was ninth in the women’s high jump, clearing 1.89m. Yaroslava Mahuchikh of Ukraine equalled the meet record of 2.00m to win. Mahuchikh topped her compatriot Iryna Geraschenko (1.98m), with Australia’s Commonwealth Games champion Eleanor Patterson (1.98).

World.title: How Dis Mek: RIVER RAFTS
World.content:
Visitors to the island boarding a raft at the start of the Rafting on the Martha Brae tour. (Photos: Gavin Jones)

RIVER rafting is one of Jamaica’s popular vacation activities for locals and visitors alike but have you ever considered the mechanics behind the making of the rafts?

Claude Johnson, raft captain #102 at Rafting on the Martha Brae, explained to the Jamaica Observer’s How Dis Mek the process behind the making of rafts during an interview on the banks of the Martha Brae river in the hills of Trelawny, where dozens of his coworkers’ rafts were docked.

Bamboo, Johnson explained, is ideal for raft creation because each joint on a stalk is essentially an air-filled sealed vacuum, allowing the stalks to float extremely well.

“The reason why we choose bamboo is because it’s air-packed, so as the joints don’t burst, everything is okay. The bamboo can take [withstand] up to a thousand [pounds] on it. You see the more length you have, the more weight you can take on top of it. You can build it 28 feet, 29 feet — those lengths are the good lengths,” said Johnson.

He explained that even if some of the bamboo joints pop open, due to age or sun damage, as long as the others remain sealed the integrity of the raft is maintained.

The use of rafts in Trelawny is well documented. Initially, rafts were used to ferry goods from rural Trelawny to the parish capital of Falmouth. Recreational rafting began in the 1970s under the Jamaica Tourist Board and has been operated by River Raft Limited since 1985.

Raft captains must be fully trained and certified before they can operate, with lessons in controlling the raft and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) certification compulsory.

Once licensed, the captains are responsible for the creation of their own rafts. To create the raft, captains need what they refer to as a “dozen stalks of bamboo”.

“If you don’t have any and you can’t go into the field to cut it, you have some people cut it and sell it for $10,000 for a dozen, [but] when we say dozen we mean 14 bamboo to make a raft,” Johnson explained.

Then to move forward, captains need a partner, because raft building is a two-person job.

Working alongside Richardo Geinues, Captain #114, Johnson demonstrated that the stalks must first be cut to the same length, placed exactly next to each other, and bound tightly to create a flat surface.

Captains use ratcheting straps to tightly bind the stalks and prevent any chance of movement. Before the binding, the stalks are pierced at one end, at the same spot, to allow for a stick to be threaded through them and bound with metal wire and pliers.

The tension from the metal wire keeps the stalks together, forming the flat bed of the raft. Then another stalk is cut into five pieces and threaded in a similar manner on top of the raft.

World.title: Absentee dad got married, now wants custody
World.content:
DEAR MRS MACAULAY, My daughter migrated and my grand-daughter, who is nine, has lived with me and my husband for almost three years. Her father rarely visited, but got married recently and suddenly wants full custody. The child barely knows him. Do we have any legal standing to prevent this?

From your very concise letter, I cannot say whether your daughter had applied for and obtained a legal order of custody, care and control of her child. I deduce that your grandchild lived with her mother, your daughter, for the first six years of life, until she migrated. I also conclude that your daughter left her child in yours and your husband’s care when she migrated, thus making you both the guardians of her child. I assume that this was not done by a deed, but by word of mouth and the physical handing over of the child to you.

You have also not stated the details of your daughter’s request. Was it until she made an application and obtained the necessary visa for her daughter to join her abroad, or was it until the child attains majority? And also, was the “father” pursuant to the Registration (Births and Deaths) Act, registered as the father of the child? Or was he so declared by an order of a court?

It seems that all arrangements were done with the absence and non-intervention of your grandchild’s putative father. You also make no mention of whether he ever provided any maintenance for the child during the years the child has been with you and your husband, or while with your daughter. All these are pertinent questions as to his status, which the court ought to consider on his application for legal custody, whether full or joint, with you and/or the mother of the child.

It seems to me that you have concluded that because your daughter is abroad, she cannot intervene in any application made by the father, or file an application herself for legal custody (which she should have done before her departure and during the years of the non-interest or non-involvement of the putative father). But matters in the Family Court or the Supreme Court can be heard by video conferences/

Zoom when a party is abroad (or in Jamaica but unable to attend personally). There is therefore no reason why your daughter cannot act herself or join with you to intervene in any action by the father.

The question you want answered is whether you and your husband as grandparents can intervene in the court to stop the presumed father from obtaining a legal custody order. By the way, I know of instances like this when such fathers get police officers to accompany them to “collect” their children, and these officers insist that the father has the legal right to the child. But in such circumstances, the officer should advise the father to go and apply for custody in the Family Court, and the application must be served on the person with whom the child is residing. It is for the court to decide and make any order for the custody, care and control of a child who has not had any relationship with his/her presumed father. A police officer is not a judge or jury in any legal matter.

If this happens, do not accede to any pressures of a police officer. Rather, call the station and speak with the officer in charge and report what is happening. Such matters where the father has been absent from the life of his purported child for years must be decided by in a court of law and not a police officer.

Your position raises several issues of facts and law which need to be considered and determined by the court in the circumstances you have sparsely related. The court, pursuant to the Children (Guardianship and Custody) Act, has a discretion, when a child was allowed to be brought up by another person (you and your husband), and where a father abandoned or deserted the child, to make an order that is not averse to the best interests and welfare of the child.

It is my opinion that you and your husband could act both as the guardians of the child and grandparents who were made the guardians by your daughter who had full custody of the child while the father showed hardly any interest in the child. I am also assuming that your grandchild is still with you, and you refused to just hand the child over to this father, because you and your husband are the child’s guardians appointed by the mother who had full custody and care and control.

So you can intervene as the

de facto guardians and apply to be so declared, and for full legal custody of the child, with the consent of your daughter, evidenced in an affidavit sworn to by her. These applications must be made in the Supreme Court.

I must advise you, however, to retain an attorney-at-law to represent yours, your daughter’s, and your grandchild’s interests by preparing and filing the necessary applications and affidavits in support in the Supreme Court or Family Court of your parish, whichever is relevant. If the father has applied, file your defence as quickly as possible. Remember, your daughter can also be a party to the application.

It is such a pity that your daughter, like so many others, made these important decisions which direct the lives of so many children without first seeking and obtaining legal advice. Legal consultation and advice protect the rights and lives of so many, and ultimately save anguish, worry and money.

Your lawyer can also add that an access order be made to enable the father to have specific access periods with the child, so that a relationship can develop between them as the law intends, and also to ensure that the rights of the child are recognised, respected and upheld.

So please act as quickly as you can to obtain the services of a lawyer to act for you all in this very important matter.

All the very best.

Margarette May Macaulay is an attorney-at-law, Supreme Court mediator, notary public, and women’s and children’s rights advocate. Send questions via e-mail to allwoman@jamaicaobserver.com. All responses are published. Mrs Macaulay cannot provide personal responses.

World.title: Saudi Arabia to invest €6B in massive French theme park site
World.content:
This article is also available in: French

The massive project is being built on the former site of Mirapolis, a massive theme park that has been shuttered since 1991. | Patrick Hertzog/AFP via Getty Images

PARIS — Saudi Arabia will spend €6 billion to build a massive entertainment complex boasting three theme parks near Paris, French President Emmanuel Macron said.

Macron and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman signed an agreement formalizing the deal to build what the French leader called “a new global destination” at the Elysée Palace on Monday. It is expected to create 22,000 jobs, Macron said.

The massive project, which Macron said will also include hotels, catering facilities and housing for young workers and students, is being built on the former site of Mirapolis, a massive theme park that has been shuttered since 1991. Among the parks being built is one centered around manga, as POLITICO reported earlier this month.

World.title: Mirapolis : l’Elysée et l’Arabie saoudite officialisent un investissement à six milliards
World.content:
Le démarrage du chantier, situé à Courdimanche (Val-d’Oise), n'a pas encore de date officielle. | Patrick Hertzog/AFP via Getty Images

Trois parcs d’attractions vont sortir de terre sur le site de l’ancien parc à thème de Mirapolis.

PARIS — Mirapolis, c’est désormais signé. Près d’un mois après les révélations de POLITICO sur le projet de résurrection de l’ancien parc d’attractions du Val-d'Oise grâce à des capitaux saoudiens, l’Elysée et Riyad ont signé lundi un accord actant ce méga-investissement, lors de la visite à Paris du prince héritier Mohammed ben Salmane.

L’investissement prévisionnel s’élève à 6 milliards d’euros et prévoit la création de 22 000 emplois, selon les éléments communiqués par l’Elysée à l’issue de la cérémonie de signature. Il comprend le développement de trois parcs à thème et de loisirs, accompagnés de services d’hébergement et de restauration, ainsi que la construction de logements, notamment destinés aux jeunes actifs et aux étudiants.

“Une annonce hors normes (...) du jamais vu depuis Disneyland Paris”, s’est réjoui Emmanuel Macron sur X.

World.title: Burnham ups the ante in fight against Russia — and leaves Merz in the shade
World.content:
The trip gave Burnham his first chance to show his commitment to the Coalition of the Willing — a grouping of Ukraine’s allies championed by his predecessor, Keir Starmer — as he co-chaired its latest meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron.

Burnham was allowed to enjoy the limelight as the only E3 leader to attend the session in person, with Macron hosting Saudi Arabia’s Mohammed bin Salman and Merz attending to a domestic crisis.

Sitting alongside Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Burnham said Russian threats against the U.K. will not deter him and show British assistance is having an impact.

The British PM said: “It’s clear Russia is running out of options so Putin is now hoping he can win through a campaign of terror using ballistic missiles against Ukrainian civilians.”

The new agreement on missiles is unlikely to have any short-term impact on Russia’s war against Ukraine, but represents a gradual shift in the U.K.’s posture towards deeper cooperation with Kyiv and sharper confrontation with Moscow.

Burnham has also signed a deal allowing the U.K. to access Ukraine’s Avengers AI lab, allowing both sides to collaborate on the development of new battlefield technology, using sensors and cameras to capture and collate information on objects such as tanks, artillery, air defense systems and drone targets.

World.title: Spain’s Sánchez calls national security meeting 26 days into Ceuta migration crisis
World.content:
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez will convene the country’s National Security Council on Tuesday over the migration crisis in Ceuta — 26 days after tens of thousands of people crossed from Morocco and overwhelmed local authorities.

Sánchez held two online meetings with ministers on Aug. 7 and 17 to coordinate Spain’s response to the crisis in Ceuta. But this is the first time he’s called for an emergency meeting of his National Security Council, which includes part of his cabinet alongside defense and intelligence leaders. The meeting will begin at 8:30 a.m. in Madrid’s Moncloa Palace, El País reported.

The prime minister had been under pressure to convene the body for weeks. Earlier this month, left-wing Izquierda Unida leader Antonio Maíllo called the meeting “essential” and urged Sánchez to rethink Spain’s relationship with Morocco. “First, holidays. Then, national security,” said Cuca Gamarra, a lawmaker for the center-right People’s Party, after Monday’s announcement.

World.title: Ukraine faces €23B defense funding hole as Western cash lags
World.content:
U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham was in Kyiv Monday for a meeting of the so-called coalition of the willing.

European Council President António Costa, Luxembourgish Prime Minister Luc Frieden, Moldovan President Maia Sandu, Estonian President Alar Karis, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and other Nordic and Baltic leaders also attended in person, while French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz joined remotely.

“Ukrainian people deserve not just continued support but our gratitude ... I am determined we [the coalition of the willing] will work together to deliver the support you need,” Burnham said in a statement.

The funding gap originated after the defense ministry brought forward spending originally planned for the second half of the year, while the EU’s €90 billion loan was delayed by roadblocks from Hungary.

“At the beginning of the year, decisions were made at the ministry to use in the first half of the year funds that were intended to be disbursed in the second half," Zelenskyy said during a meeting with reporters on Saturday. The shortfall comes on top of €30 billion in funding Europe has already pledged to Ukraine this year as part of the €90 billion loan.

Purchases made included "fiber-optic drones, middle-strike drones, interceptors,” former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov told POLITICO in June.

World.title: Far-left firebrand Mélenchon gaining ground in French presidential race, poll shows
World.content:
The National Rally leader has long been the favorite to win, and Mélenchon’s rise raises the risk of a runoff between two candidates who hold deeply skeptical views of the EU and NATO.

In one scenario tested, which includes three candidates from the political center, the France Unbowed leader would receive 16 percent of the vote ahead of former prime ministers Édouard Philippe on 14 percent, and Gabriel Attal on 8 percent. Le Pen came in well ahead of all of them with 35 percent.

Without Attal in the contest, the poll found Mélenchon and Philippe would be tied for second place at 17 percent each. Moderates have for weeks voiced concern that the field is too crowded and risks ceding the election to the political extremes.

“I’ve been warning for months of the likelihood of a face-off between Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon,” said government spokesperson Maud Bregeon, who is supporting Philippe’s candidacy. “The likelihood of this risk has increased, unsurprisingly.”

World.title: Star news anchor steps down as her partner launches French presidential bid
World.content:
Léa Salamé is seen ahead of the evening news broadcast in Paris on Oct. 7, 2025. | Stephane de Sakutin/AFP via Getty Images

Journalist Léa Salamé said she will temporarily step down from her role anchoring French public television’s primetime news broadcast, the 20h, while her romantic partner, the MEP Raphaël Glucksmann, runs for the French presidency.

“The 20h is a strategic platform where interviews with the candidates and campaign reports will be among the highlights of the coming year,” Salamé said in an Instagram post on Monday announcing her decision. “Wherever the campaign takes place, I’ll step aside. Everywhere else, I am and will remain a journalist.”

Since taking her seat in the anchor’s chair of the 20h on France TV, Salamé has faced questions over the potential conflict of interest if Glucksmann, who has long signaled his presidential ambitions, were to join the race to replace Emmanuel Macron next year. Glucksmann announced his candidacy Sunday on TF1, France TV’s main competitor when it comes to the evening news.

World.title: Tornado in Aude: at least 26 injured and around 100 homes damaged
World.content:
According to the prefecture of the département of Aude, the tornado struck late on Monday afternoon, at 5.20 pm, in particular in Pomas, a village of around 1,000 inhabitants located between Carcassonne and Limoux.

 

Numerous videos posted on social media show a powerful vortex of wind moving through several communes in the département under stormy skies.

The prefecture of Aude is now reporting "26 people with non-life-threatening injuries, who have been treated and passed through the casualty assembly point, including five people evacuated to a hospital." Among them is a pregnant woman, injured when her house collapsed but protected by her sofa.

Damage to property is extensive. Around a hundred homes have been affected in Pomas, with many roofs ripped off and houses blown apart.

More than 115 firefighters have been deployed, including 14 urban search and rescue specialists, accompanied by a dog-handling team. The Red Cross is also due to reinforce the operation.

To accommodate residents who cannot return to their homes, two emergency shelters have been opened for the night, in Pomas and Limoux.

The gendarmes, for their part, are to carry out regular patrols in the affected areas to secure damaged properties.

The severe weather has also disrupted traffic. Several departmental roads have been closed after trees fell and to allow the emergency services to intervene.

At 7.30 pm, 2,800 households in around ten communes in Aude were still without electricity.

The tornado struck as parts of south-west France were under an orange alert. Météo France recorded wind gusts of up to 117 km/h. The orange alert was lifted at 7 pm.

World.title: US Treasury Secretary launches 'Operation Economic Outcast' aimed at isolating Iran
World.content:
The United States is launching what it has branded "Operation Economic Outcast" against Iran as Washington seeks to sever Tehran's financial lifelines amid the ongoing war.

 

In a press conference on Monday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent outlined a new, "unprecedented campaign" against Iran and its "enablers," describing it as an "economic onslaught" aimed at isolating the Iranian regime.

"Treasury has mapped every node, every facilitator, and every network that Iran has used to smuggle oil and evade sanctions," he said. "Beginning today, the actions of Treasury and other agencies will tighten the noose and block every potential source of revenue that funds the IRGC and the evil Iranian regime".

"Any entity that facilitates money laundering on behalf of Iran will be removed from the US dollar system," he continued, adding that US President Donald Trump was contacting unspecified world leaders requesting that they stop working with Iran.

As part of the campaign, the Treasury Department announced on Monday that it had also "issued determinations against five critical sectors - digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping - that the Iranian regime uses to try to prop up its failing economy."

Moving forward, Bessent said Iran was now left with "a very clear choice."

"Complete global isolation and a subsistence economy, or a path back to normalcy, with an opportunity to rejoin the global economy".

A small boat sails past cargo ships and other commercial vessels anchored in the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas, Iran, Wednesday, Aug. 5, 2026. Amirhosein Khorgooi/ISNA via AP

Bessent's warning comes around six months after US and Israeli strikes on Iran marked the beginning of the war in the region, which the Trump administration says aims to ensure Iran can never obtain a nuclear weapon.

The conflict has largely ground to a stalemate in recent months, with negotiations faltering and a growing dispute over the Strait of Hormuz.

The strategic waterway, a crucial oil and gas transit chokepoint that connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea, has been a sticking point in talks between Washington and Tehran, with both sides claiming control over the passage.
