World.title: Iraq, Qatar provide oil for loading inside Hormuz via bids
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Trade sources reported on Monday that Iraq’s national oil marketer, SOMO, and QatarEnergy are presenting crude oil through unusual bids that mandate purchasers to load cargoes within the Strait of Hormuz.

SOMO announced that it is offering Basrah Medium and Basrah Heavy crude for loading in September from either the Basrah oil port or a single point mooring, along with the necessary supporting facilities, as reported by Reuters.

QatarEnergy provided free-on-board oil loading at al-Shaheen, Qatar Marine, and Qatar Land ports in September and October.

Earlier, SOMO provided substantial discounts on Basrah crude in August to entice customers to load shipments from the Strait of Hormuz.

SOMO asked potential term purchasers to designate contractual volumes of Basrah Medium or Basrah Heavy crude for complimentary onboard delivery from the Basrah Oil Terminal or other port-related infrastructure.

Iraq’s oil marketer provided discounts ranging between $25 and $27 per barrel on Basrah Medium, according to the loading period. It provided discounts of $27.80 to $29.80 a barrel for Basrah Heavy.

Maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz decreased due to ongoing military operations in the region and heightened shipping security risks.

The significant price reduction aims to compensate for rising maritime insurance costs and freight expenses by transferring transit risk to purchasers.

World.title: Iraq to introduce new banknotes with three zeros removed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq intends to remove three zeros from its currency to modernize financial transactions, reduce physical cash circulation, and return stockpiled funds to the official banking system.

Under the suggestion, a 25,000-Iraqi dinar note would become 25 Iraqi dinars, but the currency’s purchasing power and true financial value would stay unaffected.

According to Jamal Kocher, a Kurdish member of the Iraqi parliament’s finance committee, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has asked for the removal of zeros from invoices.

Kocher told The New Region that if the plan is implemented, 1,000 Iraqi dinars would be converted to one dinar, while 25,000 dinars would be equivalent to 25 dinars.

Earlier in August, Communications Minister Mustafa Sanad acknowledged the plan to eliminate the zeros and modify the currency.

The redenomination strategy aims to bring undeclared cash, estimated to be between 8 and 10 trillion Iraqi dinars that are currently held outside banks, back into official channels. This initiative seeks to combat crime, corruption, and money laundering.

According to the idea, everyday prices, incomes, and savings will alter correspondingly, resulting in a direct mathematical shift rather than a change in actual wealth.

Iraq has sought printing partners in the United Kingdom and Australia, as well as its traditional suppliers in France and Germany, to create an estimated 7.5 billion new banknotes.

While government officials such as the Communications Minister and Finance Committee members have emphasized the importance of an official implementation date, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) has yet to present a formal draft bill to parliament.

World.title: Iraq to raise oil exports via Turkey’s Ceyhan to 750,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil announced on Sunday a proposal to increase oil exports through the Turkish port of Ceyhan to 750,000 barrels per day by using tanker trucks to transport crude oil from southern oilfields.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the plan includes increasing exports through southern ports.

Iraq and Turkey recently inked a one-year short-term deal to continue operations through the critical Iraq-Turkey oil pipeline.

The agreement, reached in Ankara following discussions between Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar and Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair, guarantees the ongoing transportation of at least 750,000 barrels of Iraqi crude oil per day to the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Turkey’s state-owned crude oil and natural gas pipeline corporation (BOTAS) signed an agreement with Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) and the North Oil Company (NOC).

The new deal is now valid for 12 months until both countries develop a new, long-term legislative framework.

The previous agreement, which was reached in 1973, officially expired on July 27.

The short extension of the deal is crucial for Iraq’s revenue from oil exports, as Baghdad seeks alternative export routes to mitigate risks linked to the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Eto’o urges support for embattled FIFA president Infantino
World.content:
Paris – Former Cameroon star Samuel Eto’o has thrown his support behind beleaguered FIFA president Gianni Infantino, saying he “hasn’t done anything wrong” despite facing mounting pressure to step down over a controversial World Cup sell-off plan.

Infantino has come under intense scrutiny since the collapse of a proposal to secure private investment in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup.

UEFA, which oversees European football, has threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions with several continental and national federations also withdrawing their support for Infantino.

However, Eto’o, president of the Cameroonian football federation, dismissed criticism of Infantino’s leadership, suggesting the backlash was driven largely by political manoeuvring ahead of FIFA’s presidential election next year.

“I don’t think that President Gianni Infantino has done anything wrong,” the former Barcelona, Inter Milan and Chelsea striker told CNN.

“I think the timing of all of that is because there’s an election coming out.”

Infantino’s plan, which would reportedly have distributed substantial funding to FIFA’s 211 member associations, faced strong opposition from several confederations and was ultimately abandoned.

The FIFA president remains under pressure, with the possibility of a no-confidence vote being triggered. UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF — which governs North and Central America and the Caribbean — have all voiced concerns over FIFA’s direction in recent weeks.

But the Confederation of African Football (CAF) earlier this month “unanimously reconfirmed its support” for Infantino, and Eto’o’s backing is aligned with that position.

“President Gianni Infantino has changed football,” said Eto’o, urging fellow African countries to support the Swiss official.

“He’s given opportunities to nations that didn’t have those opportunities to take part in the most beautiful tournament, the World Cup. He enabled smaller nations to get seats at these competitions.

“He has helped our continent. He’s helped our federations to develop much more quickly, and we need to acknowledge that. We need to accept and recognise what he’s done, and we should support him for everything he’s done up to now.”

World.title: Trump claims Iran ‘collapsing’ as US threatens ‘economic D-Day’
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump said Monday that Iran was “collapsing” as Washington prepared to announce the details of a new economic pressure campaign that Tehran has derided as an admission of defeat.

Almost six months into their war, the two sides are locked in a stalemate, with peace talks stalled, Iran keeping the key Strait of Hormuz shut and Washington persisting with a naval counter-blockade of Iran.

Under political pressure at home over the economic impacts of the conflict, Trump has pivoted away from military action to economic levers.

“IRAN IS COMPLETELY COLLAPSING!!!” the president posted Monday in his trademark all-caps style on his social media platform Truth Social.

His remarks came hours after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in a column for the Financial Times, declared that an “economic D-Day” had begun against Tehran and warned that any country that continued to enable the Islamic republic would become a “global pariah”.

Bessent also claimed on X that the US had “dismantled Iran’s military capabilities, destroyed nearly 100 percent of its military factories, and buried its nuclear programme”.

Iran responded with defiance, saying the latest US measures were an admission of military defeat, and it warned countries against aiding Washington.

Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi posted on X that the US turn to financial warfare proved Bessent’s claims false.

“Your narrative doesn’t add up,” Gharibabadi said, asking why, if Washington had achieved its goals, “there is a need for ‘the largest financial invasion in history’ and the mobilisation of ‘all institutions and powers’ of the United States!

“Is this a victory or an admission of America’s defeat?”

The US and Israel linked the launch of their war in February to Iran’s nuclear programme, but the focus since the early days of fighting has been on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital route for global oil and gas supplies.

Tehran continues to blockade the strait, which it did not restrict before the war, driving up global inflation and heaping domestic pressure on Trump ahead of mid-term elections in November.

– Oil exports plunge –

Bessent was due to set out details of the US plan on Monday, but it is unclear how much more economic pressure Washington can put on Tehran.

The US naval blockade of Iran has seen its oil exports via the Strait of Hormuz fall from two million barrels a day pre-war to just 0.4 million by mid-August, according to maritime tracker Kpler.

Meanwhile, the country has been under crushing international sanctions for decades, with a brief period of easing under a 2015 nuclear deal that Trump later ripped up as part of a “maximum pressure” campaign.

The Islamic republic has weathered those efforts and, before the war, continued to export millions of barrels of oil, mostly to China, and evade sanctions through complex international financial networks.

Bessent and Trump have both warned countries against helping Iran, signalling a shift in their focus, with the Treasury secretary’s FT column dwelling on nations who “appease” and “enable” Iran.

Tehran responded on Monday by warning countries not to cooperate with the US efforts. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said taking part would “definitely have its own consequences”.

For ordinary Iranians, the standoff is likely to bring only more economic pain after years of rampant inflation, which in December and January fuelled massive anti-government protests.

Sarah Hassanbeigi, a 32-year-old pharmacist in Tehran, put it simply: “It’s really very difficult. I don’t think people can really take this much longer.”

On Sunday, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian admitted that Iran faced “many problems in society”.

“We are striving with all our hearts to overcome inflation, livelihood problems, unemployment, and to secure the future of the people, so that they can live with dignity and pride,” Pezeshkian said.

– Delegation from Pakistan –

Last week, the Iranian president, considered a relative moderate, said Tehran should “bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity”.

That followed supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei appointing hardliners to key security positions.

Hassanbeigi said she wanted peace. “Naturally, negotiations mean that both sides have to compromise. My personal opinion is that Iran should compromise now,” she told AFP.

Throughout the war, diplomatic efforts, pushed on by mediators, have sought a negotiated end to the conflict.

On Monday, Pakistan’s army chief was expected in Iran. Islamabad was a leading mediator in talks that helped secure an April ceasefire that later fell apart.

Omani Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi was also due in Iran on Tuesday, as Muscat and Tehran seek a deal on regulating passage through Hormuz.

World.title: Liverpool must improve on ‘unacceptable’ season, says Van Dijk
World.content:
Liverpool – Virgil van Dijk said Liverpool “need to show a reaction” from a bitterly disappointing season that cost Arne Slot his job as manager, but called for patience with new boss Andoni Iraola.

The Reds needed a 99th-minute equaliser from the penalty spot by Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue a 2-2 draw at Newcastle on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

Slot guided Liverpool to glory and a 20th league title in his debut campaign in 2024/25, but paid the price for finishing fifth last season when he was dismissed in May.

Many of the same flaws were in evidence in Iraola’s first outing at St James’ Park as Newcastle sliced open the Liverpool defence on the counter-attack.

But they twice came from behind to avoid a losing start to the new season.

“It’s absolutely normal in any type of profession, work, whatever you do, if you come in new and you have new plans and new ideas, then it takes a bit of time with new players,” said Van Dijk.

“It’s down to us to do it as soon as we can, as soon as possible, because we want to improve, we want to win, we want to be better. That’s what we are going to try to do.

“We need to show a reaction from last year, that we are much better than last year, because this was very unacceptable.”

Iraola has not been aided by a lack of new arrivals in the transfer market.

Despite the departure of club legend Mohamed Salah and a long-term injury to Hugo Ekitike, Liverpool have only added Spanish winger Victor Munoz in attacking areas as well as defenders Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo.

Paris Saint-Germain’s two-time Champions League winner Bradley Barcola has been linked with a move to Anfield, while two bids for Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh have reportedly been turned down.

“Everyone wants to see quality arrive regardless and I fully trust the club and the board to make the right decisions,” Van Dijk added.

“That’s the only thing I can say, so let’s see what we are going to do.”

World.title: Iraq suggests a security council involving Iran, Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has officially suggested forming a joint security coordination council with Iran and Saudi Arabia to address what it calls a severe crisis of trust between the two regional powers.

The Security Affairs Adviser to the Prime Minister of Iraq, Qasim al-Araji, put forward the diplomatic initiative on behalf of Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government to stabilize the region where Iraq strives to manage its own turbulent security climate.

Baghdad clearly planned the initiative to reconcile serious tensions between Riyadh and Tehran.

Tensions rose as Saudi Arabia intercepted multiple drones aimed at its oil facilities and capital. Riyadh denounced Iran-backed militias that operate from inside Iraq.

The idea comes during a very unstable period, including recent US-Saudi joint airstrikes targeting Popular Mobilization Forces’ (PMF) sites in Iraq and leading to serious criticism from Baghdad for sovereignty violations.

Baghdad is also pressuring Tehran for waivers for oil tankers from Iran’s navigation restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

Additionally, al-Araji underlined Iraq’s transition to ultimate domestic sovereignty.

With the scheduled withdrawal of the US-led international coalition forces from Iraq, Baghdad is adopting a strategy to put all armed factions and weaponry under strict state supervision, consolidating the country’s ultimate authority over war and peace choices.

Neither Saudi Arabia nor Iran has released a formal public response to the Iraqi initiative.

World.title: Iraq foreign reserves decline 11.6% to $86.17B in June 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Official financial statements from the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) show that Iraq’s foreign exchange reserves declined to $86.175 billion at the end of June 2026, marking a decrease of $11.257 billion (-11.6%) compared to the $97.432 billion recorded at the close of 2025.

According to reserve records published on Monday, August 24, 2026, the contraction followed an early-year peak above $102 billion before downward momentum set in through the second quarter.

Monthly Reserve Trajectory (H1 2026)

End of 2025 Baseline: $97.432 billion

January 2026: $101.082 billion

February 2026 (Peak): $102.131 billion

March 2026: $100.341 billion

April 2026: $97.809 billion

May 2026: $93.673 billion

June 2026:$86.175 billion(Month-over-month drop of $7.498 billion)

The overall drop reduced the local currency value of the total portfolio from 126.661 trillion IQD at the end of 2025 to 112.027 trillion IQD by June 30, 2026—a net decline of 14.634 trillion IQD (-11.6%).

Reserve Component End of 2025 (IQD) End of June 2026 (IQD) Net Change Change (%) Investments & Securities 93.266 Trillion 81.998 Trillion -11.268 Trillion -12.1% Monetary Gold Reserves 31.488 Trillion 29.415 Trillion -2.073 Trillion -6.6% Cash Vault Holdings 1.907 Trillion 0.614 Trillion -1.293 Trillion -67.8% Total Equivalent Value 126.661 Trillion 112.027 Trillion -14.634 Trillion -11.6%

The reserve reduction aligns with broader fiscal pressures in the first half of 2026, during which lower oil revenues widened the state budget deficit and prompted the central bank to meet elevated domestic foreign currency demand.

While liquid investment instruments fell by 11.268 trillion IQD to absorb trade financing and foreign wire settlements, cash assets held in central bank vaults rebounded moderately in June (up to 614 billion IQD from 366 billion IQD in May), even as overall foreign exchange reserves adjusted downward to $86.175 billion.

World.content:
SC flags private access to sensitive PF, I-T data, asks Centre to prevent misuse by firms

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday expressed concern about a commercial technological ecosystem which allegedly accesses, retrieves and verifies sensitive individual information on provident fund and income tax returns and told the Centre about the desirability of devising an antidote to the problem with the assistance of domain experts.Hearing a PIL by Piyush Sharma, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana noted the matter essentially fell within policy domain but termed private access to sovereign data - individual information given to govt under legislative mandate - and its commercial exploitation as worrisome.Petitioner said his personal inquiry into the issue had revealed that "upon merely furnishing PAN and UAN details to a private verification workflow, the petitioner received complete employment history corresponding the said identifiers. No OTP authentication was generated. No explicit consent was obtained. No visible authorisation-based identity verification process was undertaken".Without blaming govt agencies for any leakage of data, the petitioner highlighted the insecure status of individual data given to govt under the mandate of different laws, as they are accessed at will by private entities."Despite the statutory architecture governing EPFO and I-T data, there appears to be an emerging and concerning pattern wherein private employment verification ecosystems rely upon data corresponding to statutory employment and financial records for purposes such as employment verification, moonlighting detection, dual employment screening, labour market profiling and employment decision-making," he said.SC agreed it was a serious matter but said it must be dealt with through a policy decision. On learning the petitioner sent two comprehensive representations on the issues to Centre, it asked govt to take "necessary steps to prevent misuse of individual data by private enterprises."

World.title: Mizoram's 'misogynistic' marriage, divorce law faces challenge in SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Entrepreneur and Congress functionary Meriam L Hrangchal Monday challenged the constitutional validity of Mizo Marriage, Divorce and Inheritance of Property Act, 2014, which was enacted by Congress govt headed by Lal Thanhawla, terming it "misogynistic and pro-Mizo men".

Hrangchal, daughter of former deputy CM Lalhmingthanga, told a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant that the law, which codified customary law, applied to any person belonging to a Mizo tribe and extended to marriages where the male member belonged to a Mizo tribe.

The 2014 Act denies Mizo women, who marry outside the Mizo community, access to a comprehensive community-specific statutory framework governing marriage, property and inheritance, thereby infringing their right to equality, dignity and personal liberty under Articles 14 and 21, she said.

The law marginalises the independent identity of Mizo women and refuses them the benefits under the 2014 Act which extends to marriage between a Mizo man and a non-Mizo woman but does not cover marriage between a Mizo woman and a non-Mizo man, she said, citing her own marital relationship.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"The effect of such provisions is that Mizo women who marry non-Mizo men, and the children born out of such marriages, are excluded from the statutory regime, notwithstanding their subsisting connection to the Mizo community," she said.





The bench said the issue raised in her petition was important but asked why she was bypassing the high court. Her counsel said the community being small, she feared for her safety if her petition was heard by the Aizawl bench of Gauhati HC.

The CJI-led bench understood her apprehension and requested the CJ of Gauhati HC to hear her petition in Guwahati without sending it to the Aizawl bench.

World.title: 22 million hectares of degraded land restored during 2011 and 2020
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India has restored nearly 22 million hectares of degraded and deforested land during the 2011-20 period as against its target of restoring 26 million hectares by 2030, said Union minister

at a UN conference Monday.

While addressing the 17th session (COP17) of the UNCCD conference in Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia, he also pitched for "diversified, adequate, predictable and sustained international finance" for land restoration and drought resilience, saying it is not a cost, but an investment in food, water, biodiversity, livelihood and long-term resilience.

Underlining how the country's restoration efforts had generated approximately 1.2 billion person-days of employment during the 2011-20 period, he said these figures demonstrated restoration could deliver both environmental and socio-economic outcomes by reviving degraded landscapes while creating employment and supporting rural livelihoods.

According to Indiaâs second progress report on its land restoration efforts, covering the period 2011â2020, Telangana restored the maximum (4.2 million hectares) degraded area followed by Madhya Pradesh (3.8 million ha), Odisha (2.6 million ha), Gujarat (1.7 million ha) and Andhra Pradesh (1.6 million ha) through afforestation, water resource management, sustainable farming practices, agroforestry, mangrove restoration and natural regeneration of formerly forested land.





Indiaâs Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas shows that 97.8 million ha of land, or nearly 29.8% of the countryâs geographical area, are affected by land degradation and desertification. Around 82% of Indiaâs degraded land falls in nine states/UT - Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Jammu & Kashmir, Karnataka, Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and Telangana.

World.title: SC to consider Tarun Tejpal's plea for exemption from surrender
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

Monday said it would pass order on former Tehelka editor

's plea seeking exemption from surrender after Bombay High Court convicted and sentenced him to 10 years of imprisonment in a 2013 rape case, with Goa govt opposing his plea and contending that his appeal was not admissible since the convict had not filed a separate application seeking exemption from surrender or shown a certificate that he has already surrendered as per Order XXII Rule 5 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013.

The matter was heard by a single judge, Justice Alok Aradhe. Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the state govt, contended that existence of the appeal was dependent on Tejpal either filing a certificate that he has surrendered or, alternatively, requesting the court to allow an exemption from surrender.

Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, representing Tejpal, said there was no need to surrender yet since the high court itself had granted him time to surrender.

"This rule doesn't apply because this is a case where stay has been granted by the high court, so there is no question of applying this rule. Suppose the court says no stay, I will have to go to jail," Sibal said, requesting the court to list the appeal for Aug 31.

After hearing both sides, Justice Aradhe said he would pass an appropriate order in the matter.

The Goa bench of Bombay high court convicted Tejpal under multiple provisions of the IPC and sentenced him to 10 years rigorous imprisonment each under sections 376(2)(f) and 376(2)(k), with the sentences to run concurrently. World.title: 3 Bambiha members deported from Malaysia
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a major operation against the Bambiha criminal network, Indian agencies have executed a coordinated crackdown on its key overseas operatives, deporting three of its members from Malaysia who were ordering hits and carrying out extortions in India on behalf of the group's kingpin Lucky Patial.

Announced by Union home minister Amit Shah on X Monday, the high-profile action targeted Jaspreet Singh (alias Jas Behbal) of Faridkot, alongside Ajay Singh (alias Ajay Malaysia) and Pawandeep Singh, both from Rajasthan's Sri Ganganagar district. Shah posted that Indian agencies had got the three absconding gangsters apprehended in Malaysia and deported to India.

"The fugitives....are linked to the Bambiha gang and are accused of multiple crimes, including extortion, cross-border arms and narco-trafficking, and a foiled grenade attack in Ludhiana...our agencies have facilitated the deportation of 51 hardened criminals in 2026 alone."

World.title: Abhishek Banerjee in SC for speedy order on rebel MPs
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Trinamool general secretary and Lok Sabha MP

has moved the Supreme Court seeking an expeditious decision by Speaker Om Birla on petitions seeking disqualification of the 20 rebel party MPs who have aligned themselves with Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI).

According to the SC website, a bench comprising CJI and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana has listed Banerjee's plea for hearing on Aug 25.

The petition challenges the delay in deciding on the disqualification proceedings against the rebel MPs. In the recently concluded Monsoon session, Banerjee had also met LS Speaker Om Birla on Aug 12 to reiterate his demand for a speedy decision.

World.title: Showcase India's strengths to woo tourists: PM Modi

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi on Monday asked young diplomats to showcase India's civilisational, cultural and geographical strengths to make it a more attractive global tourism destination.

Talking to officer trainees of the 2025 batch of Indian Foreign Service, he asked them to serve as catalytic agents for the country's economic engagement with the world.

World.title: In a first, Census 2027 will not record data on begging
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a departure from previous exercises, Census 2027 will not record data on begging separately, with the questionnaire having omitted the category 'beggars and vagrants etc' from the list of 'non-economic activity'.

This, as per sources, is due to the very less return in this category in the last census; just around 3.8 lakh non-workers and marginal workers declared themselves as 'beggars and vagrants' in Census 2011.

Another key change in is the inclusion of 'natural calamities' as a 'reason for migration', in addition to work, business, education, marriage, moved after birth, moved with household and 'any other'.

While the 2011 census and earlier had listed 'beggars and vagrants etc' as marginal and non-workers engaged in 'non-economic activity' - in addition to students, household duties, dependents, pensioners, rentiers and others - they will now be counted among 'others'; as a result, the number of beggars in the country or their classification by age, religion, state/UT, educational status etc will no longer figure in census tables.

Sources said the count of 'beggars and vagrants' returned by previous census exercises was not considered reliable, as many respondents in this category were reluctant to return themselves as such due to associated social stigma. "Census rules require the enumerator to record the occupation/non-economic activity as declared by the respondent," an officer said. The count of non-worker beggars/vagrants was thus recorded at around 3.8 lakh in Census 2011, 6.3 lakh in Census 2001 and around 5.4 lakh in Census 1991.





As for the new census fields 'father's particulars' and 'mother's particulars' - which will capture date and place of their birth as well as religion - sources said they need to be filled only where the mother and father are not listed in the same household or are no longer alive. The enumeration form already records the religion and date and place of birth of each member of the census household, including parents.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Sources told TOI that some of the trends that may emerge from recording religion of both parents include generation-wise prevalence of inter-faith marriages and history of religious conversion.

Also, date and place of birth of parents will give the aggregate data on how many Indians fulfil citizenship criteria as per Citizenship Act.

While the latest questionnaire seeks details like mobile number, Aadhaar, voter ID and Indian passport number, where "available", technically requiring every individual having these documents to share their number, sources said the enumerators have been trained to only persuade the respondents to do so, by assuring them that all individual data will remain confidential. If the respondent is still reluctant, the enumerator shall leave these fields empty.

"Even blank fields will enable the census team to cull out data on which of the documents - Aadhaar, voter ID and passport number - respondents are most reluctant to share due to privacy concerns," an official told TOI.

World.title: Stone quarries put Assam semiconductor plant at risk
World.content:
Dust-producing stone quarries and crushers in the vicinity could cripple Assam’s semiconductor unit, a signature pet project of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, before it can start, an environmental activist has warned.

Tata is developing the ₹27,000 crore Semiconductor Assembly and Test (TSAT) facility in Morigaon district’s Jagiroad, about 55 km east of Guwahati. It is a major component of India’s chip-making ambitions and is linked to the vision of building a self-reliant ecosystem under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM).

Over 60% of the work at the TSAT facility, coming up where a unit of the Hindustan Paper Corporation once stood, is complete.

According to the ISM guidelines, a semiconductor plant requires ISO Class 1 to 5 vibration-damped cleanrooms to prevent microscopic dust contamination, and millions of gallons of ultra-pure water daily for wafer-rising, chemical processing, and cooling.

However, stone quarries and crushers within a 5 k.m. radius of the facility have reportedly been covering the Jagiroad area with a blanket of dust. Local organisations said excavation and blasting carried out in the hills of Sonaikuchi Reserve Forest (near the semiconductor plant) have caused flash floods and threatened public health.

Raising concerns over the potential impact of dust and pollution on Assam’s flagship industrial project, Golaghat district-based environmental activist Rohit Choudhury urged the State government to enforce restrictions on polluting industries and activities within a 15-km radius of the TSAT facility.

In a letter to the Assam Chief Secretary on August 22, he cited an RTI (Right to Information) reply from the State’s Industries, Commerce, and Public Enterprise Department and an earlier government directive to argue that exemption granted to pre-existing and pipeline polluting industries could undermine the very objective of protecting the proposed Ratan Tata Electronic City at Jagiroad.

Cabinet decision

On March 10, the Assam Cabinet decided that no cement plants or other polluting industries would be permitted within a 15-km radius of the Electronic City. The Industries Department issued an order on May 2, directing officials to ensure strict compliance, scrutinise industrial proposals, and establish a monitoring mechanism to flag violations. The order said the restriction was “mandatory and binding”.

However, the Industries Department’s July 30 response to Mr Choudhury’s RTI application on June 26 revealed that the Cabinet subsequently clarified that the restriction would apply prospectively and would not apply to pre-existing or pipeline projects. It also directed officials to examine whether the restriction could be reduced from 15 km to 5 km by amending the relevant policy.

Mr Choudhury questioned the distinction between new and existing polluting activities, arguing that emissions and dust from either category could have the same consequences for the semiconductor facility.

“Stone mining, quarrying, and crushing are major sources of particulate matter (PM10, PM2.5, and TSP) and gaseous pollutants, which are incompatible with the stringent environmental requirements of semiconductor manufacturing. Allowing such activities near the facility will have catastrophic consequences for this nationally significant project,” he wrote.

He also referred to an April 20 order by the Divisional Forest Officer, Nagaon Division, cancelling operations in the “Jagiroad Stone Mining Area” of Sonaikuchi Reserve Forest. This indicated that the operating stone quarries were illegal.

At least two Jagiroad-based organisations have also protested the stone quarrying and crushing in the vicinity. On August 11, the local unit of the Bir Lachit Sena submitted a memorandum to Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, seeking immediate intervention against illegal hill excavation and blasting activities at Sonaikuchi.

The unit’s president, Arup Bora, urged the State government not to grant permission or allot land for quarrying around Jagiroad, citing the need to protect the environment and public health.

The Madhya Assam Koch-Rajbongshi Students’ Union submitted a similar petition to Assam Environment and Forest Minister Jayanta Mallabaruah on August 18, seeking action against illegal mining in Nagaon and Morigaon districts. The organisation also named a contractor involved in illegal mining at Jagiroad and in the hills of the adjoining Karbi Anglong and West Karbi Anglong districts.

World.title: U.S. removes Syria from state sponsor of terrorism list
World.content:
The United States on Monday (August 24, 2026) removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism, rescinding a decades-old designation that came with severe economic restrictions and marking another step in warming ties between the countries.

The U.S. Department of State also revoked its designation of al-Nusra Front — latterly known as Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) — as a global terrorist organisation. The Treasury Department announced corresponding sanctions relief.

Rebels led by HTS overthrew long-time Syrian ruler Bashar al-Assad in December 2024, with the group's leader, Ahmed al-Sharaa, taking over as president as the country rebuilds after more than 13 years of civil war.

"Today's action will help foster additional investment in Syria to promote political and economic stability," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement.

Treasury said the moves were "in line with President [Donald] Trump's promise to deliver sanctions relief to Syria."

But the agency stressed that its removal of restrictions on Syria "does not change Treasury's posture with regards to countering global terrorism and our commitment to hold bad actors in Syria accountable."

Warming ties

HTS was earlier known as al-Nusra Front and was formerly the branch of Al-Qaeda in Syria. It broke ties with the jihadist group in 2016.

Also Read | ​New beginning: On Syria’s present and future

The United States had initially announced in July its intent to delist Syria as a state sponsor of terrorism, a move seen as a vote of confidence in Sharaa.

Mr. Trump met on the sidelines of a NATO summit in Turkey with the Syrian President, a former jihadist who has sought to recast himself as a unifying figure after the toppling of the Assad family, which ruled with an iron fist for a half-century.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Monday's (August 24) delistings gave Syrians "a path to prosperity."

The action "eliminates the final major barriers for private sector investment in Syria and promotes Syria's economic recovery and reintegration into the global economy," he said in a statement.

Top officials in Damascus hailed the delisting as a major opportunity for the country, still economically devastated after more than a decade of war that rights groups say killed more than half a million people.

Syrian Foreign Minister Assad al-Shaibani described Washington's delisting as a "historic milestone" and said it reflected "the new Syrian state's commitment to international peace and security."

Finance Minister Mohammed Barnieh described the move as a "success for Syrian diplomacy," according to the official news agency SANA.

It "opens a major and long-awaited door to strengthening Syria's integration into the global economic and financial system, attracting investment and modern technologies, and supporting development opportunities."

Central bank chief Safwat Raslan lauded the development, adding that his institution was "working to build a modern and reliable financial system capable of evolving with developments and taking advantage of all opportunities."

World.title: Armed men ambush patrol in South Sudan, kill two UN peacekeepers
World.content:
Armed men ambushed a patrol travelling to a remote area of South Sudan on Monday (August 24, 2026), killing two UN peacekeepers, the United Nations Mission in South Sudan said. Though violence is rampant in the African country, attacks against peacekeepers are rare.

No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack. Seven others were wounded — three peacekeepers, two members of the South Sudanese police and two civilian staffers — the mission known as UNMISS said in a statement. The two peacekeepers killed and three injured were from Ethiopia, UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said.

The mission said it had deployed a “Quick Reaction Force” to secure the area and support the emergency response after the attack. The patrol was going to the area of Pajut in the state of Jonglei when it came under attack.

“Such deadly violence targeting UNMISS personnel who are serving to support peace in South Sudan is unacceptable,” Anita Kiki Gbeho, the head of UNMISS, said in the statement.

The killings bring the number of peacekeepers killed by militias since January 1 to 9, Dujarric said, stressing that attacks against UN peacekeepers may constitute war crimes under international law.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres condemned the ambush “in the strongest possible terms” and called for a prompt investigation that would lead to the prosecution of those responsible, Dujarric said later on Monday (August 24).

“The secretary-general reaffirms the United Nations' commitment to stand with the victims and their families during this profoundly difficult time,” the spokesman said.

Government troops in South Sudan have been combating fighters and militias loyal to opposition leader Riek Machar, who was suspended last year as vice president as he faces charges of treason and other offenses. Machar says the charges are politically motivated.

A 2018 peace deal between President Salva Kiir and Machar, who is under house arrest, has collapsed, leading to fears of a return to full-blown civil war.

Between January and July, more than 450 incidents of violence against humanitarian workers and assets were reported, more than double the number recorded during the same period last year, according to UN figures.

The conflict escalated in December when opposition forces seized government outposts in Jonglei. The government has been carrying out a counteroffensive since January, with aerial bombardments and ground assaults, despite an official commitment to the peace agreement.

The United States has urged for talks between Kiir and Machar. Earlier this year, it called for “urgent action to uphold peace and mitigate the risk of civil war through an immediate return to dialogue among the parties to the 2018 peace agreement.”

World.title: India-China talks: ‘Structural differences have not disappeared,’ says Hu Shisheng
World.content:
Ahead of talks in Beijing on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) between National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi, Hu Shisheng, a leading Chinese strategic affairs scholar on South Asia, said the focus of both countries would be on “institutionalising stability” even as “structural differences” in the relationship remained.

Also Read | Eyes on Xi visit, ‘early harvest’ as Doval heads to Beijing

India and China will on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) hold the 25th round of talks between the Special Representatives (SRs) on the boundary question. Mr. Doval and Mr. Wang, who is also a member of the Politburo, will also take stock of relations ahead of next month’s expected visit to India by Chinese President Xi Jinping for the BRICS Summit, his first visit in seven years.

“On the border, I would expect the immediate focus to be less on a dramatic settlement and more on institutionalising stability. The priority is to prevent misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC, strengthen military and diplomatic communication, and turn last year’s idea of an ‘early harvest’ into an operational process,” Mr. Hu, who is Director of the South Asia Institute at the China Institutes of Contemporary International Relations (CICIR) in Beijing, told The Hindu.

He was referring to an agreement at last year’s 24th round on establishing an Expert Group under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) on border affairs to explore “early harvest on boundary delimitation”.

“The two WMCC meetings this year have discussed delimitation, so there has been procedural progress, but there is still no public indication of a concrete sectoral delimitation agreement,” Mr. Hu said. “The realistic next step would be to operationalise the Expert Group, agree on its mandate, timetable and criteria for identifying relatively less contentious sectors, rather than expect an immediate breakthrough on the boundary itself.”

The broader challenge facing the two SRs, he said, was whether both sides “can work out a sustainable modus vivendi that avoids confrontation, keeps differences manageable, and preserves space for cooperation”.

Mr. Hu said the timing of Mr. Doval’s visit, before the September 12 BRICS Summit in New Delhi, added significance to the visit with Mr. Xi expected to visit India.

“Both sides have a strong incentive to keep the border stable and create a favourable political atmosphere for possible leader-level interaction,” he said, adding that he viewed maintaining stability on the border, achieving “concrete and operational progress” on “early harvest” outcomes, and creating favourable conditions for the BRICS Summit as immediate priorities for the border talks.

Also Read | China’s media slams India’s move of formally naming 27 places in Arunachal Pradesh

At the strategic level, he added, Mr. Doval’s visit would help “clear potential obstacles ahead of the BRICS Summit and lay the groundwork for possible leader-level engagement.” He said ensuring no unexpected border incident before the summit, setting the political tone and identifying deliverables for a possible leaders’ meeting, and coordinating the handover of the BRICS agenda from India to China, which takes over as chair next year, would be three essential issues on the table.

The view in Beijing, as in Delhi, is that the normalisation in relations since the October 2024 meeting between Mr. Modi and Mr. Xi is likely to remain gradual and measured.

“As for the broader normalisation, I would describe it as strategic risk management rather than strategic realignment,” Mr. Hu said. “Recent difficulties in India-U.S. relations may give New Delhi greater incentives to diversify its strategic options, while the relative stabilisation of China-U.S. ties reduces some of the external pressure on China-India relations. But the structural differences between China and India have not disappeared. What we are seeing is an attempt to build a more stable form of competitive coexistence – keeping the border peaceful, restoring practical cooperation, and expanding coordination through BRICS and the Global South without pretending that strategic competition no longer exists.”

World.title: Parents of 16-year-old Keralam boy who died in accident donate organs
World.content:
A 16-year-old boy from Alanallur in Palakkad district, who slipped into brain stem death while he was being treated for traumatic injuries following a road traffic accident, has become the saviour of three lives in the State.

P.H. Aadil, son of Shahul Hameed and Shiny and a Class XI student of Vettathoor Higher Secondary School, had been seriously injured when the two-wheeler on which he was riding along with a friend collided with a car at Mannarmala near Perinthalmanna on August 21.

Though he was first admitted to Maulana hospital in Perinthalmanna first and later shifted to Aster MIMS at Kozhikode, he suffered brain stem death by 9.48 p.m. on August 23.

After his parents expressed their wish to donate his organs, Kerala State Organ and Tissue Transplant Organization (K-SOTTO) stepped in and coordinated with other hospitals to find suitable recipients and arrange organ harvesting and transportation.

Aadil’s liver went to a patient at Aster MIMS, and his kidneys were received by patients at Kozhikode Government Medical College and Baby Memorial Hospital, Kozhikode.

He is survived by his parents and two sisters.

World.title: Canada will announce retaliatory tariffs against U.S. on August 25, official say
World.content:
Canada will announce retaliatory tariffs against the United States on Tuesday (August 25, 2026), an official familiar with the plans told The Associated Press, escalating a trade fight that has sharply worsened since negotiations with the Trump administration collapsed.

The official spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the plans publicly.

Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Monday (August 24, 2026) that Canada may need to move away from matching U.S. tariffs dollar for dollar and instead use more targeted retaliation aimed at protecting Canadian workers and businesses.

President Donald Trump escalated the dispute again on Monday (August 24, 2026), telling Canadian leaders to “fall in line” or face consequences “far WORSE” than tariffs already imposed and threatening new 50% tariffs on Canadian vehicles, auto parts and steel.

Mr. Carney accused Washington of trying to subordinate Canada and said U.S. trade demands had confirmed Canada's fears that the United States was seeking to dismantle major Canadian industries.

“An attitude at the negotiation table that Canada is a subsidiary of the United States” is “not something we're going to accept,” Mr. Carney said.

Mr. Carney was even more blunt in French.

“We learned during the negotiations that the Americans want to destroy our major industries, including autos, steel and aluminium,” Mr. Carney said. “That was one of the main reasons we said no. It was a bad deal.”

The fiery words from both sides show how U.S.-Canada relations have deteriorated since Mr. Carney walked away from trade negotiations with the Trump administration late Friday (August 21, 2026), triggering the President's threatened 50% tariffs the next day on about $20 billion worth of Canadian goods.

Carney cast doubt on the U.S.'s reliability as a partner, saying Canada was finding reliable partners “everywhere in the world, except in the United States. Except in the United States. And Russia.”

Trump unleashes personal attacks on Canadian leaders

Mr. Trump on Monday (August 24, 2026) came back with further tariffs, warning that he would impose them on Canada's auto industry beginning next year.

“Canada has been ripping off the United States of America for years,” Mr. Trump wrote on social media, criticising what he called the country's “ridiculously high tariffs” on American farmers.

Mr. Carney said Washington's auto-sector proposals would gradually have the effect of dismantling Canadian production.

“This is the most successful automotive partnership in history,” Mr. Carney said, referring to the deeply integrated Canada-U.S. industry.

Meanwhile, Ontario Premier Doug Ford unleashed his own tirade. In an interview with The Associated Press, he said Mr. Trump had underestimated Canadians' willingness to endure economic pain rather than give in to U.S. pressure.

“We're all in,” Mr. Ford said. “Up here, we're at a fever pitch; everyone's in for an economic war. They know they're going to have to sacrifice.” Mr. Trump responded in a social media post by attacking Mr. Ford personally, calling him “the less charismatic, intelligent, and overall unimpressive brother of the late, great, Rob Ford,” and once again referring to Canada's Prime Minister as “Governor Carney.”

Mr. Ford dismissed the insults: “If you think an insult from him hurts me? Well, bring it on, buddy, I'm ready.” Mr. Ford is a Progressive Conservative whose party differs from that of Mr. Carney, a Liberal, but the two underscore broad political unity in Canada over the trade fight with Mr. Trump.

Ford threatens critical minerals and electricity

Ford said “everything is on the table” if the dispute worsens, including cutting off electricity and critical minerals from Ontario.

Critical minerals are increasingly important to U.S. national security and manufacturing. The Pentagon has sought more secure supplies of minerals used in military aircraft, missiles, munitions and electronics as Washington tries to reduce reliance on China, which dominates the mining or processing of several strategically important minerals.

Ford said Canada should also consider increasingly severe retaliation if Mr. Trump continues targeting Canadian industries, including oil and potash, while Ontario could raise electricity prices or stop sending power south.

“We power 1.5 million homes and businesses,” Mr. Ford said. “Everything's on the table. I'll do whatever it takes.” Mr. Ford has used electricity as leverage before. During an earlier phase of the dispute, Ontario imposed a 25% surcharge on electricity exported to Michigan, Minnesota and New York.

Mr. Trump responded by threatening to double tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminium before both sides backed away.

Auto industry becomes a central battleground

Mr. Ford accused Mr. Trump of not simply seeking a better trade deal but aiming to hollow out Canadian industries and move production south.

Mr. Ford said Mr. Trump wants to make Canada a vassal state.

“He wants to bleed out every single sector and bring them down to the U.S.,” Mr. Ford said.

The auto sector is especially important to Ontario, the centre of Canada's vehicle manufacturing industry. Plants and suppliers in Ontario are tightly integrated with factories in Michigan and other U.S. states, with parts routinely crossing the border multiple times during production.

Automakers including Ford, General Motors and Stellantis operate major assembly plants in Ontario, and the wider supply chain supports tens of thousands of jobs. Mr. Trump's new threat of a 50% tariff on Canadian vehicles and parts puts that sector directly at the centre of the escalating dispute.

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Monday (August 24, 2026) that “the only reason Canada has auto production in the first place” was because of the 1960s Auto Pact, under which Canada used access to its market to encourage vehicle production north of the border.

Ford says he opposed preliminary deal

Mr. Ford also disclosed that he had opposed the preliminary agreement Mr. Carney was considering before Canada walked away from negotiations, and that he was unwilling to restore American liquor to Ontario store shelves as part of an agreement.

“I wasn't going to put the booze back on the shelves,” Mr. Ford said. “I was ready to go out there and call a press conference … and say I'm not buckling over.”

Mr. Ford said he understood Washington had sought language late in the negotiations that would have restricted Canada's ability to negotiate trade agreements with other countries without U.S. approval. Mr. Carney has called that demand unacceptable and a question of Canadian sovereignty.

Mr. Carney said the dispute also exposed a deeper divide over language and culture, saying protections for French and Canadian culture that Washington views as trade irritants are considered fundamental rights in Canada.

“Who does he think he is?” Mr. Ford said of Mr. Trump. “You gotta be kidding.”

World.title: Youth Morcha storms DM office highlighting critical gaps in schools, questions FIR on activist
World.content:
Activists of Justice Morcha, a forum of youths pushing the issues of employment and education in Uttar Pradesh, on Monday (August 24, 2026) reached the District Magistrate (DM) office in Deoria, demanding improvement of critical gaps in basic school infrastructure

The group reached the administration after a case was filed against one of its members, Rajat Singh, for showing the poor condition of government schools on camera in Deoria.

“Many activists of the Justice Morcha reached the office of DM Deoria. A case was filed against our colleague Rajat for showing the poor condition of government schools on camera. Today, when Rajat and his colleagues reached the District Magistrate’s office regarding this matter, the District Magistrate immediately left the office,” said Abhinav Mishra, who claims to be associated with the forum.

“We are only demanding improvement of critical gaps in basic school infrastructure. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath claims that the picture of government schools has changed. If the picture of schools has really changed, then why are cases being filed to show the ground reality? Is the Kayakalp scheme also running only on paper? If officials are looting public money under the nose of the Chief Minister, then who will take responsibility for it,” he asked.

On August 22, the police in Deoria booked Mr. Singh, a member of the group, on charges of entering a primary school in Gauribazar’s Damar Bishwa village without authorisation and spreading misinformation. The police registered the First Information Report (FIR) on a written petition submitted by Gauribazar’s block education officer, Vinay Sheel Mishra.

The FIR was registered under sections 329(4): house trans pass and 353(2): circulating false statements, rumours, or alarming reports—including via electronic media—with the intent or likelihood of promoting feelings of enmity or hatred, of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

The Congress reacted sharply to the police action, calling it a nefarious attempt to silence youth voices. “Under the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government, over one lakh schools have been closed; only in Uttar Pradesh, roughly 25,000 schools are shut. Pupils hailing from marginalised social groups like the Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and Scheduled Castes (SCs) are being forced out of the education system,” said Ajay Kumar ‘Lallu’, a senior U.P. Congress leader.

“Youths are raising voices against this injustice. Filing an FIR is a nefarious attempt to silence voices. The fact is, in the name of infrastructure development, organised loot is ongoing in the State. The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and the BJP want to deprive poor people from the ambit of education,” he added.

World.title: Around 40 dead in gang attack near Haiti’s capital
World.content:
Gang members attacked displaced people huddling inside a church near Haiti’s capital, killing around 40, some of them execution-style, the mayor told AFP on Monday (August 24, 2026).

“We have counted around 40 bodies. Searches are continuing. Some people are still missing,” after the attack Sunday night (August 23, 2026) in the town of Kenscoff in the hills above the capital, its mayor Massillon Jean said.

He described “a night of terror” in a town plagued for months by gang violence.

Mr. Jean said that among other places the assailants targeted a site housing people who had already fled violence.

“The bandits raided a displaced persons camp located in a church. They executed several people. There are fatalities and dozens of wounded. Some people were abducted by the criminals,” Mr. Jean said.

In a statement issued after the attack, the office of Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aime expressed “deep compassion” for the bereaved families and all the victims.

The government also announced that reinforcements would be sent to restore security in the area.

Kenscoff, a mountainous municipality southeast of the Haitian capital, has for several months been the scene of clashes and incursions by armed groups seeking to expand their control.

Haiti, the poorest country in the Americas, has for years suffered from chronic political instability, natural disasters, corruption and violence from powerful gangs that carry out rampant killings, rapes, looting and kidnappings. The gangs control much of the capital city.

Nearly 1.5 million Haitians are currently displaced in a country of about 11 million, and more than five million are facing severe food insecurity, according to UN figures.

The crisis worsened in early 2024, when gangs launched a wave of violence that forced the unelected Prime Minister to resign.

Haiti has not held any kind of election since 2016. Its last president, Jovenel Moise, was assassinated in July 2021 and not replaced.

A general election is scheduled for December of this year.

World.title: CDF Munir vows continued efforts to stabilise region in meeting with Iran’s Ghalibaf
World.content:
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir met Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf in Tehran on Monday during his visit to the Iranian capital, according to Iranian state broadcaster Press TV.

The CDF and interior minister reached Tehran earlier today, Iranian media reported, after Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) described the visit “as part of Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and stability”.

According to the Iranian broadcaster, Ghalibaf reaffirmed Tehran’s commitment to upholding the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, while criticising the United States for failing to honour its commitments. He said this approach had “hindered regional stability and further eroded trust in Washington”.

Field Marshal Munir said Pakistan would continue its efforts to help restore stability in the region, Press TV reported.

Later, Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, expressed his distrust of Washington during a meeting with Field Marshal Munir, according to the Fars news agency.

“America must change its behaviour and take practical actions regarding the implementation of the conditions of the agreement,” Rezaei was quoted as saying by Fars.

Iranian news agency ISNA has also published photographs of a meeting between Field Marshal Munir and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.

Earlier today, CDF Munir and Naqvi met with Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni in Tehran, state media in Pakistan reported.

Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said that the visit undertaken by CDF Munir and Naqvi was taking place as bilateral ties between Islamabad and Tehran “reach one of their strongest stages”, state broadcaster IRIB reported.

Baqaei added that the Pakistani delegation’s visit was unrelated to the visit of Oman’s foreign minister, who is expected to arrive today. He noted that “both visits will address regional security issues”.

ISPR said CDF Munir will “focus on promoting efforts towards peaceful, lasting and comprehensive resolution of the conflict in the Middle East” during the visit.

Baqaei on Sunday said CDF Munir was expected to travel to Tehran to continue efforts to bring peace and security to the region.

He said CDF Munir would lead an official delegation and the “visit aims to strengthen bilateral cooperation between Iran and Pakistan and to continue Pakis­tan’s good offices in support of peace and security in the region”.

During the visit, CDF Munir would meet and hold talks with senior officials Iran, Baqaei added.

The United States and Israel triggered the Middle East war with a massive wave of strikes against Iran on February 28, triggering Iranian retaliation across the region.

An April 8 ceasefire ended nearly 40 days of intense bombardment, but control over the Strait of Hormuz soon emerged as a key flashpoint in the conflict.

Iran has controlled the vital energy conduit since the war began. Reopening the strait, vital for global oil and gas supplies, has become a US priority, but Tehran insists the waterway will remain closed until Washington lifts its naval blockade on Iranian ports, removes oil sanctions and unfreezes Iranian assets abroad.

Pakistan has played a key role in efforts to halt war between Iran and the United States, brokering a memorandum of understanding (MoU) in June, but peace negotiations currently appear stalled.

Last week, US President Donald Trump announced that Washington would ramp up economic pressure on Iran “on an unprecedented scale”.

Washington has urged other governments, including Beijing, to join efforts to further isolate Iran’s economy.

The US is expected to announce details related to the planned sanctions on Mondau, which ​US officials have ​said would be “ the ⁠toughest sanctions in history ” on Iran.

Additional input from AFP

World.title: Govt increases petrol price by Rs0.39, high-speed diesel by Rs2.40
World.content:
The government on Monday raised the price of petrol by Rs0.39 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.40 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs341.98 per litre while HSD will cost Rs370.69 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on August 25.

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Joint opposition announces strategy against economic crisis, political repression
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The joint opposition held its first parliamentary meeting at Parliament House on Monday and announced a collective strategy to address violence, the economic crisis and political repression.

The meeting was attended by opposition party leaders, including Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas Jafri, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and others.

Speaking at a press conference after the meeting, the JUI-F chief said opposition parties had agreed to play a joint role in parliament and stressed that collective strategies and actions would be pursued through mutual consultation.

He said it was not the time to divide the provinces, warning that such a move would only increase mistrust among the federating units.

“We completely agree that this is absolutely not the time to divide the provinces; neither is the environment conducive to it nor is there any prior preparation.”

“Dividing the provinces will increase unrest,” he said, claiming that the 18th Amendment had become a “thorn in the throat” of the establishment.

He said all opposition parties agreed that Pakistan, at the state level, could not afford the prevailing situation. “People are also on the streets in Kashmir,” he said, alleging that violence was being used instead of addressing public grievances.

Fazl also called for the release of prisoners and the creation of a positive political environment.

He described the day as a “blessed day” and said lawmakers sitting on the opposition benches had decided to act as a joint opposition.

“We are together today in view of the law and order situation in the country,” he said. “On one side, our land is red with blood, while on the other, our rulers are walking on red carpets during foreign tours.”

He said the deteriorating law and order situation was also severely affecting the national economy. Referring to Pakistan’s rivalry with India, he said the two countries often talked about war and competition, while India had now become the world’s fourth-largest economy. He also questioned Pakistan’s standing in international judicial rankings.

Addressing the press conference, Achakzai said the opposition’s unity was a positive development, adding that opposition members had reached an agreement despite the “suffocating atmosphere” in parliament.

“It is a day of happiness and facilitation,” he said, expressing hope that the alliance would play an important role in restoring Pakistan’s lost glory.

“Today, there is unrest and bloodshed across the country, with more than 100 people losing their lives every day, yet no one seems to be paying any attention.

“The Constitution clearly lays down the procedure for creating provinces. In contrast, creating provinces through an executive order, in the same way that districts are created, would amount to an attack on the foundations of Pakistan.

“We warn those forces that if you do so, you will not be able to stop the people of Pakistan, and everyone will take to the streets. Pakistan can no longer afford to tolerate such circumstances,” he asserted.

“The poor are crying out for food, people are worried about employment, children are being deprived of basic necessities, and the education system is being ruined,” he said.

Meanwhile, Abbas said the opposition’s unity during the month marking the birth of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was a good sign.

“We are cultivating enmities instead of friendships,” he alleged, adding that the lives of citizens were not secure.

He also alleged that the sanctity of the home and the privacy of families were being violated and said that the honour and dignity of citizens were not protected.

Referring to the condition of incarcerated PTI leader Dr Yasmin Rashid, he said her situation was known to everyone. He also claimed that the Supreme Court had ordered the transfer of PTI founder Imran Khan to Shifa International Hospital, but alleged that the law and judicial decisions were being ignored.

Barrister Gohar said leaders of opposition parties had met and agreed to remain united.

“All opposition parties will adopt a common position in parliament,” he said, adding that they would speak with one voice on law and order, inflation and Pakistan’s relations with other countries.

He said the PTI had assured the JUI-F that it would give it full support.

On the question of provincial restructuring, he said no constitutional amendment concerning the provinces could be made overnight, stressing the need for consultation and consensus.

World.title: PTI says ‘Form 47’ govt lacks mandate to reshape country's governance structure
World.content:
PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said on Monday that the incumbent “Form 47” government had no mandate to reshape the country’s governance structure, adding that the party would welcome anyone willing to ally with it “in principle” on the issue.

Speaking on Geo News programme ‘Capital Talk’, Raja said the recent discussions with Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam chief Fazlur Rehman at the latter’s residence were based “on principle”.

“We all agreed that whatever has happened to this country over the past four years was against everyone’s wishes and expectations. In terms of the rule of law and the Constitution, the country has fallen into a deep ditch,” the PTI secretary general said.

“At this point, if someone feels that we are not where we were expected to be four years ago, whatever the reason, we need to consider the current situation objectively. Anyone can join us in principle,” he added.

Raja cautioned against altering the country’s federal system, describing discussions about an overhaul of the country’s entire structure as “hazardous”.

“The Form 47 assembly has no mandate to revamp the country’s system or governance structures,” he reiterated.

The senior PTI leader said any party that agreed with the PTI “in principle” on these issues could ally with it.

“Any political party that wants to strengthen the system, liberate the judiciary and reject rule by force in Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Balochistan or elsewhere can join us,” he said.

“It does not matter what our past was. We are very clear about our principles and our goal. We will welcome anyone who can go with us to some extent. A party can also end its journey with us. We are not depending on anyone,” he added.

Regarding the PTI’s call for a long march on Sept 27, Raja said the party would not stop any political party from joining it and would welcome those that did.

“Decisions will be taken at party forums — the core and political committees. If a party expresses its willingness to join the march, we will assess its goals and purpose,” he said.

Last week, the JUI-F chief also held a meeting with National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas and other opposition leaders, announcing the formation of a “united opposition”.

During the meeting, the leaders agreed to continue “further consultations among opposition parties” and formulate a joint course of action.

Meanwhile, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, who is an ally of the government, also met with the opposition leaders and agreed to maintain contact and cooperate on legislative matters in the parliament.

World.title: Family, legal team of Imaan and Hadi voice concerns over medical facilities at Adiala jail
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The families and legal team of incarcerated lawyers and human rights activists Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chatta have voiced concerns over the medical facilities available at Adiala jail.

On January 24, rights lawyers Imaan and Hadi were sentenced by an Islamabad sessions court to a total of 17 years in jail on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca).

Following their convictions, which were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts , the couple challenged their convictions before the Islamabad High Court (IHC) on February 7.

In a statement issued on Monday, the family and legal team said they were satisfied with the weekly meetings with the couple at the jail. However, they said Imaan had been experiencing health issues for the past three weeks, raising concerns about the medical facilities available at the jail.

“Imaan had initially complained of heavy bleeding from her gums, but there was no dentist available to examine her at the jail. We arranged for medicine to be sent to her after consulting our dentist, but not all of it reached her,” the statement alleged.

The following week, Imaan also suffered from stomach problems, and medical attention remained inadequate, it added.

“Worse, a medicine, Zedron, meant primarily for cancer patients and which specifically states that it should not be given to women of childbearing age, was administered to her to stop her nausea and vomiting,” the statement claimed.

For the past week, the family and legal team said Imaan had been suffering from a serious chest infection.

“They conducted a blood test which showed a high white blood cell count, indicating an infection. She needs to undergo a chest X-ray, but the jail authorities have still not arranged one to determine the cause of the infection and rule out serious diseases such as tuberculosis,” they said.

They maintained that their concern was compounded by the alarming fact that inmates in the women’s section of Adiala jail who had been diagnosed with infectious diseases were not isolated but housed alongside other inmates, as well as children.

“The women’s medical facilities and the availability of doctors leave a lot to be desired,” they stated.

“This is a health crisis in the jail, and the well-being of prisoners is the responsibility of the state, which must not take it lightly,” the statement said.

They reiterated that all these health issues could be avoided if their applications for suspension of sentence were heard in a timely manner.

They urged the jail authorities and the government to arrange Imaan’s chest X-ray as soon as possible and provide adequate medical facilities, including dental care, to all women prisoners.

They emphasised that detainees with infectious diseases should be isolated or quarantined with dignity to protect other detainees; that specialist doctors and access to relevant medication should be provided to all detainees; and that the government should not oppose the applications for suspension of sentence filed by Imaan and Hadi, which are scheduled to be heard by the IHC on Sept 8, 2026.

World.title: Protest at Islamabad varsity turns ugly after clash between uniformed individual, students
World.content:
A security official is in custody and facing disciplinary action under military law following reports of a scuffle at Islamabad’s Sarhad University of Science and Information Technology (SUSIT), sources involved in the investigation said late Monday.

The individual allegedly discharged a weapon during a scuffle with protestors at the university’s Chattha Bakhtawar campus, where students had been agitating against the dismissal of a senior official and other varsity-related issues.

A video shared widely on social media of the incident shows a uniformed individual approaching a group of young men, who are reportedly SUSIT students. He is accompanied by a woman, who is said to be a university official.

The video showed the suspect hitting an individual with a stick and exchanging heated words with gathered protestors, following which a scuffle breaks out. An angry crowd surrounds the officer, and some individuals appear to assault him, following which he draws a pistol and points it at the crowd.

The woman accompanying him appears to try to stop him, but the man then points the weapon into the air and discharges it, at which several police officers approach and encircle him.

In a later video, a senior Islamabad police official can be seen addressing the students. The individual was escorted out of the university by police, the police officer says, assuring that he will be dealt with strictly and swiftly under the army’s disciplinary procedures.

“The Pakistan Army’s foremost priority is to maintain a strict system of discipline and ensure justice. Further action will be taken in light of the findings of the inquiry,” sources privy to the matter said.

No official statement has been issued by the police, security forces or university yet.

World.title: Trump administration moves to impose more than $100,000 fee for H-1B worker visas
World.content:
President Donald Trump’s administration on Monday released a proposed regulation to codify an unprecedented more than $100,000 fee on new H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers, that Trump first imposed last year but has been blocked by the courts.

The fee first imposed by Trump in a temporary proclamation last year vastly raises the cost of the visas that are heavily relied on in the tech, education and research sectors.

A federal judge in June ruled that the fee was illegal and blocked the Trump administration from collecting it. A Boston-based appeals court is reviewing that decision while a different court considers whether a judge in Washington, DC, properly rejected a challenge to the fee by a major business group.

Trump’s 2025 proclamation imposing the fee expires in September, one year after it was issued, but directed the US Department of Homeland Security to adopt regulations making it permanent.

The proposed $103,265 fee by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), posted online in the Federal Register on Monday to be formally published on Tuesday, kicks off a 30-day public comment period.

The rule could be finalised by the end of the year.

The H-1B program allows US employers to hire foreign workers with training in specialty fields and offers 65,000 visas annually, with another 20,000 for workers with advanced degrees, approved for three to six years.

The order Trump issued last year sharply increased the cost of obtaining some H-1B visas, which had typically come with about $2,000 to $5,000 in fees, depending on various factors.

Debate over visa program

Trump, a Republican, and other critics of the H-1B program say it is abused by many companies who replace American workers with cheaper foreign labour. But business groups and many individual companies have said the visa program is needed to address a lack of qualified American workers for some jobs and to allow US businesses to recruit top talent.
